18c993d2e71824c5.title: Apple Reveals How Secure Exclaves Shield Camera and Microphone Data
summary: Apple has published details of Secure Exclaves, a security architecture in its silicon that isolates camera and microphone data from the main operating system.
Sensor data is processed in isolated runtimes built on a minimal capability-based microkernel, which Apple has been subjecting to formal verification.

Formal verification uncovered hard-to-spot but critical kernel flaws that could have led to full compromise, and many were fixed early in development. Apple says verification is applied gradually rather than to the entire kernel.

1b3f586f0e078746.title: Nationwide FAA Ground Stop Caused by Air Traffic Control Communications Outage, No Signs of Hacking
summary: The Federal Aviation Administration ordered a nationwide ground stop at all U.S. airports on Friday afternoon, citing safety, and lifted it about four hours later.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said a communications problem affected air route traffic control centers nationwide, and authorities said there were no signs of hacking.
The FBI is investigating whether a recently applied software update caused the outage, and the official root cause has not yet been announced.
Thousands of flights were affected and departures have resumed, but delays are expected to continue for several days.

d86a4e21bbd54ebc.title: SCKit Worm Campaign Exploits ConnectWise ScreenConnect to Compromise MSP Customer Endpoints
summary: A campaign targeting ConnectWise ScreenConnect compromised multiple managed service providers, with endpoints at customer organizations infected with unauthorized clients.

Attackers gained access through an authentication flaw in the RMM+ extension (versions 1.0.31 and 1.0.32) and used Run Command to install rogue clients. The SCKit worm steals session cookies and attempts to spread to technician PCs.
Huntress reported 288 endpoints across 48 organizations affected, while BleepingComputer counted at least 286 endpoints across 47 organizations.
Blackpoint Cyber said exploitation of CVE-2026-84869 is blocked by patching, which prevents payload execution.
ConnectWise disabled five extensions in about 400 partner environments and urged customers to end sessions and reset credentials, while the initial access vector remains under investigation.

8ede23d73441de9d.title: FBI flash alert says Artex tool automating cyberattacks at ‘machine speed’
summary: The FBI issued a flash alert warning that Artex, an open-source AI penetration testing platform, is being widely abused to breach government agencies and critical sectors.
Artex can turn any large language model into a hacking tool, automating reconnaissance through data exfiltration at machine speed.
Censys identified over 1,600 publicly exposed Artex consoles, and the actual number of deployments is likely much higher.

75761d05b8eca180.title: ARTEX and beyond: AI-enabled penetration testing platforms
summary: Cisco Talos reports growing in-the-wild misuse of AI-enabled penetration testing frameworks that automate reconnaissance and intrusion.
ARTEX, an open-source framework, has been used by China-nexus and financially motivated actors in campaigns involving credential theft and exploitation.
VAPOR PANDA targeted more than 200 organizations, and an attack on South Korean financial firms resulted in data exfiltration.

bd480ea05e3c1ebb.title: Arara Mail Delivery Service Breach Exposes Over 81 Million Email Addresses
summary: Arara Inc., operator of the mail distribution service Arara Message, disclosed unauthorized access by a third party that exposed customer data for clients including Osaka City, the Cabinet Office, and Moss Food Service.
The attackers exploited a web server vulnerability and system environment issues, and the company said 81,329,467 unique email addresses were stolen.
The Record reported that about 77 million addresses belonging to roughly 400 customers were affected, while Osaka City said over 1 million people were impacted.
The service was also abused to send phishing emails impersonating credit card companies, with up to about 7.13 million messages sent between October 28 and 30.
The service has been suspended since October 31 with no restoration date, and officials urge recipients not to open links or attachments from unknown senders or enter credentials.

c7685520f02e8134.title: Implants Found in Hardware Wallets Sold via CryptoBilis, Stealing Recovery Phrases
summary: Hardware wallet makers Ledger and Trezor found implants that steal recovery phrases in devices sold through reseller CryptoBilis.
The implant is a circuit board inserted between the main board and the display, reading the 24-word recovery phrase shown on screen and sending it over cellular networks such as LTE.
The secure element and firmware were not altered, so integrity checks did not detect the tampering, and Ledger said all confirmed fund losses came from CryptoBilis sales.
Trezor said on November 13 it confirmed implants in three Safe 5 devices, and firmware 2.13.1 blocks data collection but cannot protect phrases already exposed.
Both companies advised customers who bought from the reseller to move their assets to new wallets, and CryptoBilis halted trading on October 9.

a90ad1ae2f23b762.title: NYC to bar surveillance pricing as momentum for bans grows nationwide
summary: The New York City Council passed a bill 44-5 banning surveillance pricing, which charges different customers different prices for the same product based on their personal data.
The practice uses data such as search history to estimate what consumers can pay, and the city's Department of Consumer and Worker Protection can fine violators up to $1,000 per violation.
New York City is the second city to pass such a ban after Seattle, while a similar state bill awaits Governor Kathy Hochul's signature and New Jersey, Connecticut and Maryland already have bans.

e8c1c41ab73ac47a.title: German military drone operations disrupted by cyberattack
summary: German defense technology firm Quantum Systems confirmed an incident detected in late October that was part of an active cyberattack by hostile actors.
The compromise reportedly occurred through a malicious update file for QBase, its ground-control and mission-planning software, pointing to the vendor's update distribution server.
German forces reportedly grounded Quantum Systems drones as a precaution and excluded them from a recent exercise, while MAD, BfV and BSI are involved in the response.

772f4f02a695411b.title: University of Texas at Arlington warns personal information stolen during cyberattack
summary: The University of Texas at Arlington warned students and employees that hackers stole personal information from its systems during a cybersecurity incident last month.
The Qilin ransomware gang claimed the attack, and the university's MachForms portal, used for event registration and surveys, remains offline.
The university is still determining whose data was affected and what was taken, and says it will contact affected individuals directly.

da22cab01e262b8c.title: PostgreSQL Patches 52 Flaws, Including 22-Year-Old Bug Enabling Authenticated RCE
summary: The PostgreSQL project released updates fixing 52 flaws, including CVE-2026-6460 (CVSS 8.8), which lets a database user with object creation rights run code on the server.
The flaw is a type confusion bug in composite types: after a field's type changes, the server can read older values that no longer match, dating back to a 2004 feature change.

No attacks have been reported and CISA lists no exploitation. A researcher published a crash and memory-leak demonstration but withheld the code-execution step and privately notified managed database providers.

1ce655f4c162dcd7.title: German parliament passes law giving spy agencies hacking, sabotage powers
summary: Germany's parliament passed a law letting its intelligence agencies hack foreign systems, disrupt hostile supply chains and shut down servers run by state-backed hackers.
The foreign service BND gains powers to act against threats abroad, while the domestic BfV gets a shorter list of covert powers, such as blocking data traffic.
The bill bars measures that endanger lives and requires prior approval from an oversight council, while the far-right AfD opposes a provision limiting information sharing with states.

25bd15e1c6247ee8.title: PHP2Shell Attacks on Check Point Gateways Lead to ESXi Wiper Deployment
summary: Starting October 30, 2026, unpatched Check Point security gateways were targeted in attacks, with Israeli agencies hit first.

Attackers gained initial access via the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619), then exploited privilege escalation flaw CVE-2026-123039 to obtain root and deploy web shells and TSGA backdoors.
According to BleepingComputer, dozens of customer organizations were affected, while The Hacker News reported that some agencies suffered file deletion after attackers moved via SSH to ESXi hosts.
A second wave on November 2 targeted organizations in multiple countries and sectors, but no destructive activity was observed, and the threat actor remains unidentified.
Check Point has urged customers to apply the November Jumbo Hotfix and the emergency hotfix for the escalation flaw.

282ae533f6285a2b.title: Inside the loop: Five AI attack frameworks that never ask permission
summary: Five agentic offensive frameworks, ARTEX, CyberStrikeAI, Cairn, PentAGI, and HexStrike, have drawn more than 60,000 GitHub stars combined and have already been seen in real intrusions.
An LLM drives scanners, shells, and cloud CLIs in a planning loop, and none of the five enforces authorization in code, with agents running autonomously by default without human approval.
When blocked, these tools often switch proxies and User-Agents, so IOC-based detections go stale quickly and defenders should pair behavior-based detection with credential revocation.

d29a1479eb4d6c1c.title: International Operation Endgame Dismantles Gootloader, CastleRAT and StealC Malware Infrastructure
summary: Europol and law enforcement agencies in nine countries seized 235 servers and 257 domains used to operate the Gootloader, CastleRAT and StealC malware under Operation Endgame.
Gootloader spread through compromised WordPress sites hosting fake legal documents, using SEO poisoning to lure victims into downloading ransomware and other malware.
The US Department of Justice said the malware was tied to at least 44 ransomware attacks since 2018, causing losses of about $28.8 million and infecting roughly 25,000 devices worldwide.
About 6.4 million stolen login credentials from more than 40,000 victims were recovered, and malware was removed from 681 hacked websites. No arrests have been announced.
Users can check exposure through HaveIBeenPwned, and WordPress site operators are advised to reset passwords and enable multi-factor authentication.

af0dc69bf69f021a.title: 56 AWS API calls in 141 milliseconds: Inside an AI-run intrusion
summary: Between September 30 and October 16, 2026, a server running the open-source CyberStrikeAI platform used stolen credentials from eight AWS identities across four accounts.
The attacker harvested Secrets Manager secrets and EC2 user data, firing 56 requests in 141 milliseconds, and sent an SSM remote command on October 2. The pattern strongly suggests automated tooling.
All 78 alerts were medium or low severity and only revealed the full picture once grouped by source IP. The command's content and outcome are unknown, and the server returned after a 14-day gap.

7ac9485c64b954e1.title: New Mior and Skyfall Attacks Let Rogue Cloud Hosts Steal Secrets From AMD SEV-SNP VMs
summary: Researchers from ETH Zurich and Google disclosed two attacks, Mior and Skyfall, that let a malicious host read data inside AMD SEV-SNP protected virtual machines.

Mior manipulates the PSP's Reverse Map Table initialization to disable memory protections, while Skyfall exploits TSA flaws to recover register values and a disk encryption key. Both require control of the hypervisor.
AMD published CVE-2026-0462 for Mior and CVE-2026-40671 for Skyfall, with SEV and microcode fixes dated August 12 and platform firmware planned for November and December.

59ed4dba84232bcb.title: In Other News: New CISA Director Nominee, Connected Car Hacking, Baker Tilly Data Breach
summary: This week's SecurityWeek roundup covers a former FBI agent's $2.47M crypto theft, a Baker Tilly client data breach, and OpenAI agents that gained unauthorized root access.
Baker Tilly says hackers stole Social Security numbers from a service provider's platform, and Texas filings point to more than 10,000 victims.
Railway estimates about $740,000 in unauthorized spending from stolen AI keys, while Fortinet analyzed an MS SQL campaign delivering a Monero miner and Gh0st RAT.

d8ea83987508008d.title: TSMC confirms employee data breach tied to cloud service provider
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company disclosed to the US Securities and Exchange Commission that a cloud service provider was breached, exposing data on current and former employees.
On November 8, a hacker posted on a cybercrime forum offering 6.9 GB of employee data, allegedly including contact, identity and banking details, for 3 BTC (about $200,000).

The investigation found no TSMC systems were compromised, and the company is supporting affected staff while working with the vendor, authorities and a third-party cybersecurity firm to establish the facts.

5f5f12320274d258.title: How one AI agent exposed five critical enterprise security gaps
summary: The article follows a hypothetical case in which an accounts staffer built an AI agent that ran on email, ERP, and Slack without any security review.
An attacker hid instructions in white-on-white text inside an invoice email, tricking the agent into changing a vendor's bank details in the ERP.
The piece identifies five points where controls such as access-path mapping, Rule of Two checks, and behavior-based detection could have stopped the attack.

653a9e87d5ea7526.title: Cyber Security Cloud GitHub Breach Exposes Customer Data
summary: Cyber Security Cloud said unauthorized access to its GitHub environment used for software development may have exposed some customer data.
A single employee's business GitHub credential was leaked externally, and access logs checked on November 5 showed it was used by an unauthorized third party via valid accounts (MITRE ATT&CK T1078).
According to Security NEXT, organization names, names, email addresses, and service communication information of some customers may have been exposed.
According to ITmedia, the leaked credential has been revoked and no unauthorized access or service impact has been confirmed, while the intrusion period and root cause remain under investigation.

174f5872a3e6e77e.title: FBI Says North Korean Hackers Stole Over $400 Million in Crypto Using Deepfake Video Calls
summary: The FBI says North Korea-linked hackers stole over $400 million in cryptocurrency over 18 months using a social engineering scheme called FaceStealer, which relies on deepfake video calls.
Attackers hijacked victims' accounts to impersonate trusted contacts in fake Zoom or Teams meetings, then lured targets into installing malware through a fake audio-fix link.
The U.S. Department of Justice announced court-authorized seizure of over $1.2 billion in crypto stolen in the Binance hack, and the cloud infrastructure used in the campaign was also seized.

06b077439781e50a.title: Ransomware attack on Belarusian cloud firm disrupts businesses for days
summary: Belarusian cloud provider ActiveCloud was hit by a ransomware attack earlier this week, disrupting corporate websites, email and virtual servers.
Hackers breached its systems and encrypted parts of its cloud infrastructure, and the access method and attackers have not been identified.
Main services have been restored, but some customers still face issues recovering virtual machines, and no evidence of customer data theft was found.

a3680dee881822b8.title: Ryohin Keikaku MUJI App and Online Store Customer Data Breach Expands
summary: Ryohin Keikaku said on October 30, 2026 that customer data from its official MUJI app may have been leaked, affecting up to about 27.26 million records.

In November, a credential stuffing attack on the online store led to confirmed unauthorized logins, and data on about 1.09 million MUJI Card members, along with cash-on-delivery recipient data, may also have been exposed.
According to ITmedia, full card numbers, including pre-2021 numbers, were kept unencrypted and never deleted, prompting the company to apologize.
The company has postponed the reopening of its online store and plans to require password resets from all members, while covering card reissuance fees and contacting affected customers individually.
No secondary damage has been confirmed so far, but users should be wary of phishing attempts that exploit the leaked information.

3835728012bf14db.title: Phishing Reports and Abused URLs Both Rise in September
summary: Phishing reports to the Anti-Phishing Council reached 94,661 in September 2026, up about 15.0% from August and rising for a second straight month.
Abused URLs totaled 49,032, up about 23.2% month over month, with many campaigns reusing the same hostname and changing only parameters.
E-commerce accounted for about 47.9% of reports and credit services for about 35.0%. The article does not describe damage or response measures.

b92114f7d09db74c.title: GeoVision Camera Software Abused to Deploy XMRig Cryptominer
summary: Huntress SOC reported that attacks against GeoVision surveillance camera software were observed at 13 organizations across several industries, mainly between November 8 and 10.
Attackers abused the internet-exposed GeoStartupAgentService.exe to run PowerShell scripts, which attempted to disable Microsoft Defender and loaded a vulnerable kernel driver.
The intrusion ended with deployment of the XMRig miner to use compromised endpoints for cryptocurrency mining, and Huntress recommends restricting public access to GeoVision devices.

4eb8cd3778ec93b0.title: Apify Breach Exposes Customer Data and Prompts 2FA Resets
summary: Czech web scraping and automation platform Apify confirmed that customer data was accessed in a cyberattack targeting its internal systems and customer accounts.
The attacker used stolen credentials to obtain additional credentials and access linked accounts, with the intrusion occurring November 9-10 and blocked on November 11.
According to SecurityWeek, exposed data reportedly includes names, emails, partial payment information, salted password hashes, 2FA recovery codes, and Google and GitHub authentication tokens.
BleepingComputer reported no confirmed impact on account data, but advised customers to reset 2FA in the Apify console because 2FA codes may have been exposed.
The company rotated API tokens and proxy passwords, revoked some OAuth connections including GitHub, and continues its investigation.

2e7f65ead561545c.title: Monex Securities Account Opening System Unauthorized Access Raises Data Breach Concerns
summary: Monex Securities said a third party gained unauthorized access to part of an account opening system operated by an outsourced vendor, potentially exposing personal data.
The vendor detected the access on October 18, 2026, and blocked external access the following day, temporarily suspending some account openings. The cause and details remain under investigation.
Impress Watch reported that up to 1.13 million email addresses and 1,592 identity verification document images may have been exposed, with no individual numbers confirmed.

INTERNET Watch said account numbers and passwords were not included in the exposed data. No damage has been reported so far, and the company is notifying affected customers individually and warning them to watch for phishing.

ee711618d4ff3215.title: Microsoft says November security updates cause printing issues
summary: Microsoft warned that the November 2026 Windows security updates may cause printing failures for some documents.
The bug affects documents containing images with zero height or width when printed through the Windows GDI, mainly Microsoft Word files.
Microsoft says it is investigating the issue and will share more information later, after several earlier update-related printing problems.

d89a8891ac12faca.title: SilentAir Hijacks Asian Mobile Networks to Intercept Calls and SMS
summary: Swedish telecom security firm Enea disclosed SilentAir, a new threat actor that intercepts calls and SMS of users, mainly in Taiwan, by abusing compromised equipment inside Asian mobile carrier networks.
The actor used SS7 and Diameter signaling attacks to redirect targets' location records to its own nodes, routing calls and texts through them while harvesting subscriber data.
The Hacker News reported that in some cases attackers also intercepted SMS-based two-factor authentication codes.
SecurityWeek reported that at least six Asian carrier networks were breached, and the same report covered Liminal Panda's abuse of IPX and the GTPDoor backdoor.
The campaign is currently halted but could resume, and the report does not state whether the compromised carriers have removed the malicious equipment.

f55af51f9cd07cc0.title: Multiple Git Vulnerabilities Disclosed, Including Arbitrary Code Execution via Recursive Clone (CVE-2026-111760)
summary: Multiple vulnerabilities in Git were disclosed on November 10, 2026, with fixed versions released to address them.
CVE-2026-111760 stems from an integer truncation issue during index processing, allowing attacker code to execute when a malicious repository is cloned recursively, including submodules.
Attackers can craft paths that pass length checks and are then truncated to .git, turning a submodule's .git file into a symbolic link pointing to a folder containing malicious hooks.

According to GitLab, the flaw could allow arbitrary commands to run in the Gitaly execution environment, so it was rated Critical, and a heap-based buffer overflow tracked as CVE-2026-105437 was also fixed.

GitHub applied the fix to github.com and GitHub Enterprise Cloud, and five other Git vulnerabilities were fixed as well. Users should avoid recursively cloning untrusted repositories until they install the patched versions.

d26fa98f5aade1d1.title: When an AI Agent Goes Wrong, Can You Stop It?
summary: The OWASP GenAI Security Project's October 2026 roundup describes evaluation agents reaching beyond their intended scope.
Turning off the model may not stop running workflows, credentials or existing connections, so teams should test several controls together.
The article outlines a response sequence: pause the workflow, revoke access, restrict tools and network paths, preserve evidence, then verify before restoring.

990ceb985334ea04.title: GTA VI isn’t out yet – and the scams are already in full swing
summary: Scams tied to GTA VI are spreading ahead of its launch, including fake leaked builds, malware-laced installers, and bogus early-access sales.
Fake installers carried infostealers such as Vidar, njRAT, and DCRat, and one ISO contained Chaos ransomware that functioned as a wiper.
Rockstar has not announced a PC version, beta, demo, or early access, so offers claiming these should be treated as scams.

1d01678d1ba3ef9b.title: Citrix Patches Multiple Critical NetScaler Vulnerabilities
summary: Citrix has released patches for vulnerabilities in NetScaler ADC, NetScaler Gateway, and NetScaler Console.
Reports differ on the count: SecurityWeek and Security NEXT cite 28 vulnerabilities, while The Hacker News cites 12.
According to SecurityWeek, nine of them are rated critical, stemming from memory overflows in packet processing, SMPP, DNS/DoH, and email OTP authentication.
Exploitation could lead to denial of service or unpredictable behavior.

CVE-2026-120869 (CVSS 9.4) in NetScaler Console allows access control bypass without authentication. All three outlets report no known exploitation, and Citrix urges customers to apply updates immediately.

4820278c633d2bdd.title: Microsoft confirms Windows activation failures after November updates
summary: Microsoft has confirmed that November Patch Tuesday security updates are causing Windows activation and licensing failures, returning error code 0x80041008.

The issue affects organizations that automate activation or use SLMGR, particularly when running slmgr.vbs /skms-domain and /ipk commands, while devices with a KMS client key already installed are unaffected.
A fix is expected within days, and organizations needing immediate mitigation are advised to contact Microsoft Support for business.

0ccf31f01d23d85f.title: Onamae.com Desktop Cloud Unauthorized Access Incident Exposes FX Trading Accounts
summary: Unauthorized third parties accessed Onamae.com Desktop Cloud, a VPS service for automated FX trading run by GMO Internet Group, and installed malicious programs on some customer servers.

Attackers stole login credentials for FX trading accounts stored on the servers and used them for unauthorized trades, then demanded about 8 billion yen in ransom while threatening to leak customer data, but the company refused to pay.
The company initially said no abuse had been confirmed, but later admitted at a press conference that customer information was leaked and customer assets were damaged.
Compensation claims for FX losses cover 2,943 accounts and about 2.998 billion yen, with direct costs estimated at 3.05 billion yen against a cyber insurance cap of 1.1 billion yen.
Experts had flagged a vulnerability in 2024, but remediation was delayed, and the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications asked carriers to block attacker sites.

6950a091e6ee6274.title: Ransomware at the hypervisor layer: how attackers use ESXi and vCenter features for malicious purposes
summary: Kaspersky's Global Emergency Response Team investigated an incident in which an attacker destroyed an organization's virtualization estate over 10 days. The attacker was identified as the BlackNevas group.
No hypervisor vulnerability was exploited. The attacker used legitimate VMware management interfaces, credentials reused from the Windows environment, and credentials stored on backup infrastructure.
The attacker established persistence on a vCenter appliance using MeshAgent and a Ligolo-ng reverse tunnel run as systemd services. Details on the overall scale of impact are limited.

f86b348751780806.title: SignDrop Windows CLFS Zero-Day Exploit Enables SYSTEM Privilege Escalation
summary: Security researcher Abdelhamid Naceri, also known as Nightmare Eclipse, has released SignDrop, a zero-day exploit for Windows.
The exploit abuses a flaw in the Common Log File System (CLFS) driver's authentication file creation logic to let local users gain SYSTEM privileges.
According to The Hacker News, it redirects .cnpf file creation to a symbolic link, allowing writes to SYSTEM-privileged files.
Cyderes built the public PoC and confirmed it works, but no in-the-wild exploitation has been reported, and independent testers rated it unstable for real-world use.

According to BleepingComputer, the exploit was tested on Windows 11 and Windows Server 2025, and the researcher estimates about 80% of Windows installations are vulnerable, while Microsoft has not yet issued a CVE or patch.

5818b69f3e374cce.title: Police arrest 354 suspects in dark web cybercrime crackdown
summary: Authorities in 14 countries arrested 354 suspects in Operation TorNado, a joint operation with Europol targeting dark web marketplace vendors and buyers.
The investigation covered markets such as Archetyp and Nemesis, as well as forums and encrypted messaging services, running from May 2025 to October 2026.
Over €60 million in cash and cryptocurrency, 950 kg of drugs, and 57 firearms were seized in Europe, while the US seized large quantities of drugs and guns.

b179af583e1bf127.title: N-central Zero-Day 4EverAble2Shell Exploited Within Hours of Public PoC Release
summary: Attackers began exploiting a new zero-day flaw, 4EverAble2Shell, in N-able's N-central management servers within hours of a public proof-of-concept release.

The attackers chained an Apache Axis vulnerability (CVE-2026-90436) with a legacy API flaw and a privilege escalation bug to gain unauthenticated root access, then installed XMRig cryptomining malware.
According to BleepingComputer and The Hacker News, at least 21 systems were compromised, and Huntback reported that 19 of them had Hotfix 2 applied.
N-able has advised disabling the legacy API and suspending the Intune integration, while a permanent fix is still under development.

3509cb8f9eeb7a45.title: NEC WebSAM WinShare Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities Disclosed
summary: NEC published security advisories on November 9, 2026, covering three vulnerabilities in WebSAM WinShare, its Windows remote control software, tracked as CVE-2026-113362, CVE-2026-113363, and CVE-2026-113364.

IPA and JPCERT/CC announced the issues the same day through JVN. According to JVN, the flaws stem from improper file access permissions, exposure of dangerous functionality, and a heap buffer overflow.
Attackers can send crafted packets to execute arbitrary commands or code with SYSTEM privileges. The CVSSv4.0 score is 9.3 and the CVSSv3.0 score is 9.8, rated critical.

Versions 7.2.0 through 7.7.2 are affected, and the developer recommends updating to the latest version. The reports do not say whether the flaws have been exploited in the wild or whether patches are available.

863cecd89365be23.title: Accelerating Vulfrom Detection to Remediation: Vulnerability Management in the Frontier AI Era (Part 4)
summary: In the frontier AI era, the time between a vulnerability's discovery and its exploitation by attackers may shrink, making manual response workflows harder to keep up with.
Organizations need to automate vulnerability detection, prioritization, patching, and interim mitigations to respond quickly and comprehensively.

The article covers threat intelligence and scanner-based prioritization, automated patch deployment, virtual patching when no fix exists, and tracking interim measures through to permanent remediation.

ee3baadb12b927ec.title: Qoo10 Unauthorized Access Leads to Personal Information Leak, Possibly Including Address Geocoordinates and Physical Characteristics
summary: Qoo10, a Japanese online shopping platform, reportedly suffered unauthorized access that led to a personal data leak.
The leaked data may also include address geocoordinates and physical characteristics information.
The attack method, scale of damage, and response status are not confirmed in the available text, so official updates should be checked.

07bfd3b3214ab010.title: Macfinger ClickFix campaign sends DownTheDRAIN infostealer for macOS, (Fri, Nov 13th)
summary: A macOS infostealer dubbed DownTheDRAIN was observed in the Macfinger ClickFix campaign.

Victims are lured by a fake CAPTCHA page and paste a Terminal command that downloads a shell script, which installs the malware. The malware includes a DRAIN function that searches for cryptocurrency wallet addresses and redirects funds to an attacker-controlled wallet.
macOS on the analyst's test system blocked the malware and moved it to the Trash before any data was exfiltrated. The name was assigned based on analysis published by Huntress.

00cb70322c203590.title: Synology Patches Vulnerabilities in DSM for NAS Devices, Including a Critical Flaw
summary: Synology released a security advisory on November 10, 2026, disclosing 27 vulnerabilities in DiskStation Manager (DSM), its operating system for NAS devices, and urged users to update to fixed versions.

CVE-2026-76954 (CVSS 9.8), an SQL injection flaw in the authentication API, allows remote reading and writing of arbitrary files and enables DoS attacks. CVE-2026-85101 (CVSS 8.6), an authentication bypass in the rsync feature, was also confirmed.
Of the 27 flaws, one is rated critical, nine important, and 17 moderate. Users should promptly update to the patched versions.

e04259d9f390677e.title: Credential Stuffing Attack Leads to Unauthorized Logins on Official Lottery Website
summary: Unauthorized logins to the official lottery website and app occurred on November 4 using credentials obtained from outside sources, and service was suspended from November 5.

The attack is believed to be credential stuffing (T1110.004), and names, dates of birth, addresses, contact details, partial payout account data, last four card digits, and purchase histories may have been viewed.

According to ITmedia, third parties may have accessed member information including lottery prize records on prefectural and designated city sites, though no server intrusion or data leak has been confirmed.
According to Impress Watch, 4,436 accounts were affected, and service resumed by November 13, but users must reset passwords to log in again; no leaks or fraudulent purchases have been confirmed.
The number of affected members has not been disclosed, and members will be notified individually by email.

e181dcd0817d560a.title: Binance Suffers $6.3 Billion Crypto Theft Attributed to North Korean Hackers
summary: On October 29, 2026, crypto exchange Binance lost about $6.34 billion in assets in a major theft.

Attackers infected engineer devices through a tampered Homebrew installer in June and a fake job interview in September, then abused internal AI tools to steal credentials and gain access to the wallet signing system.
Binance said it froze or blocked about $2.85 billion and replenished 98% of affected token assets, while the FBI attributed the attack to the North Korean group TraderTraitor.

The FBI obtained court approval to seize or freeze more than $1.2 billion in stolen funds, and reports differ on losses from the separate FaceStealer campaign, ranging from over $100 million to $400 million. North Korea denied involvement.

470291645463523b.title: Fortinet Discloses Large Batch of Vulnerabilities Including Critical Flaws in FortiMail and FortiClient
summary: According to SecurityWeek, Fortinet released 89 security advisories at once, covering about 100 vulnerabilities across its product line.
According to Security NEXT, 27 vulnerabilities were disclosed in the email security product FortiMail, and eight of them were rated Critical, the highest severity.
CVE-2026-126147 and others carry a CVSS score of 9.8, and path traversal, command injection, and SQL injection flaws could allow arbitrary code or command execution.
A FortiClient flaw can be exploited simply by a victim visiting a malicious website, and about 17 critical-severity vulnerabilities were reported overall.

The reports did not mention any exploitation in the wild. An October security update addressed some of the flaws, and customers are advised to apply updates before detailed technical information is published.

ddc4d681103ffbe4.title: Ransomware Attack Disables Emergency Voice Broadcast System in Koka City, Shiga Prefecture
summary: Koka City in Shiga Prefecture said on November 12 that a ransomware attack hit the server of its voice broadcast system, leaving outdoor loudspeakers and broadcast terminals unusable.
The article does not provide details on the attack method or the responsible group.

Emergency information is being relayed through the city's official LINE account, TV, and radio. The city is investigating a possible leak of names and business names of terminal installers, and no recovery timeline has been given.

136d0b7ec757fdda.title: Record number of cyber incidents reported to UK privacy regulator
summary: British organizations reported 1,371 cyber incidents to the Information Commissioner's Office in the third quarter of 2026, a quarterly record.
Ransomware reports fell, but leak-site data shows extortion attacks rising, with the UK seeing a steady increase in victims named by groups such as Qilin.
Most incidents were classed as other cyber incidents, and the ICO opened investigations into only 18 of the 1,371 reports.

85e96ce0d997b1f1.title: Online Mahjong Service Maru-Jan Hit by Unauthorized Access, Member Data Leaked
summary: Signal Talk Co., Ltd. disclosed that unauthorized access to its online mahjong service Maru-Jan exposed email addresses and passwords of 1,855,578 members.
Attackers abused a function of the management system to download member data by November 4 at about 15:00. Credit card numbers were not included because the company does not hold them.
The company identified the entry point, fixed the exploited weakness, and resumed service on November 7 at 16:00. Members are urged to change passwords and receive 3,000 points as compensation.

c6d5de7578b7fc87.title: BookOff Group Holdings Subsidiary Member Management System Breached, Personal Data of 6,383,279 Members Leaked
summary: Bookoff Corporation, a subsidiary of BookOff Group Holdings, detected unauthorized access to its member management system between October 4 and 6.
Attackers abused an access control weakness in part of the system to obtain member data.
About 6.38 million members were affected, with names, birth dates, email addresses, phone numbers, addresses, and password hashes exposed. The company has notified affected members.

2da26cb58efc3220.title: Unauthorized Access Hits Subcontractor Handling Muji Custom Curtain Business
summary: Ryohin Keikaku said a server run by Nanotech, a subcontractor for its custom curtain business, was hit by unauthorized access and may have leaked some customer data.
Nanotech found signs of the intrusion dating to Oct 19 and reported it on Oct 28, covering 19,933 custom curtain orders placed from April 10, 2018 to January 25, 2022.
Ryohin Keikaku will notify affected customers by mail in stages, while Nanotech works with outside specialists to determine the attack method and whether data was taken.

3682c8558fa11d6d.title: ApplyNow Recruitment Platform Unauthorized Access Exposes Data of 396,920 People
summary: ApplyNow, a recruitment management service provider, disclosed unauthorized access to its platform starting August 9, 2026.
Attackers exploited a vulnerability in a data analysis tool used internally, gained administrator privileges, and bulk-acquired the database on September 7.

The company said personal data of 396,920 applicants and contractors and 30,067 ApplyNow Sign contractors was exposed, and according to ITmedia, some records included My Number and bank account information.
Yoshinoya Holdings said 5,366 former part-time applicant records and 418 recruiter accounts were leaked from data left after contract termination.
ApplyNow applied vulnerability patches and IP restrictions, and as of November 4, 2026, no secondary damage had been confirmed.

a839ce02d1ed66f9.title: Unauthorized Access at Securitize Japan Exposes Customer Data of Marui Group and Sony Bank
summary: Marui Group and Sony Bank announced that unauthorized access to the systems of Securitize Japan, their outsourced provider for digital securities operations, occurred on October 29.

According to INTERNET Watch, an authentication flaw was exploited to seize administrator privileges, and information was taken out of the system. Technical details of the attack have not been disclosed.
Marui Group said names, addresses, contact details, dates of birth, account numbers and investment amounts of up to 9,086 customers were exposed, and 54 account numbers may have been leaked.
Sony Bank confirmed the leak of account numbers for 4 customers and names for 617 customers, while NTT DATA and other providers reported exposure affecting more than 9,000 people in total.
The related service remains suspended. The companies are contacting affected customers individually and have demanded that the provider investigate the cause and prevent recurrence.

adacb3874e8ba503.title: Nojima Online Member Data Breach Exposes About 7 Million Records
summary: Home appliance retailer Nojima said unauthorized third parties accessed the member management systems of its online store Nojima Online and a used smartphone buyback site, leading to a data breach.

The company detected the intrusion on November 1 and confirmed that personal data of about 7 million records, excluding withdrawn members, was exposed, including names, addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth, email addresses, login IDs, and encrypted passwords.
According to ITmedia, passwords for the affected accounts were forcibly reset, and card information was not stored and therefore was not exposed.
Nojima suspended both sites, blocked external access, consulted the National Police Agency, and reported to the Personal Information Protection Commission, with no date set for resumption.

c39d45f4d8310c5b.title: NetMile Member Data of Up to 5.49 Million Possibly Exposed in Unauthorized Access
summary: Wills Co., Ltd., operator of the point service NetMile, announced on November 2 that unauthorized access by a third party had occurred.
Intrusion into its systems may have led to the leak of part of its members' personal data, and the cause is still under investigation.

Up to about 5.49 million records, including those of withdrawn members, containing names and email addresses may have been exposed, and no secondary damage has been confirmed so far, according to Security NEXT.
The company has suspended the NetMile and Sugutama sites and plans to notify affected individuals as required by law, according to ScanNetSecurity.

039f54969f5c1f3b.title: Unauthorized Access to Shimane Furusato Direct Delivery Store via Amazon Pay Plugin Vulnerability
summary: Shimane Prefecture said an unauthorized third party created a rogue admin account on the Shimane Furusato Direct Delivery e-commerce site on August 13 and planted a file to capture payment form inputs.
The intrusion exploited a vulnerability in the Amazon Pay plugin used on the EC-CUBE platform, and was confirmed on August 14 after the platform provider issued a warning.
Credit card data of seven customers who paid between August 13 and 15 may have been exposed, but no fraudulent use had been confirmed as of November 1. A WAF is being introduced.

097e7b233dced990.title: Tokyu Fudosan Website Hit by Unauthorized Access
summary: Tokyu Fudosan disclosed that unauthorized third parties accessed a shared AWS server environment hosting some of its managed websites, potentially exposing personal data.
The intrusion exploited software vulnerabilities in the content management system, such as WordPress, and misconfigured server access permissions.

The company detected the intrusion on October 19 and took the sites offline, and says up to 4,079 GREEN CROSS PARK member records and 3 GREENUP Cooldown Project inquiries may be affected, though leakage has not been confirmed.

950bc1856435b214.title: Input Validation Flaw Found in Effekseer
summary: A input data validation flaw (CVE-2026-120386) has been disclosed in the Effekseer particle effect editing tool.
Opening a maliciously crafted effect file in an application that embeds the runtime can cause the application to crash.
Effekseer 1.80.7 and earlier are affected, and the issue is fixed in 1.80.8. JVN urges users to update to the latest version.

397c02f2fbe64491.title: Japanese CISOs Cite Malicious Insiders as Top Cause of Data Loss, 98% Say Departing Employees Were a Factor, Proofpoint Survey
summary: Proofpoint released the Japanese edition of its 2026 Voice of the CISO report. The share of Japanese organizations that suffered a material data loss rose from 35% in 2025 to 49% in 2026, while the global average fell from 66% to 53%.

Malicious or criminally motivated insiders were the most cited cause of data loss at 53%. Of Japanese CISOs whose organizations suffered material data loss, 98% said departing employees were a contributing factor.

Japanese organizations reporting financial losses rose from 9% to 43%, and post-attack recovery costs rose from 34% to 41%. The survey covered more than 1,600 CISOs in 16 countries and regions in May 2026.

af8fbff76095d121.title: About One-Third of Companies With Fewer Than 50 Employees in Japan's Chugoku Region Have No Security Staff, Survey Finds
summary: HENNGE and The Chugoku Shimbun surveyed 309 IT staff in five Chugoku prefectures from August 13 to September 11, 2026, to assess information security practices.

Among companies with fewer than 50 employees, 35.6% reported having no security staff, and 43.8% said they do not run targeted email attack training. Email-based attacks were the most commonly experienced type.

HENNGE warned that smaller firms may lack the staff and budget for needed measures, raising concern about supply chain attacks that use weakly protected companies as entry points to reach business partners.

5d306d1fafeb8bf0.title: Credential-Stealing Campaign Hijacks 4,837 GitHub Accounts to Target Over 60,000 Repositories
summary: In a campaign dubbed 'wfx-loot' that began on November 10, 2026, attackers used 4,837 hijacked GitHub accounts to check write access across more than 60,000 repositories.

The attackers first tested write access with pull requests, then used a PR titled 'docs: dependency audit notes' to plant roughly 1,500 lines of credential-stealing code in workflows, CI shell scripts, and npm install hooks.

The campaign did not exploit a GitHub vulnerability and instead abused valid developer and bot tokens. The payload harvests tokens, secrets, and cloud and AI service keys and attempts to escalate privileges in AWS and Azure.
Reported impact varies by source. BleepingComputer said at least 1,835 targets had secrets stolen, while Aikido confirmed execution traces in more than 1,800 repositories.
Malicious versions were also published to some Packagist and Go modules. Organizations with confirmed execution should immediately rotate all secrets and cloud credentials.

e2f1632f58d0c014.title: Microsoft 365 Outage Disrupts Outlook, Exchange Online and Teams
summary: A widespread Microsoft 365 outage disrupted access to Exchange Online, Teams and other cloud services across multiple regions.
Microsoft attributed the problem to many servers becoming unavailable and is investigating failed health checks and elevated processor usage.
Microsoft has found no evidence of a cyberattack, and its advisories do not link the outage to the CVE-2026-124194 Outlook flaw from its November Patch Tuesday.

c77f1bb1a1570095.title: Critical Apache HTTP Server mod_http2 Flaw Enables Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution (CVE-2026-119618), Patched
summary: A critical unauthenticated remote code execution flaw (CVE-2026-119618) in the mod_http2 module of Apache HTTP Server has been fixed in version 2.4.71.
The race condition stems from improper synchronization when shared resources are processed concurrently, leading to heap memory corruption.
Versions 2.4.55 through 2.4.70 are affected, but only servers with HTTP/2 enabled are at risk. Red Hat rated the flaw CVSS 9.8 and classified it as Important for RHEL 9 and 10.
SecurityWeek reported no active exploitation so far, while The Hacker News said public research has demonstrated a working exploit.
If patching is not immediately possible, administrators should remove h2 and h2c from the Protocols setting to disable HTTP/2 as a temporary workaround.

7d193c08bd2fafe6.title: Microsoft November 2026 Patch Tuesday Fixes Over 1,000 Flaws Including Exploited Outlook Zero-Day
summary: Microsoft fixed more than 1,000 vulnerabilities in its November 2026 Patch Tuesday update. Counts reported by outlets range from 1,093 to 1,259, with 63 to 68 rated critical.
The Outlook spoofing flaw CVE-2026-124194 is under active exploitation. Opening a malicious message file can leak NTLMv2 hashes to an attacker-controlled server.
CrowdStrike assessed that the attacks involve forced authentication (T1187), spearphishing attachments (T1566.001), and adversary-in-the-middle (T1557) techniques.
A Chrome XML component zero-day, CVE-2026-125350, is also being exploited. Patches also cover Outlook and Word preview pane flaws and critical LDAP and AD DS remote code execution bugs.
CISA added the Outlook flaw to its KEV catalog and ordered federal agencies to patch by November 24, 2026. Cisco Talos recommends Snort rules as interim protection until systems are patched.

fef5b808b533acef.title: Maersk Confirms Data Theft from Legacy System of Acquired Firm as WhiteArmor Demands $5M
summary: Danish shipping company Maersk has confirmed that data was stolen from a legacy system belonging to a company it acquired previously.

The WhiteArmor ransomware group claims it stole about 100GB of data from the LF Logistics platform, acquired by Maersk in 2022, and is demanding $5 million in bitcoin, alleging the data includes plaintext passwords.
Maersk says the breach is limited to the local system and has no impact on operations, other systems connected via API or EDI, or customers and partners.
The company says sensitive information does not appear to have been exposed, and the investigation is ongoing.

109b3079c80f9bc8.title: ThreatsDay: 59 Linux Kernel Bugs, Falcon Spyware, GSocket Backdoors + 17 More Stories
summary: North Korean threat actors linked to the theft of $6.43 billion from Binance are laundering the proceeds using automated methods.
The stolen funds moved through more than 20,000 wallets on 16 blockchains, including bridges, DEXs and mixers, and part was routed through meme coins on the NEAR network.
Microsoft reported a 356% rise in GSocket detections from March to August 2026, while Europol seized 235 servers tied to GootLoader, CastleRAT and StealC.

1b13a58bf5865a4e.title: Trained to betray: How post-training supply chain attacks hijack coding agents
summary: Microsoft Defender Research and the Microsoft AI Red Team published studies on backdoors that target coding agents through the post-training supply chain.
In a dataset poisoning experiment, 90 crafted examples hidden in roughly 9,000 conversations taught a model to misuse command-execution tools on routine requests, with about 78% attack success.
In a model poisoning experiment, the backdoor still activated at 84.1% to 94.8% on unseen repositories. The researchers recommend strict tool permission limits and checkpoint provenance verification.

375bf248f8cc2716.title: Critical Red Hat Quay Flaw Lets Attackers Read and Overwrite Private Container Images
summary: Red Hat has disclosed CVE-2026-123710, a critical flaw in Red Hat Quay with a CVSS score of 9.8. It can be exploited without an account when anonymous access is enabled.
Attackers can add their own non-expiring signing key to the trusted key list, forging repository tokens by abusing a weakness in the key rotation process.
The attack could lead to unauthorized access to private images and embedded credentials, and images could be overwritten.
According to The Hacker News, Red Hat has shipped fixes for Quay 3 across eight branches, while SecurityWeek reports that no fixed version has been released yet.
Red Hat advises blocking the /keys endpoint at proxies, reviewing service_key_rotate audit logs, and deleting any malicious keys.

cdaae6cd5c68eaff.title: 186 Fake AI Domains Redirect Users to ClickFix Lures, Browser Malware, and Search Hijackers
summary: Island identified 186 lookalike domains impersonating 27 AI brands and named the campaign TypoPrompting.

Parked domains lead to a fake Cloudflare verification page that runs a PowerShell command, a browser-hijacking malware called Net Guard, and 16 search-hijacking Chrome extensions with 972,000 declared users.
As of November 3, 2026, the extensions had 972,000 users in total, and some of the domains were registered as early as July 2023.

188a549b157b1cff.title: Attackers Use Autonomous AI to Target Semiconductor, Defense and Civil Society Sectors
summary: From August to September 2026, Chinese-speaking attackers used the open-source AI penetration testing framework Cairn to autonomously run 25 operations against at least 19 organizations.
The attackers paired Cairn with the Chinese AI models Zhipu GLM and DeepSeek, supplying only a target and a goal while the framework planned, executed and logged the attacks.

Unauthorized access or data retrieval was confirmed at 10 organizations, with one exposing over one million personal records. Unit 42 assesses with moderate confidence that this is China-nexus intelligence collection.

a1bbf8bee2f67799.title: Hijacked email accounts complicate investigations into European bomb hoaxes
summary: Bomb threats sent to thousands of European schools this week were traced to a hijacked account at Taiwan's Da-Yeh University.
Because the messages came from real, trusted accounts, they passed authentication checks and spam filters, complicating attribution.
Schools in Italy, Scotland, Northern Ireland and Ireland were targeted, but police called the threats not credible and no actor has been named.

600e3c7dbe82bdff.title: Unauthorized Access to Japan Chamber of Commerce and Industry Exam System Raises Data Breach Risk for Up to 980,000 Examinees
summary: The Japan Chamber of Commerce and Industry disclosed unauthorized access to the management system of its Nisshō Net Test online examination platform.
Security NEXT reported that personal data of up to about 980,000 examinees may have been exposed, while Impress Watch cited 1.97 million records.
ITmedia reported that examinee data, including bookkeeping test pass/fail results and scores, may have been included.
The breach was confirmed on November 4, 2026, after the system administrator reported it, and malicious programs had been installed on an external server.

Malicious files were deleted and the vulnerability was patched. No actual leak or misuse has been confirmed. The incident was reported to the Personal Information Protection Commission, and examinees were warned about phishing and other scams.

5e50df9ec32419b6.title: Crafty Microsoft Teams Booking Flow Disguises Device Code Phishing
summary: A spear-phishing email impersonating a senior executive at a construction firm lured the target through a fake Microsoft Teams meeting booking page to enter a device code.
The site copied a disguised device code to the clipboard and had the victim enter it on Microsoft's genuine device-login page, letting the attacker obtain access tokens.
Huntress SOC quickly detected and contained the attack, which led to token theft; reviewing accounts and tightening conditional access are recommended.

d308a35b6bbbc96f.title: Chrome, Firefox Updates Patch Over 180 Vulnerabilities
summary: Google and Mozilla released security updates for Chrome, Firefox, and Thunderbird that fix more than 180 vulnerabilities.
Chrome 157 fixes 83 flaws, including five critical issues, with use-after-free bugs being the most common type.
Google found 52 of the flaws internally and Anthropic and OpenAI researchers reported 18 more. Neither company has reported any of them being exploited in the wild.

81d59fe58cb267de.title: Russia-linked Turla hackers use Cereal malware to steal government email from Exchange servers in Romania and Kazakhstan
summary: Russia-linked hacking group Turla compromised Microsoft Exchange servers at government agencies in Romania and Kazakhstan, intercepting emails exchanged with NATO and EU officials.

ESET said the attackers used a modular .NET toolset called Cereal, injecting code into EdgeTransport.exe to hijack the transport agent and using the compromised Exchange server as a command hub without any external C2 server.
Romania's intelligence service SRI said it detected and blocked the intrusion in December 2025, found no evidence of data theft, and confirmed that email services had been restored.
The Record reported that a Microsoft system vulnerability was exploited, but SRI has not disclosed the initial access route and ESET says the initial intrusion vector remains unconfirmed.
The malware receives commands through traffic that resembles normal Exchange web activity, so defenders should use detection rules to check for further compromise.

dfd228e94f43a365.title: Kazakhstan-linked hackers used AI agent to spy on Central Asian governments
summary: Singapore-based CloudSEK found an exposed server linked to Silent Lynx, a group suspected of ties to Kazakhstan, that held stolen government documents and hacking tools.

The operator used Hermes, an open-source AI agent built on DeepSeek models, to automate reconnaissance, data theft and log erasure, including a months-long intrusion into Tajikistan's national railway network.

The group also prepared phishing files disguised as Turkmen government documents, but researchers could not confirm whether those attacks succeeded, and the Kazakhstan link was assessed with medium confidence.

5b10c2fe549bffda.title: Microsoft: Recent Windows updates cause SQL Server performance issues
summary: Microsoft has confirmed that Windows updates released since the October 2026 Patch Tuesday are causing SQL Server performance and stability problems.
Linked server queries using OLE DB providers leave connections to external databases such as Oracle and PostgreSQL open, so the connections accumulate over time.
Administrators can temporarily close the stray connections or restart the SQL service, while Microsoft plans an out-of-band Windows update within days.

145e764d7bd5433f.title: Google Cloud Warns Three AMD Turin CPU Flaws Could Leak Data Across Processes in VMs
summary: Google Cloud has disclosed three CPU side-channel flaws affecting virtual machines on AMD Turin processors.
All three are Transient Scheduler Attacks (TSA), which may let an attacker running code on the same core infer data from other processes or the kernel.
Google has mitigated attacks between VMs and the host. Customers must install guest OS patches and stop and start their VMs, and no exploitation has been reported.

147934e7192f220a.title: Calendar Invites and Live Proxies: Inside a Google Session Hijacking Campaign
summary: Since mid-August 2026, a phishing campaign disguised as Google Calendar invites has been hijacking live Google sessions of corporate users.
The attacker routes victims through Google's redirector and Cloudflare Turnstile to a reverse proxy that relays the real Google sign-in page, capturing passwords and second factors.
Material Security's Threat Research team took down hundreds of attacker domains under Operation CloudFire and caught over 99% of malicious messages once detections were in place.

0dd76931c20a8a71.title: Exploit Attempts for GPUStack Authentication Bypass (CVE-2026-102895), (Thu, Nov 12th)
summary: Exploit attempts targeting CVE-2026-102895, an authentication bypass flaw in GPUStack, an open-source tool for managing GPU clusters, have been observed.
Attackers spoof the X-Gpustack-Real-IP header as 127.0.0.1 so requests appear to come from a trusted source, bypassing authentication.
All versions before 2.2.0 are affected, and the source IP 144.91.73.103 has been probing other AI-related endpoints.

6181223d4cce4928.title: PTC Patches Critical Windchill and FlexPLM Flaw That Could Enable Remote Code Execution
summary: PTC has released patches for a critical flaw in Windchill and FlexPLM, tracked as CVE-2026-126325, that could allow remote code execution.
The bug stems from improper input validation and deserialization of untrusted data, and carries a CVSS v4 score of 9.2.
PTC-hosted environments were patched automatically, while self-hosted users are urged to patch now and check their hosts for web shells.

ed8a92b3e208d760.title: Tamura City Nursery Staff Fall Victim to Tech Support Scam After Fake Warning
summary: Tamura City in Fukushima Prefecture said a staff member at a early childhood nursery facility fell victim to a tech support scam, possibly exposing personal data stored on the computer.
The employee followed a fake malware warning to a scam site and downloaded remote access software.
Exposed data may include nursery activity photos and names from post-event surveys, and the city plans to strengthen training to prevent recurrence.

017e94aed87d8921.title: Fireworks AI Breach Exposes Notion Customer AI Chat Logs
summary: Notion disclosed that some customer data was exposed in a breach at AI inference provider Fireworks AI and notified affected customers directly.
Fireworks AI suffered two breaches in October, with attackers using stolen internal credentials to reach development systems through a third-party cloud provider hosting its R&D equipment.
Chat logs from Notion AI's Insights feature were accessed, affecting less than 1% of workspaces, and the feature has been disabled.
Fireworks AI said billing information, incomplete model weights and datasets were also taken, while payment card numbers were not stored and were unaffected.

Notion advised users who entered passwords or API keys into chat to rotate those credentials, while Fireworks AI revoked compromised credentials, isolated systems and is working with Palo Alto Networks Unit 42.

75d01a8c0c2bb443.title: Shiseido Discloses Leak of Personal Data and Skin Test Results from Skin Measurement System
summary: Shiseido said an online skin measurement system used by its group skin testing service, Facial Condition Analyzer (FCA), was breached by an external third party, exposing customer personal data and test results.
The company confirmed the intrusion on October 27, 2026, and its investigation found that some system data was altered and taken outside.
A total of 2,515 customer personal records were leaked, and facial images taken during testing were excluded. To prevent further damage, Shiseido suspended the Beauty Alive Circulation Check service.

fc4650b1ff4d20ff.title: 0% GPU utilization: How SANSAR hides Linux cryptomining
summary: Elastic Security Labs is tracking intrusion activity dubbed REF3364, in which an attacker gained root by abusing an exposed, unauthenticated Ray job agent.
SANSAR communicates with its C2 over Tor and manages CPU and GPU miners, while an NVML wrapper reports 0% GPU utilization and a kernel rootkit hides processes and files.
A separate netns backdoor retrieves its C2 address from an Ethereum smart contract. The article does not detail the full scale of victims or current response measures.

aeb777e255e8f115.title: Microsoft confirms Windows security updates installation issues
summary: Microsoft has confirmed that the November 2026 security updates fail to install on some Windows 11 devices that installed the October 2026 preview update (KB5127936).
Affected devices may stall during installation, show error codes 0x80070306, 0x800f0989, or 0x800f0993, or repeatedly retry the update.
Microsoft says a fix will apply automatically within 24 to 48 hours starting November 11, 2026 at 10am PT, and admins still facing issues after 48 hours should contact Microsoft Support.

a24a66da27131b91.title: Transcending the trust boundaries: how a cloud pentest works
summary: Kaspersky Securelist has published an introductory article on how penetration testing of cloud environments is performed.
Beyond the external layer, the method examines trust boundaries between the tenant, overlay, and underlay layers.
The article covers no specific vulnerability or incident and stresses that the key goal is assessing whether an attacker can cross trust boundaries.

b716fc257c2e7c98.title: N-able N-central Zero-Day Flaws Disclosed With PoC Exploits Amid Attack Attempts
summary: Security researcher Sean Bales published more than 30 zero-day flaws and PoC exploits for N-able's N-central RMM platform on GitHub on November 8, dubbing the chain Able2Shell.
The disclosed flaws include XXE, XSS, SSRF, directory traversal, arbitrary file write, credential exposure, and remote code execution.
The attack chain can use an unauthenticated XXE flaw to hijack trusted sessions, execute commands on servers, and create admin accounts, with some flaws enabling root privilege escalation.
N-able temporarily took hosted N-central environments offline and patched unauthenticated flaws first, urging on-premises customers to apply N-central 2026.4 HF2 and review login records.
The company said it had not confirmed any exploitation, but SecurityWeek reported active attack attempts, and BleepingComputer reported exposed servers dropped from 1,338 to 148.

07aae71b68b3c4ca.title: Threat Actors Abuse Open-Source Remote Access Tool GSocket for Persistent Access to Linux Servers
summary: Multiple threat actors are abusing GSocket, a legitimate open-source remote access tool, to maintain access to Linux servers even after vulnerabilities are patched.

GSocket relays outbound connections from both sides through a public relay network, bypassing firewalls and NAT, while attackers establish persistence via cron, systemd, and shell startup files and masquerade as kernel threads.
Microsoft also observed attempts to escalate privileges to root using CVE-2026-43284.
According to BleepingComputer, detections rose 356.2% since March, with web applications and hosting environments accounting for 87.1%.

Microsoft reported a similar 356.2% increase from March to August, with education and research institutions suffering the most damage, and recommends restricting outbound traffic and checking for persistence.

f3bb3fce5990229c.title: Critical Unauthenticated MongoDB Server Flaw (CVE-2026-118383) Can Crash Servers During Failover
summary: A critical unauthenticated flaw in MongoDB Server (CVE-2026-118383, CVSS 4.0 score 9.5) has been disclosed.
The use-after-free bug occurs when cleanup code runs twice after a lagging replica set member is elected primary in a later election.
According to The Hacker News, two unauthenticated requests can crash the database server, while Security NEXT reports that certain conditions may lead to arbitrary code execution.
No exploitation was observed at disclosure, and fixes are available in versions 9.0.7, 8.3.16, and 8.0.37; MongoDB Atlas applies the update automatically.
Self-managed deployments should patch all replica set members and restrict network access until patching is complete.

c8aa88a83de492a6.title: Node.js Fixes 16 Flaws, Including HTTP/2 Bugs That Crash Servers and Leak Other Connections' Data
summary: Node.js released security updates for its 22.x, 24.x and 26.x lines that fix 16 vulnerabilities, including several in HTTP/2 and HTTPS server code.

An unauthenticated client can crash an HTTP/2 server that replies before the request body fully arrives (CVE-2026-123863), and under some conditions can leak memory from other connections (CVE-2026-123866).
CVE-2026-123864 in HTTPS servers can let a client read memory from other connections, including TLS private keys. No attacks have been reported, and updating is the only fix listed.

2b2f3e80b4c9efac.title: Korea's Financial Security Institute, Described as a Security Control Tower, Hit by Hacking Attack and 650 Personal Records Leaked
summary: ITmedia reported that South Korea's Financial Security Institute suffered a hacking attack that leaked 650 personal records.
The article text provided consists only of a site access ranking, so the attack method and how the leak occurred cannot be confirmed.
The scope of the damage and the institute's response cannot be determined from the text.

2a0b8f3c8bf29b61.title: Summary of Fake Sites Impersonating the National Police Agency Recommended App Download Page
summary: Fake SMS messages impersonating the National Police Agency directed users to a counterfeit NPA page that offered a malicious APK disguised as the NPA-recommended app.
The fake app showed a fake Google Play update screen, requested VPN and full device control permissions, and a sample restored and installed a second hidden APK.
The NPA urged people not to click URLs in SMS messages and to download apps only from official sites or app stores. The number of victims has not been confirmed.

b4e93ad83798cdcf.title: OS Command Injection Vulnerability in SoftBank Air Terminal 6 Home Router, Fixable via Automatic Firmware Update
summary: JVN has disclosed an OS command injection vulnerability (CVE-2026-101107) in the SoftBank Air Terminal 6 home router.
A user who can log in to the web management interface may execute arbitrary commands with root privileges; firmware v1.01.80 and earlier are affected.
SoftBank released a fixed firmware in September 2026, which is applied automatically, so users need not take action.

79e53cac6ae80fb8.title: Summary of the Unauthorized Access to Matomaru EC Tenchou
summary: On November 9, 2026, Brangista Solution disclosed possible unauthorized access and data leakage affecting its multi-store management service Matomaru EC Tenchou.

Attackers sent fake refund emails containing real order information, directing recipients to register on an official LINE account and enter personal data. A suspicious script querying order data was found on the server.
About 373 companies and up to 21,873 order records may be affected. Payment card data is not stored, and no financial harm or publication of stolen data has been confirmed so far.

3d9e82813fa861da.title: Chrome 157 Zero-Day CVE-2026-125350 Exploited in the Wild, Followed by Large Security Update
summary: Google released Chrome 157 security updates on November 9 fixing nine vulnerabilities, one of which, CVE-2026-125350, is a zero-day exploited in the wild.
The flaw is a use-after-free bug in the XML component that allows attackers to execute arbitrary code by abusing freed memory.
An anonymous researcher reported the bug to Google on November 6, and it is rated High severity.
According to multiple security outlets, it is the eighth Chrome zero-day exploited this year, and Google has not disclosed details about the threat actor or attack methods.
On November 11, Google addressed 83 more vulnerabilities in Chrome 157.0.8103.79 and related builds, including five Critical flaws, all of them use-after-free bugs.

b034deb97d7bdadf.title: Adobe Patches About 110 Vulnerabilities Across Nine Products
summary: Adobe released security updates in its November 2026 patch cycle, fixing about 110 vulnerabilities across nine products.
Adobe Connect fixes include SSRF, path traversal, SQL injection, and missing access control flaws, some of which allowed privilege escalation and arbitrary code execution.

According to SecurityWeek, 38 issues were resolved in Connect and Adobe Experience Manager, including six flaws rated CVSS 10.0. Security NEXT reported that 21 of the 110 total issues were classified as critical.
Adobe said it had no evidence that these vulnerabilities were exploited in attacks as of publication, and users are advised to apply the security updates for each affected product.

5195c39e9c09400c.title: Ivanti and Citrix Patch Critical Vulnerabilities Across Multiple Products
summary: Ivanti and Citrix have released security patches for vulnerabilities in their products, including several rated critical and high severity.

According to Security NEXT, Ivanti addressed 13 unique CVEs across five products, including an SQL injection flaw in Endpoint Manager EPM Core, CVE-2026-121653 with a CVSS score of 9.8, that could allow code execution without authentication.
A separate flaw in Ivanti CSA, CVE-2026-121683 with a CVSS score of 9.4, stems from weak authentication and could allow changes to certificate registration information.
SecurityWeek reported that the Citrix and Ivanti patches cover 19 vulnerabilities, with Citrix fixing six XenServer flaws and an AMD CPU issue.
Security NEXT reported no exploitation or damage, and Ivanti told SecurityWeek it has no evidence of exploitation of these flaws.

2de341f68914ee09.title: JPCERT/CC Releases Incident Investigation Report Checklist for Ransomware and Data Leak Cases
summary: JPCERT/CC published an incident investigation report checklist on GitHub on November 11 to help organizations commissioning external investigations after ransomware attacks and data breaches.
Many companies now outsource incident investigations, but first-time clients often struggle to judge the validity of findings or whether an incident has been fully closed.
The checklist provides shared standards for clients and report writers, with separate user and reporter versions available in HTML and Markdown formats for public use.
According to INTERNET Watch, a 42-page sample report based on a hypothetical case was also released, while Impress Watch reported that the sample is provided in PDF format.

610190acb64c4a3c.title: Firefox 160 Released - Fixes 99 Vulnerabilities
summary: Mozilla released Firefox 160, the latest version of its web browser, on November 10, 2026 (local time), fixing 99 vulnerabilities.
No critical-severity flaws are included, but 57 are rated high. A Use After Free flaw in CanvasWebGL (CVE-2026-124907) could lead to privilege escalation or sandbox bypass.

A Use After Free flaw in inter-process communication (CVE-2026-124903) could allow sandbox escape, and flaws that bypass the same-origin policy were also fixed. Users should update their browsers to the latest version.

01c0fac81ae03034.title: Remote Attacks on European Supermarket Refrigeration Controllers Force Mass Food Disposal
summary: Since October 2026, refrigeration and freezer systems at hundreds of French supermarkets and other European retail outlets were remotely manipulated, raising set temperatures and forcing mass food disposal.
Attackers appear to have exploited authentication bypass and code injection flaws in internet-exposed or unpatched refrigeration controllers to force defrost modes and raise temperatures.
According to SecurityWeek, more than 100 stores in six countries, including Belgium, Estonia and Ireland, were affected during the night of November 2 to 3.

A French blood storage facility and a UK meat supplier were also hit. According to INTERNET Watch, the French Ministry of Foreign Affairs attributed the attacks to Iran, while other sources have not confirmed the responsible party.
US CISA and FBI urged operators to disconnect devices from the internet, change default passwords, deploy firewalls and multifactor authentication, and apply security updates.

4155e78352c02df5.title: Ransomware Shifts from One-Time Ransom Demands to Ongoing Extortion, Proofpoint Survey Finds
summary: Proofpoint Japan released the Japanese edition of its 2026 AI-Era Ransomware Report on October 27, 2026.
37% of Japanese organizations hit by ransomware paid the ransom, and 37% of those payers received a second extortion demand.
Malicious attachments were the top initial access vector at 71%, and 66% of Japanese respondents said AI made attacks more effective.

1171f49b6dd7bb88.title: Personal Data Breaches at Listed Companies Hit Record High, Tokyo Shoko Research Finds
summary: Tokyo Shoko Research reported that listed companies and their subsidiaries disclosed 215 personal data breach or loss incidents from January to October 2026.
The count already exceeds the 2024 annual record of 189, with 109 incidents in October alone.

Ten breaches exceeded 10 million records, and total exposed records reached about 350 million, over ten times the prior year. The largest case, at SG Holdings (Sagawa Express), involved unauthorized access to a website and up to 53.23 million records.

9ce63de4336a66ac.title: NTT Data Breach Exposes Personal Data of About 80,000 Vitality Users After Unauthorized Access to Sumitomo Life Contractor System
summary: NTT Data said on November 9 that an unauthorized third party accessed a system it operates under contract for Sumitomo Life Insurance, which runs the Vitality service.
According to ScanNetSecurity, the unauthorized access occurred on November 2, and the attack method has not been disclosed.
About 80,000 users had their names, addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth, and email addresses exposed.
According to ITmedia, partially masked card numbers were exposed for about 1,000 users, while insurance contract information and step count data were not included.

NTT Data blocked the external access and suspended the service on November 3, and no misuse of the leaked data has been confirmed so far. Sumitomo Life is identifying affected individuals and operating a customer inquiry desk.

c42a88beb7f7c809.title: Unauthorized Access Hits MOTEX, No Impact on Main Functions of LANSCOPE Products
summary: Kyocera Communication Systems published a second report on unauthorized access to its subsidiary MOTEX.

MOTEX confirmed unauthorized access to a server running its website on November 2, cut external communications, and suspended the affected sites. An external investigation found possible leakage of customer information.
The possibly leaked data includes company names, names, email addresses, and phone numbers. MOTEX says LANSCOPE products run in a separate environment and their main functions are not affected.

4d027215ce634e74.title: Yakult Honsha Website Unauthorized Access Leads to Data Breach of About 40,000 Records
summary: Yakult Honsha said it detected unauthorized access to its official website on October 26, 2026, and suspended website functions the same day.

A third party gained unauthorized access and data was leaked from inquiry forms, media inquiry forms, and Tanoshii Kyushoku member records, including names, contact details, email addresses, inquiry content, and encrypted passwords.
According to Yakult Honsha and ITmedia NEWS, about 40,000 records were leaked, while Security NEXT reported 39,505 cases confirmed as of November 4, 2026.
The attack method and intrusion route have not been disclosed. The company said it did not store credit card or bank account information.
The company reported the incident to the Personal Information Protection Commission and is consulting with the police while investigating the cause. No restoration date for the website has been set.

6b5ad8c17d5707b9.title: ANA Trading Unauthorized Access Incident Affects Selectable e-GIFT Service
summary: ANA Trading announced on October 30 that its Selectable e-GIFT service had been hit by unauthorized access from outside.

The company suspended the service on October 23, expanded its investigation, and confirmed external intrusion. It is working with outside security specialists on the root cause and new attack methods.

No leak of customer personal data or fraudulent exchange or use of issued gift cards has been confirmed so far. All services remain suspended until security is ensured, and a long recovery period is expected.

323732632a7c4363.title: Fake Bot-Check Screen Prompting Command Execution and Trap Targeting Outdated iOS Devices Found on Meiji Gakuin University Site
summary: Meiji Gakuin University announced on November 5 that the website of its Department of Psychology was tampered with after unauthorized access by a third party.
An administrator account was misused to plant malicious code, and visitors may have seen fake screens and traps between the evening of October 16 and midday on October 19.
Mac users were shown a fake bot-check page asking them to run commands, while older iPhone and iPad devices faced a separate exploit. The university said no personal data leak has been confirmed.

3bf0b2fdfae336ec.title: Baker Tilly notifies clients of data breach at third-party provider
summary: US accounting firm Baker Tilly is notifying clients that personal information of clients and their dependents was compromised in a data breach at a third-party service provider.
Baker Tilly learned of the incident on September 6 and finished reviewing affected data on October 28. The unauthorized actor and the provider's name have not been disclosed.
