Texas alone reports 10,456 affected individuals, with Social Security numbers, names, and addresses exposed. Baker Tilly is offering 24 months of Experian credit and identity monitoring.

09419016bbe54bb1.title: ARTEX and AI-Powered Red Teaming Tools: What Defenders Need to Know
summary: Unit 42 reports that attackers are using ARTEX, an AI penetration testing framework marketed for red teaming, to run autonomous intrusions.
The attacks target exposed password reset pages and APIs to reach cloud environments, sometimes within a day, without exploiting software vulnerabilities.
As of October 2026, Unit 42 counted 609 hosts running ARTEX and 1,323 running CyberStrikeAI, and recommends reducing public exposure and detecting operator behavior.

7296cb05dd1c8aff.title: HTTP Header Injection Vulnerability in KUSANAGI
summary: IPA and JPCERT/CC published a vulnerability note on November 9 describing an HTTP header injection flaw in KUSANAGI, reported by GMO Prime Strategy.
A CRLF sanitization flaw in the redirect rules of the Nginx configuration for WordPress (CVE-2026-117477) lets attackers using crafted URLs inject arbitrary HTTP response headers.

Security/Enterprise Edition 10.7.2-1 and earlier and Free/Business/Premium Edition 9.12.2-1 and earlier are affected, and users are urged to update or apply mitigations; Apache httpd setups are excluded.

95aa9877b30955e7.title: Hokkaido IT Staff Rate Their Security Measures as Adequate Below 50%, Lower Than Three Other Regions: HENNGE and Hokkaido Shimbun Survey
summary: HENNGE and Hokkaido Shimbun released survey results on security practices among 238 IT staff in Hokkaido, conducted in August 2026.
Fewer than half rated their measures as adequate, below three other surveyed regions, and email-based attacks such as phishing and BEC were the most common experienced threats.
Of respondents, 26.5% reported experiencing a cyberattack and 29.0% were unsure, while 35.7% held ISMS certification.

2196615094ecb9ec.title: eMudhra Revokes 16 Intermediate CA Certificates After Private Key Handling Flaw
summary: Certificate authority eMudhra has revoked 16 intermediate CA certificates in total after an investigation into a key handling incident.
A bug in a custom Python script used to move private keys between HSMs weakened 8 ECDSA keys to roughly 1 byte of entropy and left 8 RSA keys exposed in unprotected memory.
According to BleepingComputer, eMudhra revoked 8 RSA intermediate CA certificates on November 7, 2026 and replaced customer certificates.
According to The Hacker News, the incident dates to a key migration on April 30, 2025, affecting 195 issued certificates, 29 of which were used on eMudhra's own domains.
No evidence of exploitation has been found, and KPMG is conducting an independent review of the incident.

6dfc2034c5258bad.title: Who Runs the Ransomware Group Qilin?
summary: Qilin, a ransomware-as-a-service group, claims at least 365 victims in the past three months alone, making it currently the most active ransomware affiliate program.
Krebs on Security reports that researchers linked the administrator, known as Haise, to older forum handles, emails, and Telegram accounts used across cybercrime forums.
These attribution claims come from private-sector analysis, and the article does not indicate that law enforcement has confirmed them.

0c3eb19fd143fc6c.title: Iran-backed network directed London attacks over FaceTime, US prosecutors say
summary: US prosecutors charged three men with orchestrating attacks across Europe for Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, including arson and stabbings.
The attacks were directed over FaceTime and filmed for propaganda, with one video projected alongside a militia logo.
Prosecutors also say the network plotted an attack on RAF Fairford air base, and two defendants believed to be in Iran remain at large.

29f1f1df1cca5a24.title: Lessons from 59 Linux Kernel Bug Reports
summary: Microsoft's FORGE Lab used its MDASH tool to scan parts of the Linux kernel from late May to mid-June 2026, producing 59 public bug reports and 33 CVEs.
The root cause is a use-after-free flaw in the rhashtable walker, which kept a stale pointer after a paused walk resumed. Working local privilege-escalation exploits were confirmed for eight CVEs.
Fixes for 38 reports have been merged into mainline. Turning 26,502 raw findings into validated reports took months of expert review.

4c3178a66dcfcb61.title: Zoom Workplace for Windows Patches Two Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation Flaws
summary: Zoom has released an update fixing two vulnerabilities in Zoom Workplace for Windows and urged users to install the latest version.

CVE-2026-108186 (CVSS 9.6) stems from improper input validation, while CVE-2026-108187 (CVSS 8.1) involves origin validation flaws, and both allow unauthenticated privilege escalation over the network.
The vendor has already fixed the flaws, with the patch included in Zoom Workplace for Windows version 7.1.8 and later.
No active exploitation has been reported so far.

b6de8528e8281051.title: Xen Orchestra Authentication Bypass Vulnerability Exploited in Attacks
summary: Vates warned that a critical authentication bypass flaw (VSA-2026-062) in Xen Orchestra is being exploited in real-world attacks.
By sending a crafted authenticationToken cookie, unauthenticated attackers can log in as existing token owners and gain administrator rights, potentially taking over XCP-ng hosts.
According to SecurityWeek, a flaw in REST authentication handling returns empty tokens without filtering, exposing valid login token IDs, and a second vulnerability is still being patched.
Reports differ on fixed versions: SecurityWeek cites releases before 6.9.2 and 6.10.1, while The Hacker News and BleepingComputer cite updates 6.9.1 and 6.10.0.
Attacker IP addresses and indicators of compromise have been published, and defenders are advised to hunt for compromise, restrict management network access, and rotate credentials.

fd247aa0bdf601de.title: AntiFox AI Pentest Tool Abused in AWS Credential Theft Attacks
summary: Arctic Wolf said the AI-powered penetration testing tool AntiFox was abused in attacks that stole AWS credentials and enabled lateral movement into internal networks.
Attackers installed the open-source tool on Alibaba Cloud to target web services and AWS environments.
After compromising IIS servers, they used w3wp.exe to create ASPX web shells and harvest configuration files and database connection details.
Using valid IAM users and EC2 roles, they called AWS APIs and retrieved production secrets from Secrets Manager.
According to BleepingComputer, some intrusions also led to S3 objects being read, copied, and deleted, while the initial credential access path remains unconfirmed.

3dfb6b9e4fd4af24.title: eBPF Rootkits: Why Underground Actors Are Taking Notice
summary: Flare researchers found eBPF rootkit code and build tutorials shared on underground forums and Pastebin posts.
Because eBPF programs run without loading a kernel module, they can evade routine lsmod checks while hiding processes and activating backdoors on packet triggers.
Samples inspired by BPFDoor and Symbiote are circulating alongside a widely reposted CVE-2017-16995 exploit, and the excerpt reports no confirmed victim impact.

105041a0037d06b2.title: The XG Files: Falcon C2 Flying Under The (Browser) Radar
summary: Unit 42 analyzed Falcon (aka XG or Xiang Ge), a C2 framework that runs malicious JavaScript inside victims' browsers.
Attackers injected malicious scripts into webmail portals and government web applications to steal passwords, session cookies, and communications.
Government entities in one Middle Eastern and four Southeast Asian countries were compromised from March to May 2026, and Falcon also delivered Antino, an implant that uses OneDrive as a C2 channel.

35d31223327b6bcc.title: Hackers Target Qlik Sense Servers With Reverse Shells, Stage ActiveMQ and Veeam Exploits
summary: In October 2026, attackers targeted Qlik Sense servers across several environments in an attempt to run PowerShell reverse shell commands. Targets included customers based in the EU.
Cynet said the activity partly overlaps with the 2023 CACTUS ransomware campaign, but the vulnerability used for initial access has not been identified.
Although the reverse shell was blocked, researchers found an exposed directory containing a Go backdoor, SSH persistence scripts, and ActiveMQ and Veeam exploit tools.

b106d2aaea7e2840.title: Raksul Online Printing Service Hit by Unauthorized Access, Print Data and Personal Information at Risk
summary: Online printing service Raksul was hit by a cyberattack that may have exposed personal information and print data submitted for printing.
Attackers obtained authentication credentials for the data intake processing system, leaving some stored data accessible from outside.
The company confirmed the unauthorized access on November 8, 2026, at around 0:20 a.m., invalidated the affected accounts and credentials, and gradually resumed services from November 9.
Potentially exposed information includes names, company names, addresses, phone numbers, and email addresses contained in submitted print data and invoices.
According to ITmedia, credit card and login information were not compromised, while the scope and period of the breach remain under investigation, and no secondary damage has been confirmed.

afcbe7dfc58c8030.title: Poland shuts down government services platform ePUAP following cyberattack
summary: Poland temporarily shut down the ePUAP government services platform after detecting and stopping a cyberattack.
The attack method and perpetrators have not been disclosed, and no unauthorized access or data theft has been confirmed.
Officials say the platform was disabled as a precaution without damage, and no restoration timeline has been given. Electronic mailboxes and the Trusted Profile identity system may also be affected.

20738d41c8d52c01.title: Britain, France set out first guidelines for commercial hacking firms
summary: Fourteen governments in the Pall Mall Process adopted their first guidelines for commercial cyber intrusion capability businesses.
The non-binding guidelines call on firms to vet customers, add technical safeguards against misuse, and monitor and report abuses, and to halt sales when serious misuse is a credible risk.
There are no penalties for non-compliance, so enforcement pressure is expected to come from governments that buy the tools and license their export.

0d15a59323a1d039.title: SAP November 2026 Update Patches Maximum-Severity Flaws Including ICM2SHELL and ProxyGate
summary: SAP released its November 2026 monthly security update, with reports putting the number of new and corrected security notes between 35 and 42 depending on the source.
Nine of the flaws are rated critical, and four carry a CVSS v3.1 base score of 10.0.
A memory corruption flaw in the WebSocket message handling of NetWeaver ICM and Web Dispatcher, dubbed ICM2SHELL by Onapsis, allows unauthenticated remote code execution.

A separate access control flaw in the Gateway prxyinfo component, named ProxyGate, can be exploited by forging requests from the internal network to achieve the same result, potentially leading to full SAP system takeover.

No public exploitation has been observed, but Onapsis provided a working exploit to SAP, and RedRays urges customers to update the kernel and all Web Dispatchers together, prioritizing the SAML2 flaw that has no workaround.

319897490b6a7d3a.title: Over 35,000 Grok-Built Apps Exposed Online, Some Leaking Confidential Data and Passwords
summary: Security firm Claroc found 35,578 of 37,571 Grok-built apps open to anyone without sign-in.
App addresses appear in passive DNS records that can be searched, and the default sharing setting was Anyone with the link.
Internal data from 30 organizations was exposed, including 24 staff apps, and SpaceXSI has removed those staff apps.

589a7e5416b703b4.title: We Built An Agent That Broke All of Our Security Rules. Here's What We Learned.
summary: Token built a browser agent called Rehearsal that runs inside user sessions and, by default, broke all of the company's own security rules for AI agents.
Applications see the user but cannot distinguish the agent, the delegation, or the task scope, and current web standards do not yet link these signals.
Token added action logging, reduced agent permissions, and step-up approval for sensitive actions, and advises security teams to inventory agents and require approval before irreversible actions.

ee1f2c14a9800c0f.title: Microsoft fixes audio issues caused by September security updates
summary: Microsoft confirmed that USB Audio Class 1.0 devices failed to start or produce sound on some systems after installing security updates released since September 2026.
Affected users saw 'This device cannot start (Code 10)' errors in Device Manager, and speakers failed when using 3D audio or 8-channel modes.
The issue is resolved in the November 10, 2026 Windows security update (KB5132061) and later, and users who cannot update immediately may restore audio by switching to 2-channel mode.

32f71639eeea9d88.title: ICS Patch Tuesday: Siemens Flags High-Severity Flaws, Node2Shell Exposure
summary: Siemens, Schneider Electric and other industrial technology vendors released new security advisories covering vulnerabilities that could expose affected systems to serious attacks.

Siemens published nine advisories covering 10 vulnerabilities, two of which describe the impact of Node2Shell. Exploitation attempts of Node2Shell have been seen, but no attacks specifically targeting Siemens products have been reported.
Patches are not yet available for several affected Siemens products and some versions will not be fixed, so customers are advised to apply the recommended mitigations.

10cdb9aca6bb26af.title: Cisco BroadWorks and Openwave Webtop Flaws Exploited in Attacks, Added to CISA KEV
summary: The US CISA has added Cisco BroadWorks flaw CVE-2026-20320 and Openwave Webtop Media Transcoder flaw CVE-2026-111793 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, citing active exploitation.
The BroadWorks flaw is an XXE issue in the OCI XML parser that lets unauthenticated attackers read server files and configuration data using crafted XML requests.
The Webtop flaw stems from missing file type enforcement, allowing authenticated users to convert and process documents.

According to BleepingComputer, a China-linked threat actor used a jailbroken DeepSeek Flash AI model to target a European telecom and stole system identity private keys and SSL certificate credentials.
The Hacker News reported that the attack methods and the attackers have not been confirmed, and federal agencies must apply patches by November 24, 2026.

b47301e78796ad8f.title: Yasukuni Shrine Hit by Unauthorized Access, About 14,500 Personal Records Leaked, Passwords May Be Identifiable
summary: Yasukuni Shrine announced that unauthorized access to its online sales site exposed personal information of about 14,500 members.
The leaked data includes names, email addresses, hashed passwords with their generation data, and account management information, and the passwords may be identifiable.

The site was taken offline after the intrusion was detected on October 28, and no reopening date has been set. No credit card data has been confirmed leaked, and users are urged to change reused passwords and beware of suspicious messages.

11c420ce18f6788a.title: Citrus Ransomware: VLESS for traffic, Sn00py for encryption, and LLMs lending a hand
summary: Kaspersky researchers analyzed the attack chain of Citrus Ransomware, a previously undocumented group.
The attackers entered through contractor credentials, used VLESS tunnels built with Xray for C2, exploited CVE-2026-54121 to escalate privileges, and relied on LLM-generated scripts.
After stealing data, they deployed a Sn00py-family ransomware via Group Policy that encrypts files with a .citrus extension. The scale of damage and recovery status are not stated in the article.

0bcd906116868337.title: Microsoft fixes Exchange sign-ins broken by Windows Server updates
summary: Microsoft has fixed Outlook sign-in and mail delivery problems on on-premises Exchange Server systems that appeared after the October 2026 Windows Server security updates.
The cause was a new default memory limit for Endpoint Mapper's Endpoint Lookup calls introduced in October, which affected OWA sign-ins and left outgoing mail stuck in the Outbox on some servers.
The November 2026 Patch Tuesday updates (KB5131080 and KB5131090) resolve the issue, and a temporary registry change is offered for administrators who cannot deploy them immediately.

4fcdc1b961fc2cce.title: Chipmaker Patch Tuesday: Over 200 Vulnerabilities Addressed by Intel, AMD
summary: Intel and AMD published more than 50 new security advisories covering over 200 vulnerabilities in their products.

Intel's 24 advisories cover just over 100 flaws, including critical authentication issues in TDX MigTD reference software that enable privilege escalation, one of which may allow remote code execution.

AMD released 29 bulletins and two security briefs, with some fixes not expected until 2027. Intel will not patch three BigDL privilege escalation bugs and advises users to stop using the discontinued product.

70ae8449d95c95b1.title: Yumirink Cuenote FC Mail Service Breach Exposes Tens of Millions of Email Addresses
summary: Yumirink disclosed unauthorized access to systems operating its Cuenote FC mail distribution service, leading to the leak of email addresses and other personal data.
Attackers exploited a library vulnerability to steal credentials of support and quality control staff, then deployed malware to extract data from databases and attempted to access other systems.
Reported leak figures vary by source. The company initially estimated about 9 million records from five systems.
The count later expanded to 49 or 50 systems, with ITmedia citing about 47.86 million records and INTERNET Watch citing up to about 51.62 million.

Client companies including Bandai Namco Entertainment, JR Tokai, JR West, JR Kyushu, Resona Bank, iStyle, and Mainichi Shimbun disclosed related email address leaks. Yumirink isolated affected servers, patched the vulnerability, and deleted compromised credentials, while reporting to the Personal Information Protection Commission and continuing an external investigation.

3c0f5b9f172be3c8.title: Chained Barracuda ESG Flaws Exploited in Attacks to Gain Root Access
summary: Two vulnerabilities in Barracuda Networks' Email Security Gateway (ESG) are being exploited in real attacks, and CISA added them to its KEV catalog on November 10.
An authentication bypass flaw (CVE-2026-116606) allows restoring a tampered backup, and a command injection flaw (CVE-2026-111560) enables commands to run with root privileges.
According to watchTowr's analysis, a hardcoded secret used for checksum calculation makes backup forgery possible.
Previdian observed 17 attack attempts from 15 IP addresses between November 9 and 11, and BleepingComputer reported that the attacks targeted a small number of companies.
Mandiant reported both flaws on October 15 and 22. Barracuda urges customers to apply patches immediately and restrict management interfaces to internal networks.

85e2147534a89027.title: Railway Breach Leads to Theft of Customer AI Keys and About $740,000 in Unauthorized Charges
summary: Railway, a platform-as-a-service provider, disclosed that customer-stored AI provider keys were stolen in an October breach, resulting in about $740,000 in unauthorized usage charges.

The attacker escaped a build container through an undisclosed vulnerability in build infrastructure to obtain internal credentials, then abused a misconfigured trust relationship to gain environment variable decryption access.
Up to about 100,000 workspaces, or no more than 1.85% of the total, may have been exposed, and the company said it removed the attacker and fixed the flaw on October 21.

According to BleepingComputer, the company covered the charges and reset connected tokens, while The Hacker News reported that tokens for 1,852 linked accounts were reset and no login traces to customer accounts were found.

37638c559a79a6e1.title: Apple Patches iMessage Group Chat and Bluetooth Pairing Flaws Across Platforms
summary: Apple released security updates on November 9, 2026, including iOS 27.2.1, iPadOS 27.2.1, and macOS Golden Gate 27.2.1.
A authorization flaw in the Messages app allowed unauthorized access, letting third parties join iMessage group chats and receive messages.
A related issue let newly added group members view earlier messages, and it has also been fixed.
Five of the flaws affect Bluetooth and AirPlay pairing, enabling bypass of pairing code attempt limits or pairing without user interaction.
Reported vulnerability counts vary by outlet, ranging from 8 to 10 fixes.

7c2ea1269082c3e8.title: Microsoft Researchers Show AI Agents Can Be Backdoored by Editing Fewer Than 10 Neurons
summary: Microsoft researchers showed that an AI model can be given a hidden backdoor by editing fewer than 10 rarely used neurons, without retraining the model.
When a trigger appears, the model outputs an attacker command that an agent using it would run with the agent's own permissions, and the test success rates reached 98.8% or higher on one model.

The attacker must be able to change model weights, and the researchers recommend comparing checkpoints with their original weights, limiting agent permissions, and requiring human approval for high-impact actions.

33c31993e5525cc8.title: Summary of the Convenience Store Certificate Issuance Outage Using My Number Cards
summary: On November 10, 2026, convenience store certificate issuance of family register documents was temporarily suspended in many municipalities for several hours.
The Japan Agency for Local Authority Information Systems (J-LIS) said issuance stopped at convenience store terminals for 408 municipalities, and the cause was a failed LGWAN connection router.
Unauthorized access appears unlikely and no personal data leak was confirmed, and services returned to normal after the router was replaced late that night.

b7b0bb11e19988dc.title: Yusaku Maezawa Considers Appeal in Meta Impersonation Ad Lawsuit After Tokyo District Court Dismisses Claim
summary: Japanese entrepreneur Yusaku Maezawa says he is considering an appeal after the Tokyo District Court dismissed his lawsuit against Meta over fake investment ads that used his name and photos without permission.

The court found the ads violated his right of publicity but ruled that Meta, as a platform operator, was not directly involved in the posts, rejecting his request for an injunction and 1 yen in damages.

The court also cited Meta's removal of most fake ads within two days, finding no need for an injunction. The National Police Agency reported that SNS-based investment fraud caused about 128.8 billion yen in damages in 2025.

e269babcfbf8b773.title: Attackers on the Same Wi-Fi Could Snoop on Traffic? Attack Bypasses "Client Isolation" in 2 Seconds, US University Researchers Show
summary: Researchers from the University of California, Riverside, disclosed AirSnitch, an attack that breaks "client isolation" and blocks devices on the same Wi-Fi network from communicating.
Attackers abuse the shared group temporal key, gateway bouncing, and port stealing on access points to intercept traffic and inject data.
Every home and enterprise router and university network tested was affected, and a man-in-the-middle position was set up in about 2 seconds on the Netgear R8000. The article does not mention patches.

2f9f04439f1b5fe7.title: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Misaddressed Mail to Residents, Sent to Wrong People
summary: The Tokyo Metropolitan Government disclosed that some notices sent by the Tokyo Metropolitan Housing Supply Corporation carried incorrect addresses.
On September 28, 2026, 1,997 letters addressed to residents' association heads were mailed, and 846 of them had wrong addresses.
Seventy-six letters were returned, while 770 reached other residents. The corporation explained the situation and apologized to the affected parties.

ebc427a97210ce6d.title: Edion may have also leaked some credit card numbers and security codes; malicious program found in payment processing and error logs
summary: Edion disclosed that a malicious program in its payment processing may have leaked up to 556 sets of credit card numbers and security codes during a follow-up investigation into unauthorized access to its e-commerce site.
The program ran on the PC payment input flow, and up to 5 card records temporarily stored in system logs during order errors may also have been exposed.
The company suspended its e-commerce site and apps on November 7, 2026, with no reopening date set, and is sending password change requests to affected users.

5029f0c239cb34c9.title: Multiple FortiOS Vulnerabilities - 3 Rated Critical
summary: On November 10, 2026, Fortinet published a security advisory for FortiOS disclosing eight vulnerabilities, three of which are rated Critical, the highest severity level.

CVE-2026-126259 is an authentication flaw in the redundancy feature that can let an unauthenticated attacker send crafted HA packets in FGSP or autoscale setups and execute commands with top-level administrator privileges.

CVE-2026-126254 is a integer truncation flaw in the BGP daemon that can let malicious attributes from a configured iBGP peer propagate to connected routers, while CVE-2026-126253 is an authentication bypass in the OSPF daemon that allows unauthenticated LSA transmission. Users are urged to update.

2ea644d8d33f8749.title: Two Chinese Nationals Arrested for Using Fake TikTok App to Remotely Control Phones and Make Unauthorized Payments
summary: On November 10, 2026, a joint investigation team from Fukuoka, Hyogo, and Hokkaido police arrested two Chinese nationals on suspicion of fraud.
The suspects allegedly used fake apps such as "TikTok18+" to remotely control victims' smartphones, obtain payment screen images and barcodes, and buy goods at stores.
About 1,600 consultations were reported nationwide as of late September, and the two men have been arrested three times since September 30. Police are investigating the wider group.

64f310e5b2006e0d.title: Weekly Report: Multiple Vulnerabilities in Cloud Software Group's XenServer
summary: JPCERT/CC has compiled 14 security-related items for November 1 to 7, 2026.
They include vulnerabilities in XenServer, Airbyte, Zyxel, and Barracuda products, with Airbyte and Zyxel GS1900 flaws exploited in attacks.
Most issues can be fixed by updating to patched versions, and Japan's National Cybersecurity Office (NCO) also issued a warning on unauthorized access to websites and mobile apps.

48bd8f09075f6b21.title: Similar Cyberattacks Likely to Continue as AI May Be Used for Target Research and Intrusions, National Cybersecurity Office Says
summary: The National Cybersecurity Office (NCO) of the Cabinet Secretariat published a document on information leaks caused by cyberattacks on October 26, 2026.
Attackers systematically scan public-facing Web systems in Japan for entry points, then quickly steal personal data from databases.
Leak incidents and large-scale cases of over one million records have sharply increased, and the NCO warns similar attacks will continue, possibly with AI assistance.

d0badc9a3737770a.title: Unauthorized Access at NTT Data Subcontractor Leads to Suspension of STdirectServices Bond Benefit Program
summary: A subcontractor of NTT Data suffered unauthorized access, forcing the suspension of STdirectServices, a service that delivers benefits to bond holders.
The attack method and scope of any data exposure are not confirmed beyond the headline.
The extent of damage and recovery status are unknown, and details should be checked in later notices.

93a0e7bc6afa16ac.title: Kyushu Electric Power Transmission and Distribution Suffers Unauthorized Access, Power Usage Data May Have Leaked
summary: Kyushu Electric Power Transmission and Distribution announced on November 5 that power usage information may have leaked after unauthorized access to its systems.
The company detected an unusual error on October 30, and an investigation confirmed unauthorized access, prompting an emergency shutdown of the affected system and a review of server logs.

About 4,139 customer records may be affected, and the company plans to notify those customers individually in mid-November. The electricity usage and billing inquiry service remains suspended, and restoration timing is under review.

ef0c0f442d6fa7c5.title: Dentsu Soken Finds Misconfiguration in FACERE, Confirms Unauthorized Third-Party Access
summary: Dentsu Soken disclosed a possible personal data leak affecting certain companies using its FACERE product.
An access permission misconfiguration left stored data viewable by third parties, and unauthorized access occurred on September 10.
The company reported to the affected firm, changed settings, and blocked the unauthorized route, finding no other misconfigurations as of November 3.

78738ef929af0e45.title: Unauthorized Access to ISM CloudOne
summary: Quality Soft said on October 20 that it temporarily suspended the ISM CloudOne service after detecting suspicious access to its second server.
Investigation confirmed that a third party exploited a server vulnerability to gain unauthorized access to specific customers.
No signs of mass database extraction or leakage of all customer data were found, and the service resumed on November 4 with plans to add WAF and server EDR/XDR.

913ee71dc5f22bba.title: Mobile Order Service PICKS Hit by Unauthorized Access, Personal Data of 8,312 People Leaked
summary: DIRIGIO disclosed that a third party gained unauthorized access to PICKS, its mobile order service, and took customer data outside the company.
The attacker reportedly entered the customer information system through the company's API, and details of the attack method have not been published.

Data on 9,992 orders and 8,312 customers, including names, email addresses, addresses, and order details, was leaked. The company suspended all PICKS services on October 27, began phased restoration on October 29, and is contacting affected customers and strengthening monitoring.

ada130eb24ec04ea.title: Visual Arts Reports Unauthorized Access, No Clear Traces Found on Devices That May Have Stored Credentials
summary: Visual Arts has issued its third update on a possible leak of internal and personal data from an unauthorized access incident first disclosed in June.
An outside party apparently stole credentials for the cloud storage used by its internal portal and took data, including master data for the game anemoi, out of the company.

A forensic investigation by an external firm from September to October found no clear signs of compromise on the relevant devices. Because some records were missing, the company did not rule out credential theft, and it continues measures such as 24-hour MDR monitoring.

95febf27aa6a28d2.title: Unauthorized Access to Tin Pan Alley Server Puts About 1.2 Million Member Records at Risk
summary: World Co., Ltd. disclosed that unauthorized access to a business server of its consolidated subsidiary Tin Pan Alley led to data theft on October 17.
The company detected suspicious activity on October 28, isolated the server, blocked the access route, and suspended some internal business systems.
Up to about 1.2 million member records, including names, addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth, genders, and email addresses, may have been exposed.
According to ITmedia, no payment information or facial data was confirmed as leaked.
The company has commissioned external experts to investigate and plans to send apology and caution notices to members by individual email.

e2d9ef29346d4124.title: Online Lottery Site Hanikuji Land Hit by Unauthorized Access, Third-Party Command Execution and Credential Misuse Confirmed
summary: Kohde Inc. disclosed unauthorized access to its online lottery site Hanikuji Land, where a third party manipulated some systems.
An investigation begun in September after a inquiry form malfunction found unauthorized command execution and misuse of credentials. The vulnerability used for entry has been patched.

Personal data of up to 7,622 customers, including names, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses and purchase history, may have been leaked. Investigation is ongoing and credentials have been rotated.

5d89546e0a8cb737.title: Amadeus Breach Exposes Customer Booking Data at Japan Airlines and Other Asian Carriers
summary: Japan Airlines and Japan Transocean Air said unauthorized access to their passenger service system provider Amadeus IT Group, S.A. left traces of customer booking records being viewed externally.
The cause is reported differently: BleepingComputer cited a vulnerability in the Amadeus booking display environment, while piyolog and The Record pointed to abuse of system account credentials.

According to ScanNet, about 92,000 booking records from August 10 to September 23, 2023 were accessed, with around 2,000 including passport numbers and contact details, while BleepingComputer reported activity through September 2026.

Card numbers and passwords were not compromised, and flight operations were not affected. Cathay Pacific reported a data breach affecting 53,000 records, and All Nippon Airways disclosed similar unauthorized access to its booking data.
Amadeus has completed security measures and no misuse has been confirmed so far, while the airlines are contacting affected customers directly and warning them about phishing.

87a6204206490ed6.title: Multiple Vulnerabilities Found in SS1, SS1 Cloud and ODM Product rocoeyes
summary: IPA and JPCERT/CC disclosed multiple vulnerabilities in the IT asset management tool SS1, SS1 Cloud, and its ODM product rocoeyes through JVN.
Insecure storage of sensitive information (CVE-2026-109582) and path traversal (CVE-2026-113437) could allow attackers to obtain sensitive data or delete arbitrary files.
The developer urges users to update to the latest versions. The article does not report the scale of impact or any active exploitation.

8ea2ba601da801cf.title: Only 22.4% of Organizations Give AI Agents Restricted Credentials, Shared Accounts and Hardcoding Also Found - Okta Survey
summary: Okta Japan announced the results of its Customer Identity Trends Report 2026 survey on November 5.

Only 22.4% of organizations developing AI features grant AI agents temporary, strictly limited credentials. Shared service accounts (17.4%), inherited user permissions (11.5%), and hardcoded credentials in code (6.4%) were also reported.

Only 20.3% of companies are delivering AI features on schedule, and 17.8% of developers cite legacy identity and authentication systems that cannot support AI agents as the cause of delays. In Japan, about 60% of companies that have not started AI development point to outdated identity infrastructure as the main reason.

64315118083288e3.title: Phishing Emails That Pass DMARC: DKIM Replay Attack Mechanism and Countermeasures Explained by TwoFive
summary: Japanese security firm TwoFive published a note explaining how DKIM replay attacks work and how to defend against them.
The attack alters headers not covered by the DKIM signature, such as Content-Type, so phishing content appears in legitimately signed emails.
Recommended defenses include adding Content-Type and MIME-Version to the h= tag, avoiding the l= tag, and setting an expiration with x=.

4139bff49393447b.title: IPA Strengthens Information Security Consultation Desk Following Series of Unauthorized Access Incidents
summary: Information-technology Promotion Agency, Japan (IPA) announced on November 2 that it will strengthen its Information Security Consultation Desk after a series of unauthorized access incidents led to personal data leaks.
The desk will advise general users on handling viruses and unauthorized access, responding to phishing scams, and reducing secondary harm after information leaks.

IPA will also work more closely with consumer affairs centers and other government consultation services to respond appropriately to victims, accepting calls and emails from individual users nationwide.

ed97c37855559d12.title: IT Staff in Seven Kyushu Prefectures Rate Own Security 12 Points Lower Than Before, HENNGE and Nishinippon Shimbun Survey
summary: HENNGE and Nishinippon Shimbun released results of a security survey of 300 IT staff across seven Kyushu prefectures, conducted in August 2026.
Only 55.0% of respondents rated their company's security measures as sufficient, down 12 points from the 2024 survey.
37.7% of companies have no designated contact for incidents, and only 22.0% have a dedicated security staff member.

5455e363be2c1a27.title: Detecting sleeper agents hiding in AI model neurons
summary: Microsoft Research published a study showing that editing fewer than 10 neurons can turn an agent model into a sleeper agent.
The tampered model passes all evaluations but runs an attacker's command when a specific trigger string appears in its context.
No real-world abuse has been observed, and weight audits and detection by frontier AI agents are proposed as countermeasures.

a3da70545004c98d.title: Teket e-ticketing service member data breach and service suspension at NTT Docomo affiliate
summary: Teket, an e-ticketing service run by an NTT Docomo affiliate, suffered unauthorized access that exposed member customer data.

The operator suspended the service on November 5 after detecting possible external unauthorized access to its servers, and confirmed on November 6 that intruders had breached the member information system.
All members' names and email addresses were exposed, and buyers' birth dates, addresses, phone numbers and ticket issuance codes were also included.
According to ITmedia, the company announced the breach on November 8. Non-member buyers may also be affected, and the scope of the data breach is still under investigation.
No secondary damage has been confirmed, and no date for resuming service has been set. Organizers are telling buyers to present their purchase confirmation email at entry.

67c5a4fb4eade07d.title: US Army member arrested in UK over allegations of spying for Russia
summary: London's Metropolitan Police announced the arrest of a 41-year-old U.S. Army soldier on suspicion of spying for Russia.
The arrest was made under the spying provisions of the UK National Security Act, with counterterrorism police working alongside the FBI and the U.S. military.
The soldier is in custody in London, searches are underway at two sites in Gloucestershire, and the Kremlin has not yet responded.

6fd7068a18961649.title: Nitori Holdings Breach Exposes Up to 37.62 Million Customer Records
summary: Nitori Holdings said unauthorized access by a third party may have led to the leak of up to 37.62 million customer personal records.
The attacker appears to have accessed its systems from mid to late October. The company confirmed the unauthorized access on November 6 and blocked it, and log analysis revealed the activity.
Exposed data may include member numbers, names, email addresses, postal addresses, phone numbers, birth dates and order information. The company said passwords and card data were not affected.

The company has reported the incident to the Personal Information Protection Commission and the police, and is investigating the cause with outside experts. It has also warned customers to watch for phishing and fraud.

cf4698872cf5b334.title: Microsoft releases Windows 10 KB5131096 extended security update
summary: Microsoft released the Windows 10 KB5131096 extended security update, which includes the November 2026 Patch Tuesday security fixes and several bug fixes.
The Patch Tuesday release addressed 1,235 vulnerabilities across Microsoft products, including one Outlook zero-day flaw that is being actively exploited.

Users enrolled in the ESU program and Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC users can install the update through Windows Update. Scripts with invalid UTF-8 encoding may fail the stricter PowerShell signature checks and need to be re-signed.

fa27f872aedc2c3d.title: Supply Chain Attack Abusing Qubole Trusted AWS Access Exposes Data Across Multiple Customer Cloud Environments
summary: Threat actors used stolen IAM credentials from the AWS account of big data platform Qubole to gain unauthorized access to the AWS environments of multiple customers.
Attackers assumed cross-account IAM roles that customers had configured to trust Qubole, then harvested keys and passwords from services such as Secrets Manager and downloaded data from S3 buckets.
Dozens of companies were reportedly affected between October 14 and 26, 2026, while SecurityWeek reported that more than ten organizations were hit.
Sentra confirmed that millions of files were exfiltrated from a single customer, and analysis found that dormant roles still trusted the Qubole account.
Qubole has not issued an official statement, so administrators should review CloudTrail logs from October 1 onward and rotate credentials.

e78b02c7bce6ba90.title: SGLang RCE Exploit Breaches NEAR AI, Steals Data From 18 Agents and About 100 Users
summary: An attacker exploited a remote code execution flaw in the open-source SGLang inference engine to run code on one NEAR AI inference server.
The attacker could view requests in confidential mode and reached a deprecated Private Chat system, downloading account details for about 100 users.
The company said chat history and logs were stolen from 18 agents on an older deployment, and it has revoked credentials, deployed a fix, and completed a forensic review.

2087d48a14d646c6.title: Microsoft Patch Tuesday November 2027 , (Tue, Nov 10th)
summary: Microsoft released its November 2027 Patch Tuesday fixes covering multiple products, including .NET, ASP.NET Core, Azure, and Chromium.
Many entries are denial of service, elevation of privilege, information disclosure, or security feature bypass flaws, mostly rated Important.
Only part of the advisory was available, so the total number of flaws and any active exploitation are unconfirmed; administrators should apply the relevant patches.

500712d16369aa3d.title: Windows 11 KB5132061 & KB5131087 cumulative updates released
summary: Microsoft released the Windows 11 cumulative updates KB5132061 and KB5131087 as part of its November 2026 Patch Tuesday.
The updates patch hundreds of vulnerabilities for versions 26H2, 25H2, 24H2, and 23H2 and are mandatory for those systems.
They also add File Explorer context menu customization, a modernized AutoPlay dialog, and Magnifier improvements, and can be installed through Windows Update.

7452f65a8ab245df.title: Three China-linked espionage campaigns tied to Sparrow malware ecosystem attributed to CopperDragon
summary: Check Point Research reported three China-linked espionage clusters, SilentDelivery, OceanGate and DarkWire, tied to the Sparrow malware ecosystem after a year-long investigation.
SilentDelivery injects obfuscated JavaScript into legitimate websites and displays fake Chrome certificate warnings to trick visitors into installing the SquadC backdoor.
OceanGate infiltrates Linux servers and then spreads laterally to Windows systems.
Observed techniques include spearphishing attachments, DLL side-loading, RDP abuse, OS credential dumping and keylogging.
Victims span government and telecom organizations in Europe, Asia and Latin America, and the activity is attributed to CopperDragon, though the victim count and response details were not disclosed.

7e2a58ecf05bbecf.title: AhsayCBS Vulnerabilities Chained to Deploy Python Backdoor and Crypto Miners
summary: In an attack observed by Huntress in October 2026, threat actors chained two AhsayCBS vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-105133, CVE-2026-105134) to bypass authentication and execute arbitrary commands.
The attackers deployed multiple JSP web shells, an in-memory loader hidden in an image, a signed API web shell, two XMRig cryptocurrency miners, and a Python implant running in memory.
The Python backdoor checks MachineGuid values to avoid running in sandboxes and analysis environments.

According to The Hacker News, signs of credential theft were found on a Veeam server, but the scale of stolen credentials remains unknown, and Huntress said it could not confirm actual data exfiltration.
Affected servers were compromised between October 8 and 11, 2026, before patching, and fixes were released in mid-October, so administrators should apply patches and check for signs of compromise.

b97c6fdb21585b03.title: Binance warns of iOS flaw that could leak crypto wallet secrets
summary: Binance warned that a flaw called worse_query in iOS 26.7.1, 27.0.1, and 27.2 could let malicious apps read files from other apps, including seed phrases and private keys.
A public proof-of-concept tool, WQ Files, uses the sandbox escape to browse and modify other apps' data without a jailbreak, and it works on the affected versions.
No crypto losses have been confirmed, and Apple released fixes in iOS 27.2.1 on November 9. Binance urges users to update and remove untrusted apps.

d36843326ee5effa.title: Blind Eagle Uses Fake Court Notices to Deliver Remote Access Trojan Across Latin America
summary: Threat actor Blind Eagle (APT-C-36) is running a new campaign across Latin America, using phishing emails disguised as court and prosecutor notices to deliver a remote access trojan.
The lures use a fake Colombian prosecutor page and HTML smuggling to evade email controls, then bypass AMSI and ETW and run an AsyncRAT-derived RAT in memory.
Researchers found no evidence of successful compromises, and judicial, administrative, and educational organizations are the main targets.

a10f6a4f90d78dc2.title: Cybercriminals are increasingly infecting regular people with spyware
summary: Threat hunting firm iVerify reported that spyware infections are rising sharply among regular consumer devices.
Its free checks found 1.07 infections per 1,000 consumer scans, and about 75% of detections involved the leaked DarkSword or Coruna iOS exploit kits.
Most infections were used for credential and cryptocurrency theft, and the rate for enterprise devices was lower.

0f4247cc44e95adf.title: Hankyu Hanshin Department Stores booking site breach exposes about 1.26 million H2O ID member records
summary: Hankyu Hanshin Department Stores said unauthorized access hit its booking site and online shopping site, exposing customer management systems to a third party.
Parent company H2O Retailing said the intrusion through the booking site was confirmed on October 16, 2026, and the online shopping and order sites were also compromised on October 17.

Security NEXT reported that data on about 1.26 million H2O ID members and 6,243 booking form submissions was leaked, while ScanNetSecurity said the exposed data included names, contact details, addresses and dates of birth.

The company cut external communications, shut down the affected site systems and reported the incident to authorities. No secondary damage has been confirmed so far, and members were warned to beware of impersonation contacts.

0d3cc2c4a4df8a55.title: Beyond the clipboard: The evolving tradecraft of ClickFix
summary: Huntress has outlined recent ClickFix trends. Attackers lure victims through malvertising, typosquatted domains, SEO poisoning, and compromised websites that show fake Cloudflare verification pages.

The PowerShell commands users paste display fake verification messages while downloading and running payloads. Some campaigns deliver Node.js-based RATs, steganographic payloads hidden in PNG files, or browser-cache-seeded delivery chains.
Some incidents involved lateral movement via loaders and RATs, reaching domain controllers. Security teams should stay alert to this technique, which continues to evolve.

8d75e33cee620271.title: Hana Kyupitto Management System Breach Exposes Up to 4.24 Million Member Records
summary: Hana Kyupitto, a flower delivery and e-commerce operator, said a third party gained unauthorized access to its management system and exposed member data.
The intrusion occurred between October 14 and 15, 2026, and one report said the leak was confirmed on October 19.
Exposed data includes login IDs, hashed passwords, and PC and mobile email addresses, affecting up to 4,238,242 records; another outlet reported about 4.24 million.
The company blocked the attack path and reported the incident to the Personal Information Protection Commission. No misuse of the leaked data has been confirmed so far.
The company says no card numbers or personal identifiers were exposed, and users are advised to change passwords and watch for phishing emails.

4d9c5d5fe01dcd92.title: OpenSSH SSHole Authentication Bypass Flaw (CVE-2026-123158) Exploited in Attacks
summary: OpenSSH disclosed authentication bypass flaw CVE-2026-123158 (SSHole) on November 5, 2026, affecting sshd on Linux systems that use musl libc without PAM, and released fixed version 10.6p2.
Accounts locked with a '*' password hash can be logged into with passwords 257 to 1024 bytes long, because musl crypt() returns '*' on failure.
SANS ISC honeypots recorded 713 exploitation attempts on November 6, and some attempts ran commands after login to download external bot malware.

According to GreyNoise, the first successful exploitation was confirmed on November 7, with root access gained and TAC Agent malware installed. WatchTowr and Previdian reported that botnet and cryptocurrency mining operators are using the flaw.

CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on November 9 and ordered federal agencies to patch by November 12. Administrators should update to OpenSSH 10.6p2 or set PasswordAuthentication no, and review login logs.

d6ed44c0e94cda7f.title: Binance Warns of iOS Sandbox Escape That Could Expose Crypto Wallet Keys, No Fix Confirmed
summary: Binance warned that a sandbox escape allowing apps to read other apps' files on iOS 26 and 27 was published on GitHub.
The researcher forcequit released worse_query code that can reach app data containers, and apps such as WQ Files have been built on it.
No attacks or thefts have been reported, and Apple has not confirmed a fix for the flaw.

bcceeccd841dff7d.title: Sharefull Part-Time Job App Hit by Unauthorized Access, Up to 7.5 Million Records Possibly Leaked
summary: Sharefull Inc. said on November 9 that unauthorized access to the internal management system of its part-time job app Sharefull may have exposed personal data of users.
The intrusion occurred on the night of November 4, 2026, and was detected the next morning, after which the company blocked access and began an investigation.

Up to about 7.5 million records may have been exposed, including bank account details used for salary deposits, addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth, emergency contacts, and residency status information. Account PINs were not included.

Corporate information on about 7,500 employers may also have been leaked. The company has reported the incident to the police and the Personal Information Protection Commission and says there is no sign of further leakage.

13b8a1dc264a9a71.title: Iran-Linked Hackers Blamed for Remote Sabotage of French Supermarket Refrigeration Systems
summary: French authorities have blamed Shahid Kaveh, a cyber unit linked to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), for remote sabotage of refrigeration systems at about 700 French supermarkets on October 11 and 12.
The attackers took over web interfaces of Danfoss and Dixell controllers, switched defrost settings to high temperatures, and pushed equipment to 50 degrees Celsius for about six hours.
The attack caused mass food spoilage and at least 15 fires, with losses estimated in the tens of millions of euros; Persian-language artifacts and Iranian IP addresses were reportedly found.
Paris prosecutors sought international arrest warrants, the Foreign Ministry summoned Iran's ambassador, and CERT-FR advised operators to disconnect exposed devices from the internet.
According to Unit 42, the initial access vector remains unknown, and a pro-Russian group's Telegram claim of responsibility has not been verified.

6221d447c4ccb7c8.title: Cyberattacks Surge, "Humans Can't Keep Up": SoftBank CEO Miyakawa Admits Exhaustion Over Endless Patching
summary: SoftBank subsidiary IDC Frontier was breached on October 7 through a vulnerability in open-source software used by its IDCFCloud authentication system, causing some servers used by 495 companies and municipalities to be stopped and encrypted.

The company said it had tested and patched its in-house applications but had not assessed the attacked OSS, and it has expanded emergency checks across group companies to include open-source components.
Reconnaissance activity has risen from about 300 million a month in 2025 to 600 to 700 million recently, and new AI models keep revealing new vulnerabilities, increasing the patching burden.

095422e4cd70c40e.title: IT threat evolution in Q3 2026. Non-mobile statistics
summary: Kaspersky published its non-mobile IT threat statistics for Q3 2026. Its products blocked more than 311 million attacks launched from online resources.
New ransomware variants reached 4,470, more than 1.5 times last quarter. Qilin ranked first with 15.39% of published victims on leak sites.
More than 81,000 users faced ransomware attacks and over 217,000 users were targeted by miners. The report also covers exploitation of several CVEs, including CVE-2026-0257.

b19eed77725fe98c.title: IT threat evolution in Q3 2026. Mobile statistics
summary: Kaspersky published mobile threat statistics for Q3 2026, showing that attacks involving malware and adware declined from the previous quarter.
Researchers reported an AI-assisted fake app targeting Brazil, a subscription-fraud Trojan, and iOS spyware delivered through the DarkSword exploit kit.
Blocked mobile attacks totaled about 1.66 million, and banking Trojans made up 31.63% of malicious apps, the largest share.

7846742f81b98ea0.title: Doutor Coffee Online Shop Breached - Possible Member Data Leak
summary: Doutor Coffee said unauthorized access to its online shop may have exposed customers' personal information.
A third party accessed the site's admin panel from October 24 to 25, 2026, and viewed data of members who registered by October 25.

Up to 24,762 member records and 9 delivery records may be affected. The site was suspended, access controls were tightened, and the incident was reported to police and the Personal Information Protection Commission.

d295cf3708940b1d.title: Whitepaper Released: How to Build an Organization That Does Not Give In to Ransomware Extortion
summary: LAC has released a whitepaper on preparing organizations to withstand extortion tactics used in ransomware attacks.
The paper stresses that having backups is not enough, recommending a three-tier backup strategy and regular recovery drills.
It also advises setting up disclosure reporting, a single response contact and decision-making roles, and ransom payment criteria in advance.

52314d42b172fd60.title: Sapporo City Suspends Sapporo Station Bus Navi After Unauthorized Access Distributes False Service Information
summary: The Sapporo City Transportation Bureau suspended parts of its official website and the Sapporo Station Bus Navi service on November 9 after unauthorized access, until safety can be confirmed.
Between about 6:35 and 12:10 on November 9, the service's distribution system was accessed externally and false bus operation information was delivered.
Emergency information during the suspension will be shared via station digital signboards and official city social media, and no personal data leak has been confirmed so far.

3f8c2038147a659d.title: Real-World Harm From Cyberattacks on Hospitals: Patient Mortality Up 30%, Breast Cancer Patient's Topless Images Leaked and Therapy Records Used for Extortion Linked to a Suicide
summary: Researchers from the University of California San Diego and other institutions systematically studied patient harm caused by cyberattacks on hospitals, publishing the findings in the Journal of Medical Internet Research.

Analyzing 59 academic papers and Reddit accounts, the team found that system outages delayed diagnosis and treatment, putting critically ill patients at risk and worsening cancer and diabetes patients who lost access to care.

One study found in-hospital mortality rose 34 to 38 percent at attacked hospitals, and reports describe a breast cancer patient's medical images leaked on the dark web and therapy records used to extort a patient who later died by suicide.

da895a04be486194.title: Access Key Hardcoded, Test Image Published Online by Contractor; Rafuru Survey Leaks Data of About 24,000 People
summary: Rafuru disclosed that the legacy system of its organizational improvement tool Rafuru Survey was accessed without authorization from July to October, exposing personal data such as names of 24,232 employees at 182 client companies.
The access key was reportedly hardcoded in the legacy program, and a contractor developer published a test environment image containing it online in 2019, which likely exposed the key.

The company discovered the intrusion in log reviews on October 27 and revoked the key. The current system no longer hardcodes keys and uses short-lived credentials, and an external investigation is underway.

cffa60042de555b4.title: Multiple Vulnerabilities Found in Roundcube - Updating Strongly Recommended
summary: Multiple vulnerabilities were disclosed in the Roundcube Webmail email software, and the developers released fixed versions 1.7.6 and 1.6.21.
The fixes cover an open redirect in IMAP error recovery during attachment retrieval, IMAP command injection when message caching is enabled, and bypasses of CSS proxy and SSRF protections.
Issues include script injection via Sieve and destructive actions in ManageSieve triggered by GET requests from external sites, with 17 fixes in total and no CVE numbers specified.

5dba6e70c0942a63.title: Plex2Shell Exploit Chain Targets Plex Media Servers, Including QNAP NAS Devices
summary: Attackers are actively exploiting a chain of four Plex Media Server vulnerabilities, dubbed Plex2Shell, shortly after public proof-of-concept code was released.
The flaws combine SSRF, admin token theft, and file path manipulation to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution with Plex service privileges.
Victims were infected with a cryptocurrency miner and a Linux proxy backdoor named myawesomeproxy, while QNAP warned that multiple NAS devices running Plex had been compromised.
CISA added the flaws to its KEV catalog and ordered federal agencies to patch some by October 23 and the rest by November 3.
Updating alone does not remove existing malicious payloads, so affected systems need a clean OS reinstall and credential resets, and Plex fixed the issue in version 1.43.3.10861.

f878554691d74301.title: Vanderbilt University Claims Ransomware Attack by BYOD Group
summary: Vanderbilt University announced Monday morning that it is responding to a cyberattack and warned that campus devices and systems used by students and staff may be affected.
The new ransomware group BYOD listed the university on its data leak site and claimed it encrypted databases and stole personal information of students and staff.
The university said its IT team is investigating and containing the incident, and asked students and staff to shut down devices and disconnect from campus WiFi.
The university has not yet confirmed the nature of the attack or whether data was stolen, and the scale of the damage and recovery status remain unknown.

5e15147c5cdf79de.title: Trust in Security Measures Outweighs Brand Recognition in Personal Data Decisions, 26.2-Point Gap
summary: Impact Holdings' subsidiary Impact Field surveyed 366 valid respondents registered with its MediF job site on personal data management and security awareness.
Forty-two point six percent of respondents said security measures and trust signals such as Privacy Mark matter most when entrusting data to a company, while brand reputation scored 16.4 percent.
Respondents most wanted guidance on secure password management and phishing email recognition (65.5 percent) and concrete response steps after a data leak (64.3 percent).

43710029754b1ba5.title: Third Party Breaches Eplus Festival App Through Brute-Force Attack on Admin Screen - Unauthorized Access Exposes Customer Data
summary: Eplus disclosed that unauthorized access to the admin system of its festival app exposed personal data of 3,571 customers.
A third party gained entry by brute-forcing the admin panel, and the company attributed the breach mainly to insufficient measures to prevent intrusion.
The company deleted the stored data, restricted external access, and notified affected customers by email, while rolling out multi-factor authentication and early attack detection.

4b6175072337741f.title: SMBC Consumer Finance Guarantee System Breached, Personal Data of Up to 320,118 Customers Sent Outside
summary: SMBC Consumer Finance said it detected unauthorized access to a guarantee business system on November 2 and blocked access the same day, announcing the incident on November 5.
Investigation confirmed that data was transferred out of the system, and the intrusion route and cause are still under investigation.
Up to 320,118 customers may be affected, with names, addresses, phone numbers, driver's license numbers, annual income, and guarantee contract details reportedly exposed.
According to INTERNET Watch, annual income and guarantee amounts were also included, while ITmedia reported that identity document images were not.
The company is notifying affected customers individually, warning them about suspicious emails, SMS, and calls, and has suspended the guarantee system while assessing the damage.

d677e77c07decb28.title: Tokio Marine Direct Insurance Discloses Unauthorized Access to Customer My Page Service
summary: Tokio Marine Direct Insurance detected suspicious access to its customer My Page service on November 4 and blocked the related IP addresses.
An investigation confirmed unauthorized third-party access, leading to the leak of customer personal data such as names, addresses, phone numbers, and policy details.
The company is identifying 74 affected customers and will notify them individually, while web procedures for its auto insurance services remain suspended.

a9327c4e407bea01.title: NTT Docomo Online Shop and My docomo Unauthorized Access Exposes Up to 300,000 Customer Records
summary: NTT Docomo said unauthorized access to its Docomo Online Shop and My docomo was detected on November 4, and both services were suspended from November 5.
The attacker used a d account as an entry point and abused linked internal systems to automatically search and extract customer data, and two-factor authentication was reportedly not bypassed.

Up to about 300,000 customer records were exposed, including names, dates of birth, addresses, phone numbers and contract details, and ITmedia reported that identity document numbers were also included.

According to Impress Watch, 294,839 lines were affected, comprising 204,157 individuals and 90,682 corporate accounts. The company said it is not a system vulnerability and will notify affected customers by SMS while considering condolence payments.
No restart date has been set, and the intrusion path and final scope of the breach remain under investigation.

4a07e23803c76076.title: Unauthorized Access to SHOGUN BURGER Official App Leads to Leak of Some Customers' Personal Information
summary: Ganesha Inc. announced on October 30, 2026 that a third party had gained unauthorized access to the system behind its SHOGUN BURGER official app.
Names, email addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth, genders, and order details of some customers may have been leaked.
The mobile order service is suspended while operator DIRIGIO runs a full system security diagnosis and investigates the cause, and it will resume only after safety is confirmed.

02190852f8ce8173.title: Vook Discloses Possible Customer Data Leak After Unauthorized Access via Data Analytics Tool Flaw
summary: Vook Inc. disclosed that personal data may have been partially leaked after a third party exploited a vulnerability in a data analytics tool used for internal operations.
The attacker reportedly used the tool to access the company's database and retrieve information. Vook found a suspicious account in the tool during an internal check on October 14.
All member login credentials were invalidated on October 22, and use of the tool has been suspended. Vook is identifying the scope of the leak and will contact affected individuals directly.

4d1eb05df1a68483.title: Personal Data of Paid and Free Members of Ryori Oukoku Web Magazine Leaked
summary: JFLA Holdings disclosed unauthorized access to its Ryori Oukoku food media site.
An external investigation found server data could be retrieved from outside, and the access route used has been closed.
About 8,000 member records were leaked, including names, company names, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, and hashed passwords, and affected customers will be notified.

e88e5875fe68f902.title: Unauthorized Access to Tōshi no Concierge Investment Service
summary: MONO Investment Co. reported on October 29, 2026 that unauthorized access to its Tōshi no Concierge service occurred on October 27, 2026.
The company confirmed the same day that part of the customer information registered with the service had been leaked.
The company has blocked the access and is investigating the cause and scope of impact, and will notify affected customers individually with apologies and details of the leaked data.

90405b5226df7007.title: KDDI Exposes Sole Proprietor Merchant Data on au PAY Store Locator Site
summary: KDDI said some merchant information may have been published on its au PAY store locator site without the merchants' knowledge.
Some sole proprietors who joined through comprehensive agent merchants had store names that appear to be individuals' names listed on the site.
ScanNetSecurity reported up to 4,417 entries were affected, while ITmedia reported that business names, contact details, and locations of up to 458,508 merchants were exposed.

The site has been under review since late August and has no set date for resuming service, and the issue was first flagged by an outside party in late August but was not announced until about two months later. Concerns have been raised that the exposure may violate the Personal Information Protection Act.

1c80fdb9aa407f18.title: Kurogane Kasei Hit by Ransomware Attack, Follow-up One Year After Investigation Results
summary: Kurogane Kasei disclosed that its systems were hit by a ransomware attack after employees lost access to the internal network on October 16, 2025.
An external investigation found traces of unauthorized access from overseas, and some personal data of business partners, employees and job applicants was leaked or may have been leaked.
In a follow-up announcement on October 28, the company said it reset devices and servers, changed all credentials, and introduced multi-factor authentication and MDR monitoring.

e0fae359f236c742.title: Improper Privilege Assignment Vulnerability in Hinemos
summary: IPA and JPCERT/CC disclosed an improper privilege assignment vulnerability in Hinemos through JVN on November 4.
A flaw in the password change API (CVE-2026-109849) lets an attacker holding certain privileges that can be granted to general users change administrator passwords.

Affected versions include 7.2.0, 7.1.0 to 7.1.2, and 7.0.0 to 7.0.4, and older versions may also be affected. Paid users should apply the patch, OSS users should update with the latest installer, and users of end-of-support versions should apply the workaround.

4f67d3e4af154b56.title: Vulnerability Allows Arbitrary Code Execution in Airbyte
summary: IPA and JPCERT/CC published a vulnerability in Airbyte that allows arbitrary code execution on November 4.
Improper class loading can cause unexpected components to be loaded, potentially letting code run as the Airbyte user in the Connector Builder or ManifestServer container.
Versions 1.7.0 through 2.1.0 are affected, and JVN urges users to update to the latest version based on information from the developer.

b7977fc8b897a6d5.title: Multiple Akeeba Products Affected by CSRF Vulnerability
summary: IPA and JPCERT/CC published a cross-site request forgery vulnerability affecting multiple Akeeba products on November 4 via JVN.
Some operations lack proper CSRF protection, so a logged-in user who visits a malicious page may be forced to perform unintended actions.
Earlier versions of Akeeba Backup, Akeeba Solo, and Admin Tools are affected, and users are advised to update to the latest versions provided by the developer.

e0a1a59f4528842b.title: Health Ministry Does Not Require System Vendors to Report Medical Data Leaks, Does Not Track Security Disclosure Non-Compliance Counts
summary: On October 20, the National Federation of Dentists and Doctors Organizations published details of a press conference with Health Minister Kenichiro Ueno.
Medley's obstetric clinic system @link suffered unauthorized access, possibly exposing patient personal data at up to 787 medical institutions.
The ministry acknowledged that medical institutions must report leaks but system vendors are not required to, and did not disclose Medley's non-compliance count on the security disclosure form.

ee4123ce7e1b69fb.title: SEGA newsletter data breach exposes 2.2 million email addresses
summary: SEGA disclosed that a breach at its newsletter provider ARARA exposed email addresses of 2.2 million subscribers.
The breach hit ARARA's email distribution service, exposing about 77 million addresses from nearly 380 corporate clients. A web server vulnerability is among the suspected causes.

Names, birth dates, card details, and passwords were reportedly not included, and SEGA has no confirmed misuse. MOS Burger and other firms were also affected, and SEGA is still investigating with ARARA.

90a9c72c829b1eb6.title: York University breach exposed personal information dating to 2007
summary: York University in Toronto, Canada, confirmed that a threat actor breached its systems and accessed personal information submitted through online forms.
The unauthorized access was discovered on October 25, 2026, and affected forms on 14 university websites that collected data from 2007 to 2026.

Exposed data includes contact details, dates of birth, York ID numbers, and government ID information, but the number of affected individuals has not been disclosed. Those with government ID or financial data exposed will be notified and offered two years of credit monitoring.

53214d4dae39be2f.title: Japan Approves Cybersecurity Emergency Package With 10 Billion Yen in Reserve Funds
summary: The Japanese government approved an emergency cybersecurity package on November 6 after a series of large-scale data breaches, according to reports.
The package has four pillars: prevention, intelligence gathering and analysis, response, and victim support, backed by a 10 billion yen reserve fund approved by the Cabinet.
Many recent information leaks stemmed from basic security failures, including unpatched known vulnerabilities, website misconfigurations, and weak security in development stages.

The plan includes an elite Top Gun team using AI to find vulnerabilities, expanded active cyber defense, and simulated attacks to test system weaknesses. Reports differ on the timing, with the team expected in November or by late November.

SecurityWeek reported that dozens of companies and government agencies suffered unauthorized access and customer data theft, and the government will set up public-private information sharing and emergency support for affected firms.

ada4744efde51659.title: EU Cyber Incident Information Sharing Gaps Exposed by Collins Aerospace Ransomware Attack
summary: The EU has begun initial operation of the Single Reporting Platform (SRP) under the Cyber Resilience Act (CRA), though reports differ on whether the start was in September 2026 or September 2025.

The European Court of Auditors said in a September 22 report that the EU's cyber incident detection and response system works only partially, due to insufficient information sharing and delayed implementation.
A ransomware attack on Collins Aerospace in September 2025 disrupted airports in several countries but was not reported as a large-scale incident at the EU level.
The sources provide no specific details on attack techniques or the scale of damage, and no response measures have been confirmed.

410c80268f9ec73e.title: Amplifon Data Breach Exposes Personal and Medical Data of Over 1.3 Million US Customers
summary: Italian hearing aid company Amplifon disclosed a cyberattack that exposed data of its US customers.
According to The Record, an attacker accessed company files from January 18 to February 8, stealing names, driver's license numbers, and health insurance and financial information.
No attack group has claimed responsibility so far.

According to SecurityWeek, the attacker copied files from some systems, exposing names, contact details, license numbers, and medical and insurance information of over 1.3 million people in the US, with some records including Social Security numbers and financial data.
Texas and Vermont authorities received reports of 85,804 and 1,027 affected individuals, respectively, while law firms claimed a total of 1,332,826, a figure the company has not confirmed.

75d9e478caa285f6.title: FORGE Lab uses agentic tools to identify memory safety issues in Rust
summary: Microsoft FORGE Lab found several memory safety issues in Rust's standard library (std and core) that can trigger undefined behavior even in purely safe code.
The root cause is unsafe code trusting user-provided implementations, panic behavior, and operating system state, and the research used the AI vulnerability scanner Hyenas.
Bugs such as a panic safety issue in MapWindows::clone and a non-UTF-8 result from str::replace were reported to the Rust issue tracker, and some remain open.

eebf8b3501db0935.title: Attackers Searching for SAP Netweaver Webshells, (Mon, Nov 9th)
summary: SANS ISC honeypot data shows a new request targeting /irj/servlet_jsp/irj/root/ant.jsp on SAP NetWeaver systems.
Attackers are exploiting CVE-2025-31324 (CVSS 10.0), which allows file uploads without authentication, to plant webshells, usually under /irj/servlet_jsp/irj/root/.
One IP address, 82.26.72.21, is probing many upload paths, including ones unrelated to SAP. The article does not report confirmed victims or further response guidance.

8ba505798f5651ff.title: Data-Wiping Attack on Russian Hosting Provider Beget Forces Cloud Infrastructure Rebuild
summary: Russian domain registration and hosting provider Beget suffered a cyberattack on the night of November 1, 2026, which wiped data across its cloud infrastructure.

Attackers gained unauthorized access to the infrastructure management system and executed a data-wiping script and malware. The company isolated all servers from the network immediately after detection.
According to The Record, hundreds of websites went offline and all binary backups of virtual servers were lost. Around 1,000 servers must be inspected individually, delaying recovery.

According to BleepingComputer, only 60% of shared hosting and 40% of dedicated servers had been restored at the time of disclosure. VPS binary backups were completely lost, and file backups can be restored only for some users.
Some sites have been restored, and the company has advised customers to change their credentials.

314bbe2396679718.title: Hackers Compromise Ethersphere's bee-js and Swarm Desktop to Deliver Wallet-Stealing Malware
summary: Attackers abused the Ethersphere project's release automation to publish malicious bee-js 13.3.0 and Swarm Desktop 0.56.2 for the Swarm storage network.

Both releases fetch and run code that steals the node wallet key and its password and installs a backdoor on Windows, macOS, and Linux. The bee-js payload runs at npm install time and the app payload runs at launch.
The malicious versions were removed and a clean Swarm Desktop 0.56.3 was released. Existing backdoors and stolen keys are not removed, so affected users must rotate keys and inspect their machines.

f7d08755520d29c3.title: 9th November – Threat Intelligence Report
summary: Check Point Research summarized the week's major attacks, vulnerabilities, and threat analyses as of November 9.
Queens Public Library in New York was hit by ransomware that encrypted its systems, while Russian hosting provider Beget suffered a destructive attack that wiped data.
The bulletin also covers patches for SonicWall, Barracuda, and OpenSSH flaws, plus threat reports on APT29 and BITTER APT.

1b73b76e4ba31716.title: Binance denies data breach after alleged ShinyHunters claims
summary: Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, has denied a claimed breach after a threat actor using the ShinyHunters name offered to sell records of 335 million users.
The actor asked for $900,000 for data said to include KYC documents, passwords, and wallet private keys, but Binance says the claim is likely a scam.

Binance says no evidence shows its systems were compromised, and similar past listings involved infostealer data from users' devices. It urged users never to share passwords, 2FA codes, or seed phrases.

e198a8120e2e987c.title: Summary of Fraud SMS Sent Through a Fake Base Station
summary: The Tokyo Metropolitan Police Department arrested a Chinese national on November 7, 2026, for allegedly operating a fake base station in Ginza, Tokyo, in violation of the Radio Act, and announced it on November 9.
The device forced nearby smartphones out of coverage and pushed them onto 2G, where they received fraudulent SMS messages directing victims to a card-data phishing site.
Eighteen victims reported losses totaling about 4 million yen, and the suspect denies the charges while police investigate possible organized involvement.

0f6befa628a9b619.title: Ukrainian Police Arrest Four Over Crypto Investment Scam Targeting Germans
summary: Ukrainian police arrested four members of a call center scam ring that defrauded Germans with fake cryptocurrency and stock investments.
The group built trust with victims by phone and messaging, then had them open accounts on a fake trading platform and send funds to wallets controlled by the group.
Some victims also gave the group access to their online banking accounts. Of the victims, 135 Germans lost more than EUR 4.3 million (USD 4.8 million).
According to The Record, the scheme totaled about USD 5 million. Police searched more than 50 locations and seized over USD 90,000 in cash.
The suspects face charges of fraud and participation in a criminal organization, with a maximum sentence of 12 years in prison.

0e77ac16cd5877a6.title: Former FBI Agent Admits Stealing $2.5 Million in Crypto From Investigation Targets
summary: Former FBI agent Patrick Stephen Yarochi has admitted to stealing roughly $2.4 million to $2.5 million in cryptocurrency from wallets belonging to fraud victims and a state-sponsored hacker under investigation.
