According to Security NEXT, a contractor employee lost a bag containing documents with the names, addresses and phone numbers of 84 households on a train on October 20.
The bureau is still searching for the missing drives, has contacted affected individuals to apologize and explain the situation, and has instructed staff to strictly manage storage media.

1a02be762dad0338.title: Furusato Choice Unauthorized Access Exposes 4.45 Million Member Records
summary: Trustbank, the operator of the Furusato Choice donation platform, confirmed unauthorized access by a third party on October 17 and suspended the service on October 19.
The attack method and intrusion path have not been disclosed, and the company is investigating the cause with external experts.
Personal data of 4,454,097 members was leaked, including names, email addresses, postal addresses, phone numbers, hashed passwords, and estimated donation tax deduction amounts.
The company invalidated all member passwords and said it will gradually resume the web version from 12:00 on November 6.
Members were urged to beware of phishing emails, text messages, and calls and to reset their passwords, while systems for municipalities and gift providers resumed earlier on October 26.

69f564e8934d7563.title: How Adversaries Are Turning the Vulnerability Ecosystem Against Defenders
summary: CrowdStrike analyzed exploitation speed for vulnerabilities with public proof-of-concept code from January to July 2026, finding a median under one day and a fastest case of 35 minutes.
Attackers quickly weaponized a public blog's guidance and detection tool for the cPanel authentication bypass CVE-2026-41940, driving widespread exploitation.
Of vulnerabilities with public POC code, 91 percent were exploited within 48 hours, and the report concludes that traditional patch cycles can no longer keep pace.

609641a947364426.title: Multiple Vulnerabilities Found in SolarWinds Dameware Remote Support Product
summary: SolarWinds has disclosed multiple vulnerabilities in its Dameware remote operation product and released fixed version 2026.3.1.
The most severe, CVE-2026-28336, is a command injection flaw that requires authentication but could lead to compromise of remotely managed hosts, rated 9.9 Critical under CVSSv3.
Fixes also cover CVE-2026-28335 (buffer overflow), CVE-2026-28327 (DLL hijacking during installation), and third-party component vulnerabilities.

f17b5694c2815bc0.title: NIKKE PC Launcher Script Tampering Used to Distribute Malware
summary: Level Infinite said four scripts in the NIKKE PC launcher were tampered with on September 27, allowing malicious programs to run when the launcher started.
Attackers used the hijacked insightjs.com domain to deliver a loader and the K2F remote access backdoor.
The malware installed a DLL into Chrome to persist and reportedly targeted passwords and cryptocurrency wallet data.

According to BleepingComputer, the payload included a malicious LuaJIT module and account and wallet theft functions, and some tampered files may have remained, so the scope remains under investigation.

Level Infinite replaced the files and refreshed CDN caches on November 4, then released scanning, removal, and account protection guidance on November 5, and urged users who launched the client after September 27 to check their PCs and change passwords.

1757022ff3a7dd87.title: National Tax Service e-Tax Suspicious Communications Detected, Service Suspended Then Restored
summary: The National Tax Service of Korea suspended its e-Tax filing and payment system on November 4, 2026 after detecting suspicious communications.
Emergency inspections were conducted on related equipment, and the specific attack method has not been confirmed.
The service resumed at 11 a.m. on November 5, and the agency said no taxpayer information was leaked.

2aad3116192a6488.title: Ruby on Rails Update Fixes 21 Vulnerabilities
summary: Ruby on Rails released security updates 8.1.4.1 and 8.0.5.2 on November 4, 2026, fixing 21 security issues.

The most severe flaw, CVE-2026-122006 with a CVSS 3.1 score of 9.8, affects image processing in Active Storage via ImageMagick. Crafted file uploads could let attackers write arbitrary files to the server.
The developers strongly urge users to update to the patched versions and warn that the 8.0 branch loses security support on November 7.

3109abadd9fe09a0.title: Google and Japanese Police Take Down XCPE Botnet Infecting 1.3 Million Android TV Set-Top Boxes
summary: Google and industry partners, along with the National Police Agency of Japan, disrupted the XCPE botnet, which comprised more than 1.3 million Android TV set-top boxes, Google announced on November 2.
Google assesses that Shenzhen-based Videostrong Technology embedded a backdoor in pre-installed firmware and operated it for financial gain.
The backdoor, planted before devices shipped, let criminal affiliates buy access and install malicious modules used for ad fraud, residential proxy rental, and additional malware delivery.
Reported infection figures vary by source, with TrendAI counting roughly 1.47 million infected devices across 206 models between June and October.

Google cut ties with the vendor and blocked C2 domains and servers, possibly severing command channels for at least 10 million other infected devices. The National Police Agency also announced unauthorized money transfer cases tied to the devices.

7acf2c3de08cb974.title: JPCERT/CC Weekly Report: Multiple Microsoft Edge Vulnerabilities and 14 Other Advisories (2026-11-05)
summary: JPCERT/CC published a weekly roundup of 15 security advisories covering October 25 to 31, 2026.
The advisories include vulnerabilities in Microsoft Edge, Sophos UTM, Cisco Secure Firewall, and Google Chrome that could enable code execution or denial of service.
Most issues are fixed by updating products, and CISA added a WordPress vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

bbd025854bb9c137.title: Ukraine fires two senior security officials amid corruption probe into scam call centers
summary: Two senior officials of Ukraine's Security Service (SBU) were fired over alleged links to a criminal network that bribed police and prosecutors to shield scam call centers.
Investigators say the group also engaged in drug trafficking, counterfeit cigarette production, currency forgery, kidnapping and assault, and identified at least 12 people involved.
During a court-authorized search, a senior SBU official reportedly threatened to use a firearm and blocked investigators. Parliament has passed new criminal penalties for fraudulent call centers.

0497f82304a52b05.title: Visa prepaid service V Preca users' data exposed through outsourced payment support system
summary: GMO Payment Gateway said unauthorized activity was confirmed on an issuing support service it provides to Life Card on October 30 and disclosed the incident on November 2.
Details of the attack method have not been disclosed.

According to ITmedia, three of the 69 affected records likely exposed card numbers, security codes, expiration dates and names of V Preca users, while the other 63 included names, email addresses, phone numbers and partial addresses.
Life Card removed the three affected accounts on October 31 after finding no fraudulent use, contacted affected customers individually and suspended some services while checking safety.
INTERNET Watch reported that no secondary damage had been confirmed and services had resumed.

da269a2b88d4ed7d.title: Unauthorized Access to Part of Lifenet Insurance Systems May Have Exposed Customer Data Held by KDDI
summary: KDDI disclosed on October 30 that unauthorized access to a system linking Lifenet Insurance with KDDI may have led to a leak of some KDDI customer data.
The attacker reportedly exploited a vulnerability in part of Lifenet's system to obtain customer information held by KDDI.
About 20,000 records may be affected, and KDDI is notifying affected customers individually while both companies investigate the full scope and work on preventive measures.

24a110c5040d0284.title: Ransomware Attack on Don Quijote Contractor Raises Possible Leak of Watch Repair Customer Data
summary: Don Quijote announced on October 28 that Cox, a contractor handling its watch repair services, was hit by a ransomware attack.
An external attack encrypted a server operated by Cox, including customer information entrusted to it by Don Quijote.
No data leak has been confirmed so far, but one cannot be ruled out, and a specialist firm is investigating and working to restore the server.

348775167b49aaca.title: Japan Post Group Labor Union Hit by Unauthorized Access, Over 40,000 Member Records Leaked
summary: The Japan Post Group Labor Union (JP Union) announced on October 26, 2026 that a third party had gained unauthorized access to a mail magazine system it operated until around 2019, leaking member information.
The breach was discovered after the website operations contractor reported it, and the contractor is currently conducting a detailed investigation.
A distribution list of over 40,000 mail magazine recipients may have been leaked, including regional headquarters names, member names, member numbers, gender, and email addresses.

c2b9a3465a1bb3cf.title: Unauthorized Access at Mirabo, Operator of Disability Support App, Due to Unanticipated Design Flaw
summary: Taito City, Tokyo, announced unauthorized access to the operator of its disability support app Sasaeru, Mirabo Co., Ltd.
A design flaw in account registration and permission management allowed attackers to create unauthorized administrator accounts and download member data, with 197 email addresses confirmed leaked.
The fraudulent accounts were deleted and the system was patched, while new member registrations are suspended and residents are warned about phishing emails.

4485fc1b43d16257.title: Doutor Coffee Employee Personal Data Possibly Leaked in Unauthorized System Access
summary: Doutor Coffee detected unauthorized access to its internal systems on October 20, 2026, and disclosed the incident on October 26.
Personal data of current and former employees stored on the systems may have been viewed and leaked by external third parties.

The 951 affected workers and former staff at four stores in Tokyo had their names, dates of birth, addresses, phone numbers and bank account numbers exposed, and the company is contacting them in sequence.
The attack method and intrusion path were not disclosed, and the company is continuing containment and investigation.

5fa39880bfed998a.title: Gifty e-Gift Fraudulent Issuance via System Vulnerability Exploitation
summary: Gifty, a subsidiary of Gifty Group, disclosed that fraudulent e-gift certificates were issued after a third party gained unauthorized access by exploiting a system vulnerability on October 25.
The attacker used the compromised system to issue new e-gifts, affecting part of the system that operates the digital gift service giftee.
According to ScanNetSecurity, the company expects losses of about 550 million yen, to be booked as an extraordinary loss in the fourth quarter of the fiscal year ending December 2026.
No unauthorized use of customers' existing e-gifts or personal data breach has been confirmed.
The company suspended the affected system, blocked the attack path, and is pursuing measures to prevent recurrence, and will not resume the system.

0e0f670ae2abd220.title: Unauthorized Access to COMSBI Enterprise Platform, a LINE Integration Service
summary: Sonic Move disclosed on October 26 that its LINE integration platform COMSBI Enterprise Platform for corporate clients was accessed without authorization on the morning of October 23, 2026.
An intruder obtained admin panel credentials, logged in, and used a flaw in the admin panel to obtain server credentials.

Some customers' admin user data, LINE Official Account settings, and end-user personal information were leaked or may have been leaked. The service remains suspended while credentials are revoked and an external forensic investigation continues.

03b2475ff2950d20.title: Unauthorized Access to Value Design Exposes Some Mos Card Numbers
summary: Mos Food Services said on October 23 that unauthorized access to Value Design, which runs server operations for its prepaid Mos Card system, exposed some card data.
Suspicious access and login attempts on the management system were detected between October 14 and 18, and the investigation confirmed leaks of card numbers, PIN numbers and balance information.

Data for 1,133,070 of about 3.8 million issued cards was exposed, and PINs linked to the leaked numbers were forced to change. Customers are urged to check for unknown charges while additional safeguards are implemented.

5d7c2392ccf1084d.title: Unquoted File Path Vulnerability in Yamaha YMS-VPN8 and YMS-VPN8-CP
summary: IPA and JPCERT/CC disclosed an unquoted file path vulnerability in Yamaha YMS-VPN8 and YMS-VPN8-CP on October 28 via JVN.
Windows service paths are not enclosed in quotes, so a user with write access to the system drive could execute arbitrary code with SYSTEM privileges.
The flaw is fixed in version 1.07.00. Where updating is difficult, the developer recommends restricting logins by untrusted users and limiting administrator rights.

d14482f0ccb5f2fd.title: DLL Loading Vulnerability in Yamaha LAN Monitor for Windows Installer
summary: IPA and JPCERT/CC disclosed a DLL loading vulnerability in the installer for Yamaha LAN Monitor for Windows via JVN on October 28.
The installer loads a specific DLL from its own directory due to improper file search path control, tracked as CVE-2026-103665.
Running the installer alongside a crafted DLL may allow arbitrary code execution with administrator privileges. Version 1.10.1 fixes the issue, and users are advised to install the latest version.

9ed3b91cfef29fe1.title: Multiple Vulnerabilities in Yamaha NWR100 Wi-Fi Routers Require Firmware Update
summary: IPA and JPCERT/CC disclosed multiple vulnerabilities in Yamaha NWR100 Wi-Fi 6 routers for small businesses on October 28 via JVN.

An OS command injection flaw (CVE-2026-97854) allows attackers to execute arbitrary commands through crafted requests, and an access control weakness (CVE-2026-109822) exposes the CONFIG file without authentication.
Severity scores differ by outlet. Security NEXT reported CVSSv4.0 scores of 9.3 and 7.1, while INTERNET Watch reported a CVSS 3.1 score of 9.8.
Firmware Rev.26.00.07 and earlier are affected, and Rev.26.00.08 fixes the issues. If updating is not possible, administrators should restrict Web GUI access and apply source IP address filters.

3660b3e2ee840cb7.title: Vercel rolls out new protection against stolen session cookie attacks
summary: Vercel is gradually rolling out Device Bound Session Credentials (DBSC) to its platform to counter infostealer malware.
Login sessions are bound to a private key stored in the device TPM, so stolen session cookies cannot be reused on other devices.
DBSC currently works in Chrome on macOS and Windows, and the rollout is gradual to handle edge cases involving OAuth apps.

a923233ca622aed1.title: Unauthorized Access to Delivery Platform Pickgo Leads to Customer Data Breach at 7NOW and Demaekan
summary: Seven-Eleven Japan said on November 3 that customer information from its 7NOW delivery service was leaked after unauthorized access to CBcloud, its delivery contractor.
The unauthorized access hit Pickgo, a delivery management platform operated by CBcloud, on November 1, and 7NOW customer data was taken from it.

The breach affected about 164,000 records containing names only, 4,762 records with names and addresses, and 209 records with names, addresses, phone numbers and postal codes. Credit card data and passwords were not exposed, and no fraudulent use has been confirmed.
Demaekan reported that about 800 recipient records were also leaked. CBcloud restricted some functions and access from outside Japan, and the service remains operational.

92d9033c524ce383.title: Two Canadians Charged Over Hacking of US Universities to Mine Cryptocurrency
summary: A federal grand jury in New York indicted two Canadian nationals for allegedly hacking multiple US university and education networks between 2016 and 2019 to mine cryptocurrency, according to the US Department of Justice.

The suspects used virtual private servers in several countries, including European nations, registered under aliases to distribute malware and steal login credentials. They used already compromised devices as a foothold to target campuses with supercomputers.
The attackers ran mining software on infected machines, damaging at least 10 computers and causing losses exceeding 5,000 dollars, BleepingComputer reported.
The intrusions lasted from June 2016 to December 2019. Roach was extradited from Canada on October 28, while extradition proceedings for the second suspect, Stubbings, are ongoing in Canadian courts.

eedd69be35970864.title: DreamHost File Manager Breach Exposes FTP Credentials and Forces Password Resets
summary: DreamHost forced password resets for email and FTP/SFTP users after a File Manager service outage in October 2026.
The company said its File Manager server was breached, allowing unauthorized access to FTP/SFTP credentials from August 2026 to October 23.
Attackers reportedly exploited a vulnerability in the file management software, and webmail session data for some users may also have been exposed, according to BleepingComputer.
The company blocked the attack path, terminated sessions, and is offering one year of credit monitoring, but has not disclosed how many accounts were affected.
Initially the company did not explain the cause, drawing customer complaints, and SecurityWeek reported that File Manager was restored after a fix.

11f47d2525270cc4.title: Debian and Ubuntu APT Flaw Lets MitM Attackers Swap Verified Packages and Run Code as Root
summary: A flaw tracked as CVE-2026-109518 in APT, the package manager for Debian and Ubuntu, lets an attacker who can modify package downloads swap a verified package for their own and run code as root.
The attack abuses HTTP redirects and temporary server errors to make APT retry downloads, and affects Debian 12 and Ubuntu 22.04 and later by default.

Debian and Ubuntu have released fixed versions, and Ubuntu rates the flaw high priority with a CVSS 4.0 score of 7.7. No exploitation has been reported, and no workaround is offered for systems that cannot yet be updated.

75e50fe468da1346.title: Ukrainian news outlet Kyiv Independent hit by suspected Russian cyberattack
summary: Suspected Russian hackers breached the website management system and newsletter service of Kyiv Independent, a leading English-language Ukrainian news outlet.
The attackers posted false messages and sent emails in Russian and English falsely claiming Zelensky had launched a nuclear strike on Kyiv.
The outlet said staff quickly removed the content and payment data was not compromised, and it is investigating with cybersecurity specialists without technical evidence tying the breach to Moscow.

477a11a451268078.title: Jailbreak Bundle for OpenAI Codex Hides Prompt Adware That Injects Gateway Ads into AI Responses
summary: Check Point Research said a Chinese-language jailbreak bundle named Haiou, targeting OpenAI Codex, modifies AI agent global instruction files to insert ads for a specific LLM gateway site into responses.
The bundle bypasses model safeguards using prompt injection and CTF scenario reconstruction, and is configured so that greetings such as hello trigger the ad.
The GitHub repository gained 403 stars after going public and appears aimed at users seeking unsupported Codex access in China, with researchers warning it could be abused as a supply chain attack.
Attacker servers were found hosting the bundle alongside Cobalt Strike, Ladon, and VulnClaw, though Check Point found no evidence that the creator was involved in criminal activity.

cd6687b678f2987d.title: mSecure Password Manager Suspicious Activity Prompts Password and 2FA Reset Advisory
summary: mSeven Software warned current and former customers of the mSecure password manager to change passwords, reset two-factor authentication, and remove passkeys after detecting suspicious activity.
According to customer support replies, an attacker stole an encrypted database from mSecure cloud storage, and only users who use sync are affected.
The company said there is no evidence that encrypted data was viewed, but it has not disclosed how the breach happened, the scope of impact, or the number of users notified.
The company said it has brought in outside security experts to investigate and that encrypted vault data cannot be accessed.

67fc46ca9133c3af.title: Google Calendar phishing campaign hijacks sessions, bypasses MFA
summary: A phishing operation dubbed Operation CloudFire has been hijacking live Google sessions from corporate users since mid-August 2026.
Lures arrive as Google Calendar invites and route through Google's redirector to a reverse proxy that relays the real sign-in page, capturing SMS and authenticator codes.
Material Security says it catches over 99% of malicious messages and took down hundreds of domains, while Cloudflare abuse reports disrupted the attacker's infrastructure.

d53061b0debe2664.title: Records for 621 Students Missing from Six Shizuoka Prefectural Schools
summary: Six prefectural schools in Shizuoka Prefecture have lost track of student guidance records covering 621 graduates.
The loss came to light when a June 30 request for a credit certificate prompted a records check, revealing 55 missing files; a prefecture-wide survey then found 566 more across five schools.
Staff interviews and on-site searches failed to locate the records, and the schools have posted apologies on their websites and are informing graduates.

23e0079f9ae6863e.title: VerifiedIDA | Making LLM-Driven Reverse Engineering Inspectable, Continuable and Reusable
summary: SentinelLABS has released VerifiedIDA, a new standard that makes LLM-driven reverse engineering results verifiable.
Its open-source IDA Pro implementation links annotations to supporting evidence, allowing analysis to be reviewed, resumed and reused.
Only a brief summary was available, so details of how it works and its scope should be checked in the original article.

c14da079df407ab6.title: The Classics Return: Vulnerable E-Mail Scripts, (Wed, Nov 4th)
summary: SANS ISC honeypots recorded a renewed rise in scans targeting e-mail sending scripts on web servers.
The scanned paths, such as sendmail.php and mail_config.php, suggest attackers are looking for forms that accept arbitrary recipient addresses, likely for spam relay.
No specific vulnerability was linked to the scans, and the author stresses that removing leftover development test scripts and secret files is essential.

bc9b79ade1a345b9.title: Critical Rails Flaw Lets Attackers Write Server Files via Crafted ImageMagick Uploads
summary: A critical Active Storage flaw in Ruby on Rails, rated 9.8 on CVSS, has been fixed in versions 8.1.4.1 and 8.0.5.2.
Apps that process uploads with ImageMagick can let unauthenticated attackers write arbitrary server files via a crafted upload, triggered just by attaching the file.
Apps using the Disk service may also expose secret_key_base and other credentials, which could enable remote code execution. The advisory does not say whether it has been exploited.

f4328deaa9fcd2f6.title: Xen Hypervisor Flaws Let One Malicious VM Read and Write Any Other VM's Memory
summary: Two Xen hypervisor flaws, CVE-2026-102703 and CVE-2026-102704, let a malicious guest VM read and write the memory of other VMs on the same host, including dom0.
The flaws stem from grant copy, the inter-VM data copy operation, where Xen reuses earlier permission checks and in some cases skips a required recheck.
All Xen versions from 4.6 onward are affected and patches are available, with XCP-ng and Qubes OS also releasing updates. No exploitation has been reported.

a0e22415c9692215.title: SlippyNunchucks Hijacks Sogou Input Method DNS to Deliver DarkVigil Backdoor
summary: China-linked threat group SlippyNunchucks hijacked DNS by abusing unencrypted HTTP traffic from the Sogou Input Method for Windows since July 2026, ESET reported.
The attackers redirected configuration requests from SGTool.exe to malicious servers, using DLL side-loading to execute the DarkVigil backdoor.
Victims were identified in Hong Kong, Thailand, Japan, Vietnam, Oman, and Sri Lanka.
Tencent fixed the flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-120422, by switching the requests to HTTPS in version 16.10, with ESET dating the fix to October 30 and The Hacker News to October 29.

b99898ca0e81f136.title: Malicious cPGuard Updates Pushed Through OpsShield Supply Chain Attack
summary: Indian IT security firm OpsShield was compromised, and its cPGuard server security software versions 5.88.12 through 5.88.19 were distributed with updates containing malicious scripts.
Attackers used stolen credentials to take over billing and licensing servers, then accessed the update distribution CDN and published fake updates.
The installed scripts planted backdoors and harvested /etc/shadow, database configuration, and SSH keys, which were uploaded to a licensing server.
According to SecurityWeek, about 2,950 servers executed the fake updates, and roughly 7,900 customer account records and password hashes were exposed in a data breach.
BleepingComputer counted 2,946 affected servers. OpsShield urged customers to update to version 5.88.25 or later and rotate passwords and SSH keys, with later releases now being rolled out.

ff152713b2d1413a.title: Google Patches 213 Vulnerabilities in Chrome 157, Including 7 Critical Flaws
summary: Google released Chrome 157 to its stable channel, fixing 213 vulnerabilities identified by CVE.
Seven are rated Critical, including buffer overflow and use-after-free flaws in Dawn, the WebGPU implementation, and ANGLE.
SecurityWeek reported bounties of $10,000 for the Dawn overflow and $1,000 for the ANGLE memory corruption.
Seventy-seven High-severity bugs were also patched, including a V8 type confusion flaw, along with 75 Medium and 54 Low issues.

SecurityWeek reported no exploitation has been observed, and users should update immediately to 157.0.8103.38/.39 on Windows and macOS or 157.0.8103.38 on Linux. Security NEXT said the update will roll out in phases over several days to weeks.

604a668fc6e9efe0.title: Russia Arrests Three Suspects and Dismantles VasyGrek Cybercrime Infrastructure
summary: Russian authorities arrested three suspects linked to the VasyGrek (Fluffy Wolf) threat group and dismantled its criminal infrastructure.
The group used spearphishing emails disguised as financial documents to execute malware and used remote access tools to siphon funds from institutional accounts.
The Russian Interior Ministry confirmed losses of 660,000 rubles, about $8,000, with one company losing the money through a malicious attachment.
Kaspersky recorded more than 100 attacks targeting Russia, Belarus and Kazakhstan between January and September 2026.
The alleged ringleader was placed under house arrest, while two accomplices were released under travel restrictions. It remains unclear whether the arrests have fully ended the group's activities.

383ea96346407c66.title: Google Issues Patches for Critical Android Flaw That Could Allow RCE Without User Interaction
summary: Google's November security bulletin disclosed CVE-2026-58868, a critical Android flaw that could let a remote attacker run code on a phone without any user action.
The flaw is a possible out-of-bounds write caused by a heap buffer overflow in onOutputReceived in FrameDecoder.cpp, and it is fixed in security patch level 2026-11-01 or later.

As of the bulletin, no exploitation had been reported and the flaw was not in CISA's KEV catalog. A separate critical flaw, CVE-2026-58882, in SMS WAP Push handling could cause remote denial of service.

baa04e58d009e5be.title: Linux Kernel IPv4 TCP Use-After-Free Flaw CVE-2026-98432 Enables Remote Root Attacks on MPTCP Servers
summary: On October 15, 2026, the Linux kernel CNA disclosed CVE-2026-98432, a use-after-free flaw in IPv4 TCP handling.
A race condition during TCP connection setup lets attackers read freed memory using crafted packets with IP options.
Servers running MPTCP listeners could face unauthenticated remote root command execution, raising concerns about kernel crashes and memory data leaks.
Anthropic demonstrated an exploit achieving remote root command execution, and reports differ on whether Claude or an internal model wrote it.
The CNA rated the flaw CVSS 9.8 Critical, while Red Hat, Oracle, and SUSE scored it 8.1 among others. No in-the-wild exploitation has been reported yet.

bf693c39e01f3976.title: Ministry of Foreign Affairs network breach may have exposed about 3,600 personal data records
summary: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs disclosed on October 30, 2026 that unauthorized access had occurred on a network that communicates with external systems.
Some reports said a third party stole mail service credentials to break into the network, and the intrusion was detected on July 27.
The ministry blocked the access and invalidated the compromised credentials, saying email addresses and names of about 3,600 records may have been exposed.
About 900 of these records belong to people who are not ministry employees, and the ministry confirmed no classified information was included.
No secondary damage has been confirmed. The ministry is contacting affected individuals directly, warning them about phishing, and is investigating with an external specialist firm.

d9b344f8708e88e2.title: Why Cookie Consent Banners Make It Hard to Decline: Tactics Revealed by a Survey of 14,000 Websites
summary: Researchers at Sungkyunkwan University in South Korea used an automated detection tool called UMBRA to survey dark patterns in cookie consent banners across 14,000 websites worldwide.
Many sites made refusing consent hard, requiring multiple clicks in settings or hiding ways to withdraw consent, and some demanded payment to reject cookies.
Between 44% and 83% of sites set third-party cookies before any consent, and 80% of collected cookies had weak security settings that could expose them to cross-site scripting attacks.

c1474011a19c25c0.title: What Separates Companies That Pay Ransomware Demands From Those That Don't? Dutch Police and Researchers Analyze About 700 Cases
summary: Researchers from the Dutch police and the University of Edinburgh analyzed 461 ransomware incident cases and 237 published negotiation chat logs.
Attackers set ransom amounts based on victims' ability to pay and haggled over prices in chat. About 25.8% of victims paid.
Whether a victim had a fully restorable backup was the strongest factor in the decision to pay. Double extortion and cyber insurance did not clearly raise payment rates.

5cec1f1883c7f3e8.title: When trust becomes the payload: Inside the threats, etc quarterly report
summary: Elastic Security Labs published this quarterly report, based on confirmed customer intrusions from April to September 2026, describing how attackers abuse signed legitimate software and trusted accounts.

Adversaries used remote monitoring tools, AI coding assistants, and Microsoft first-party clients to maintain interactive access without traditional malware, with ScreenConnect named most often among RMM abuse cases.
Attackers used AiTM phishing kits and legacy authentication gaps to bypass MFA, and in some cases logged in with infostealer-harvested credentials about eight minutes after infection.

4529f2523655e561.title: Monitoring AI agent sessions: Leveraging embedding models to aid threat hunting and attack discovery workflows
summary: Elastic Security Labs tested storing six months of Claude Code and Cursor sessions as semantic vectors and searching them.
Each turn is embedded by channel so agent behavior that query rules miss can be found through similarity search.
The authors argue embedding search suits threat hunting better than re-evaluating every session with an LLM, which costs more and varies between runs.

73f0af4dd2638af7.title: Multiple Vulnerabilities in WordPress 6.x and 7.x Enable Remote Code Execution
summary: Several vulnerabilities in certain WordPress 6.9 and 7.0 versions allow remote code execution, and exploit code targeting them has been published.

Attackers can chain an SQL injection flaw in WP_Query with a route confusion issue in REST API batch processing. This allows unauthenticated creation of administrator accounts and installation of malicious plugins.
Sites should update to WordPress 6.9.5 or 7.0.2 or later, as the SQL injection flaw also affects versions before 6.8.6 and prompt patching is strongly advised.

786fa21bcd991f5c.title: Proofpoint Blog No. 60: Ransomware Infection Rate in Japan Nearly Doubles in Two Years, 12-Country Survey 2026
summary: According to Proofpoint's 2026 AI Ransomware Landscape Report, the ransomware infection rate among Japanese companies rose to 73% in 2025, up from 38% in 2023.
Japan recorded the largest increase among the 11 countries that could be compared, although its 2025 rate remained below the 12-country average of 84%.
Japan's ransom payment rate was 37%, and about 40% of companies that paid still faced additional demands or failed recovery. Only 36% received full cyber insurance reimbursement.

14e080846524dd22.title: Kumiai App Shuts Down Service and Abandons Resumption After Critical PHP Vulnerability
summary: Japanese service Kumiai App has decided to shut down rather than resume operations after a critical PHP vulnerability was disclosed.
Only the headline is available, so the vulnerability's identifier, attack method, and any data exposure remain unconfirmed.
Beyond the service closure decision, the scale of impact and specific response measures cannot be determined from the available information.

3a12a5c7638e850d.title: Unauthorized Access to ELESTYLE System May Have Exposed Merchant Registration Data
summary: ELESTYLE disclosed on October 29 that it had confirmed unauthorized access to part of its management system on October 25.
The intruder exploited an access control flaw in certain functions of the management system, which the company fixed on October 27.
Usernames, email addresses, and internal system identifiers for 7,162 merchant registration records may have been taken, and affected merchants will be contacted individually.

2fad049a4311e228.title: Unauthorized Access Found on Chariloto Betting Service for Keirin and Auto Race After Log Review
summary: Chari-Loto, the betting service for keirin and auto races operated by Chari Loto Co., was hit by unauthorized access on October 21, 2026, leading to customer data leaks.
The attacker exploited a vulnerability in the system, and the intrusion was confirmed after suspicious logs were found during a security review on October 22.

Personal data of 373 Charika members was stolen, including bank account and credit card details. The service was suspended, patched, and resumed on October 23, and affected customers are being notified.

1d2dc271f6c984a7.title: Unauthorized Access to Expressway Information Site Dora-Tora, Registered Data May Have Been Viewed
summary: NEXCO East (East Nippon Expressway) announced on October 23 that a third party had gained unauthorized access to Drive Traffic, its expressway information site.
Email addresses, passwords, gender, prefecture, and birth year of some registered customers may have been viewed.
The company plans to notify affected customers individually by email. No confirmed data leak or attack method has been disclosed.

a405c5f95825ae53.title: Unauthorized Access to Value Card House Electronic Money Service Exposes ID Numbers and More
summary: A third party gained unauthorized access to the server of Value Card, a house electronic money issuing service provided by Value Design, a subsidiary of Pay Cloud Holdings, leading to a partial data leak.
The attackers exploited a vulnerability in a web server in part of the system, and the incident was discovered on October 19.

A total of 1,424,748 records of ID numbers, PIN numbers, and balance information were exposed, and 569,224 issued IDs were at risk of misuse but have been addressed. The company has blocked the access route and is reviewing all services with outside experts.

5bfbcbdd6fd2341c.title: Unauthorized Access at Travel Zip Co., Ltd., Manager of Taito Ward Websites
summary: Taito Ward in Tokyo said on October 23 that personal data was leaked through unauthorized access to Travel Zip Co., Ltd., the company that manages its websites.
The tourism information site TAITO Odekake Navi and an official site for a former campaign were affected, and the intrusion route and method are still under investigation.
About 5,500 records with names, email addresses, phone numbers and addresses and about 120 inquiries have been confirmed as leaked, and the ward warned of impersonation requests.

13f32bba47ffebb9.title: Good Smile Company Online Shop Unauthorized Access Raises Payment Card Data Breach Concerns
summary: Good Smile Company disclosed that unauthorized access to its official online shop occurred multiple times between October 19 and 22, 2026, targeting administrative information.
Attackers exploited a system vulnerability to take over administrator privileges and planted malicious code on the card payment page.
According to Impress Watch, card data entered between 13:55 on October 21 and 7:00 on October 23 by up to 2,800 customers may have been stolen.
ITmedia NEWS reported that full card numbers, security codes, last four digits, and expiry dates for about 402,466 cards, plus up to 7,673 order records, may also have been exposed.
The company fixed the vulnerability and reported the incident to the Personal Information Protection Commission, while the site remains closed with no reopening date set.

51a09aab7c050c6a.title: Japan Expands Consultation Desks for Personal Data Leak Victims
summary: On October 30, 2026, the Prime Minister's Office of Japan announced consultation desks for victims of personal data leaks and people at risk of exposure.
The move follows a rise in cyberattacks targeting companies and growing concern that leaked data could be used for secondary attacks.

The Information-technology Promotion Agency, Japan (IPA) expanded its individual consultation desk after leaks increased through exploitation of web system vulnerabilities and supply chain compromises.
The listed contacts include Consumer Affairs Centers, the police consultation hotline #9110, the Financial Services Agency, and the Japan Credit Card Association.

IPA provides advice by phone and email to prevent secondary damage and offers general security measure information, but its support is limited to technical advice and excludes individual investigations.

b22bd9b6c7258020.title: Vulnerability in HA Monitor Option (Management Server-less) for HA8000V Could Allow OS Command Injection via Local Access
summary: Hitachi disclosed CVE-2026-84726, a vulnerability in the HA Monitor Option (management server-less) for its server products, on October 30, 2026.
A local attacker could exploit an OS command injection flaw to run arbitrary commands on affected systems.
Versions below 3.2.6 on RHEL 7 and 8, and below 4.2.6 on RHEL 9, are affected, and Hitachi urges users to update.

643a98fdb1898f31.title: Prestige Core Solution, Which Runs Roadside Service Business Systems, Reports Up to 5.5 Million Records Leaked in Unauthorized Access; Sony Insurance and ENEOS Car Lease Affected
summary: Prestige International detected unauthorized access to its group business systems on October 29 and invalidated compromised credentials, but intrusions continued, so it shut down the affected system on October 30.
Personal data tied to roadside assistance services that subsidiary Prestige Core Solution provides to insurers and automakers was leaked, with up to 5.5 million records affected.

Leaked data includes names, addresses, phone numbers, vehicle registration and chassis numbers, and some bank account information, while no credit card data has been confirmed; the cause and unique person count remain under investigation. Sony Insurance, ENEOS and other operators have also announced related leaks.

37a5b2061a826324.title: China-Linked Vapor Panda Uses AI Pentest Framework ARTEX to Attack 200 Organizations Worldwide
summary: China-linked threat group Vapor Panda abused ARTEX, an open-source multi-agent AI penetration testing framework, to attack more than 200 organizations in 14 countries.
The AI agents automated reconnaissance, vulnerability exploitation, web shell deployment and credential theft, with human operators stepping in only at key decision points.
According to CrowdStrike, at least nine organizations were compromised, including a Greek government agency where forged admin tokens and mailbox access were observed.
The campaign used planning and execution agents working together, and included a feature to identify hosts without the Falcon sensor installed.

Separately, WorkOS said an attacker used ARTEX AI to gain unauthorized access to an internal sales app, cutting off external access and engaging an independent forensic firm, with production services unaffected.

3f5084029f30fd26.title: LLMjacking Attacks Rack Up Up to $1 Million in Unauthorized Cloud AI Charges
summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) and Mandiant warned that attackers are increasingly abusing stolen API keys and cloud credentials to make unauthorized use of large language models (LLMs), a tactic known as LLMjacking.

Intruders gained access through leaked credentials, GitHub tokens, and exposed keys, and used a LiteLLM flaw (CVE-2026-40217) to obtain administrator privileges before reselling access through LLM mixer services.
According to BleepingComputer, some victims faced unauthorized charges exceeding $100,000 per day and $1 million in total.
Recommended defenses include restricting access, rotating keys, and enforcing multi-factor authentication.

242d0136120ff642.title: Several German lawmakers and foreign policy staff received Apple warnings on spyware
summary: Germany's Federal Office for Information Security (BSI) said several German lawmakers and public figures were among those Apple warned last week about spyware attacks.

The alerts went to members of Chancellor Friedrich Merz's Asia trip delegation, including ministry staff, lawmakers and journalists. Green Party co-leader Franziska Brantner confirmed she was a target.
On Friday, the BSI sent a warning letter telling recipients to assume their devices are infected and replace them immediately. It is not known how many devices were actually infected.

75a75f9b4f20972d.title: Chainstack Reports Production Systems Breach Exposing Customer Data and Password Hashes
summary: Blockchain infrastructure provider Chainstack disclosed that an external attacker breached parts of its production environment.
The attacker entered through a third-party component, moved from a development environment to production, and the intrusion is assessed to be linked to an AI-powered campaign.
Customer account information and password hashes were exposed, and node credentials are treated as exposed, so customers are urged to rotate them and regenerate API keys.

3f465891e602aabe.title: Fake-download campaign uses trojanized installers to deliver monetization payloads
summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has identified a fake-download campaign targeting users who search for cracked software, free games, and activators.
The attackers use trojanized Inno Setup installers to silently install several monetization payloads during a single installation session.
Three monetization branches were confirmed: proxy network resource sales, distributed computing enrollment, and adware-style utility installation, often without user consent.

7d41a4d524ccd732.title: UK school estate hit by 3AM ransomware in suspected AI-assisted attack
summary: A UK school estate was hit by 3AM ransomware, and about 37 of nearly 50 reachable machines were encrypted. Bitdefender suspects the attacker used AI-generated commands and an automated agentic loop, but this is not confirmed.

The attacker harvested credentials from Veeam backup servers, dumped LSASS memory, created backdoor domain admin accounts, and tried to disable Sophos and Bitdefender protection. The initial access method remains unknown.

a9b932194e64610b.title: Russia-Linked Gorbag Hackers Target Ukrainian Law Enforcement and Defense With Infostealers
summary: According to ESET, Russia-aligned threat group Gorbag has targeted Ukrainian government agencies, defense contractors, and facilities handling foreign military aid since February 2025.

The group uses spearphishing emails with disguised documents and the WinRAR vulnerability CVE-2025-8088 to deploy infostealers such as GIFTEDCROOK and BeautyStealer, harvesting browser credentials and VPN settings before deleting traces.
About a quarter of the targets are law enforcement and judicial bodies, possibly to monitor investigations into Russian war crimes or identify collaborators.
Other reports say stolen data is sent to Telegram chats or C2 servers, and reverse shells are also used.
The scale of the damage and any links to other actors remain unconfirmed, so organizations should prioritize patching WinRAR and blocking suspicious attachments.

589900b4a41ca4f2.title: Police seizes over 100 servers in investment scam crackdown
summary: European police arrested seven suspects and seized more than 100 servers in an operation targeting a company suspected of providing fraudulent trading websites to criminal gangs.
The firm allegedly used deceptive ads to lure victims, stole their personal data, and sold it to call center fraud groups, with potential victims in at least 50 countries.
Supported by Europol and Eurojust, the action involved authorities from six countries and followed four years of investigation.

0cbf015f14c782f8.title: Android’s November 2026 Updates Patch Over 200 Vulnerabilities
summary: Google released Android security updates fixing more than 200 vulnerabilities, including about two dozen critical-severity issues.
The first patch level, 2026-11-01, fixes 119 defects, including critical remote code execution flaw CVE-2026-58868 in the Framework component that needs no user interaction.
The 2026-11-05 patch level fixes 97 bugs in the Kernel and several chipset components, including critical flaws in Bluetooth and the MediaTek modem.

d905357a8bb89528.title: Unauthenticated Node-RED Flaw CVE-2026-58115 Exploited Against Siemens IoT2050 Devices
summary: VulnCheck reports that attackers are exploiting the critical Node-RED flaw CVE-2026-58115 to install malicious payloads.

The flaw stems from a missing authentication check on the Node-RED HTTP interface, allowing an unauthenticated remote attacker to craft malicious flows and execute arbitrary code with the highest privileges.
According to VulnCheck, attacks were observed from Microsoft network IPs on October 30, and 15 additional attacks that installed web shells and other tools were confirmed by November 1.
VulnCheck's honeypot also recorded attempts to download and run a Linux botnet binary.
Siemens has released patches for SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced version 4.3.4.1 and later, and recommends removing Node-RED or configuring authentication.

e05590e17b636c9e.title: Harvard University data breach exposed info of 851,000 accounts
summary: Hackers breached Harvard University's alumni and development systems in November 2025, exposing personal data tied to more than 850,000 email addresses.
The ShinyHunters extortion gang claimed the attack and leaked a 1.1GB archive on its dark web site in early February 2026 after Harvard refused to pay a ransom.
The exposed data includes names, phone numbers, addresses, birth dates, and donation records, but Harvard says no Social Security numbers or payment card data were stored in the breached systems.

1c904602ae984a08.title: MLEP in KICS for Networks 5.0: how machine learning helps track network behavior of OT devices
summary: Kaspersky has introduced MLEP, a machine learning event processor in its Kaspersky Industrial CyberSecurity for Networks 5.0 product.
MLEP groups network sessions into 15-second event fragments, learns each device's normal communication patterns, estimates roles for uncategorized devices, and flags anomalies.
It helps complete OT asset inventories and spot unusual connections, but detection quality depends on how much network traffic the system can observe.

4c4a5ef7feb97a49.title: UK NCSC Warns of AI-Driven Cyberattack Surge Against Critical Infrastructure by 2028
summary: UK National Cyber Security Centre Director Richard Horne warned that critical national infrastructure is likely to face AI-enabled cyberattacks by 2028.
In its annual report, the NCSC said cyber incidents could rise unprecedented in the coming months.
AI is not creating new attack methods but enabling threat actors to find and exploit long-neglected vulnerabilities at scale, and it could also help build ransomware malware.

According to SecurityWeek, AI will mainly strengthen existing attack techniques rather than produce new vulnerabilities. According to The Record, AI-based malware is likely to be used in ransomware attacks against critical infrastructure by 2028.
Organizations are urged to reinforce basic defenses, including timely patching, restricting administrator privileges, and maintaining reliable backups.

b96a3b29fd148212.title: Hackers Steal Bitcoin and Litecoin from BTCPay Server Hot Wallets via Outdated Version Flaws
summary: Hackers stole bitcoin and litecoin from hot wallets on BTCPay Server, an open-source cryptocurrency payment processor, in versions 2.4.1 and earlier.
The attacker appears to have used a flaw in pre-2.4.2 versions to log in with administrator privileges, and the exploited vulnerability has not been publicly disclosed.
According to The Hacker News, the method differed from the flaw fixed in 2.4.2, and the start date of the attacks is unknown.
According to BleepingComputer, the developer said public servers were not targeted and no fund losses have been reported in version 2.4.7.
Developers urge users to upgrade to 2.4.7, reset any potentially compromised servers and stored secrets, and immediately shut down instances running 2.4.1 or earlier.

7190d18386665a0d.title: Wuffy the Toy Dog and the Money Trail to Kremlin
summary: A network of more than 250 near-identical online stores selling a discounted AI toy dog was reported to have funneled payments from buyers, with Mastercard estimating about $50 million a year in transactions.
Most victims absorb small charges rather than dispute them, while the operators rely on banks covering losses and on prices that look too low to challenge.

Ransomware proceeds were reportedly laundered through sanctioned exchanges and UK drug gangs to avoid mainstream platforms, and the UK National Crime Agency's Operation Destabilise continues to investigate.

cf0b1254b52dd1ed.title: C3RB3R Ransomware Campaign Targets Unpatched Synology NAS Devices
summary: Synology urged NAS users to immediately update DSM and enable automatic updates amid a surge in C3RB3R ransomware attacks.
Attackers are exploiting a vulnerability patched in December 2024 to encrypt data on devices running outdated DSM versions and demand ransom.
According to The Hacker News, CVE-2024-10441, a remote code execution flaw, may be among the vulnerabilities involved, though the exact exploited flaw has not been disclosed.
According to BleepingComputer, victim reports have continued for over two weeks, with some victims asked to pay thousands of dollars on the dark web for decryption tools.
Blocking internet access to administrative pages is also recommended.

4f5c110c5238c6d3.title: Attackers Target Unpatched CryptoPayment Gateway Flaw That Can Expose Wallet Credentials
summary: Threat actors are attempting to exploit CVE-2026-81648, an unpatched maximum-severity (CVSS 10.0) flaw in the CryptoPayment Gateway WordPress plugin.
A missing authorization check on an AJAX endpoint lets unauthenticated users delete arbitrary server files and recover stored wallet credentials.

Defused Cyber has observed in-the-wild attempts, no fix is available, and the plugin has been removed from the WordPress Plugin Directory. Site owners are advised to remove it, rotate wallet keys, and audit for changes.

6198aa235fd1f3c3.title: Unit 42 Threat Intelligence Highlights - Nov. 2, 2026
summary: Unit 42 has published an overview of recent threat activity it observed, led by state-linked espionage and financially motivated extortion.
Attackers are gaining access through infostealer logs, exposed credentials, and unpatched perimeter assets, and are using multi-extortion and BEC fraud.
Threat actors are also using generative AI and LLMs for social engineering and deepfake executive impersonation, though no specific victims or damage are detailed.

8ddf3c5e638b7f99.title: Largest crypto exchange in Brazil confirms cyberattack as millions flow out of platform
summary: Brazilian crypto exchange Mercado Bitcoin suspended all deposits and withdrawals on Monday after a cybersecurity incident.
Blockchain security firms said more than $46 million left the platform late Sunday, a figure the company has not confirmed.
Mercado Bitcoin says customers were not harmed and no data breach occurred, but some experts say customer wallets were also drained.

55127bb6c4d54457.title: What exploited vulnerabilities have in common: A data-driven analysis of real-world attacks
summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence analyzed about 383,000 software vulnerabilities disclosed from 1999 through September 2026 and found only about 2,000 (roughly 0.5%) linked to real-world exploitation.
Exploited flaws concentrate on takeover classes such as remote code execution, local privilege escalation, and authentication bypass, which account for 78% of exploited vulnerabilities.
Servers are patched slowly while exploits often appear within days of disclosure, so the report urges defenders to prioritize by exposure and attack paths.

aa84a621d291ce77.title: Michigan State cyber incident claimed by ransomware gang behind recent hospital attack
summary: Michigan State University required all students and employees to reset their account passwords after a security incident last month.
The BYOD ransomware gang listed the university on its leak site, claiming it stole personal data on 1.3 million current and former students.

The university said the activity appeared to be a credential compromise, with no evidence the central Active Directory was breached or other data stolen. It did not respond to requests for comment on the claims.

c2962d7b8b872bd0.title: Fintech platform Sageworks taken offline after suspected cyberattack
summary: Abrigo took its Sageworks application offline on October 30 after detecting irregular activity in its environment and began an emergency investigation.

The attack method and nature of the incident have not been disclosed, so it is unclear whether this was a breach or a technical failure. ShinyHunters-linked actors previously claimed an attack on Abrigo.
The company has restored most functions except borrower-facing features, and some researchers advised rotating Sageworks API keys.

c846717f91b3ef10.title: Polymarket Traders Lose Funds in DebugBear Supply Chain Attack
summary: Prediction market platform Polymarket halted trading on October 29 after a third-party supply chain attack, resuming about an hour later.
The attack began with tampering of a real-user monitoring script from web performance firm DebugBear, with a DNS record compromise at the domain registrar believed to be the root cause.
The malicious JavaScript sold logged-in users' positions and moved assets to attacker-controlled wallets.

Loss estimates vary: The Record cited over 2.1 million dollars, while SecurityWeek said 726 wallets were affected and 3.9 million dollars would be paid out. BleepingComputer estimated about 2.5 million dollars.
The company removed the script, reset all login sessions, and pledged full reimbursement while reporting the incident to law enforcement.

fc71621bafae9fc4.title: Threat Hunting: What It Is, How It Works, & Why It Matters
summary: Threat hunting is the proactive search across networks and endpoints for malicious activity that automated defenses missed, assuming an attacker may already be inside.

Analysts build a hypothesis, query telemetry for evidence, and turn findings into detection rules so future attempts are caught automatically. Methods include structured and unstructured hunts and intelligence-, data-, or knowledge-driven approaches.
The article generally explains tools such as SIEM, EDR, and threat intelligence platforms, along with the hunting process and best practices. It does not report on a specific incident or damage.

34f915a2fab16b3c.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: Critical CVEs, Linux DDoS Botnet, Device-Code Phishing, Android Spyware and More
summary: This weekly recap collects major security stories from the past week.
Key items include the North Korean TraderTraitor theft of about $6.4 billion from Binance, the Volt Typhoon Silent Train relay infrastructure, and a patched ChatGPT shared-link flaw.
Details on individual incidents beyond the headlines are not provided in this roundup, so readers should consult the original articles.

5efdd458444ee31d.title: Russia's statistics agency confirms cyberattack claimed by Belarusian and Ukrainian hackers
summary: The Belarusian Cyber Partisans and pro-Ukrainian group Silent Crow claim they attacked Russia's federal statistics agency Rosstat.
The hackers say they spent about six months inside the network, stole data, destroyed servers and storage, and accessed roughly 25,000 devices.
Rosstat confirmed it was targeted but denies any leak of protected information or database compromise, and the claims remain unverified.

91fef9decd05c771.title: 2nd November – Threat Intelligence Report
summary: The weekly roundup covers major breaches, including the theft of about $6.3 billion in digital assets from Binance.
It also covers AI-assisted ransomware and espionage campaigns, plus vulnerabilities in Cisco, Drupal, and the Linux kernel.
Japan Airlines reported that about 92,000 passengers were affected by a third-party breach via the Amadeus system, and a Florida education site breach may affect 4.9 million people.

252a78502c187a80.title: DarkBlinders Compromises Israeli Target and Iraqi Kurdish Government Cloud Environment
summary: An Iran state-aligned threat group called DarkBlinders ran a cyber espionage campaign against Israel and the Kurdistan Region of Iraq between August and October 2026.
The group used spear-phishing and a fake recruitment scheme to deliver trojanized Visual Studio projects, which launch the SHELBYC2 backdoor that uses GitHub for command-and-control.
A high-profile individual in Israel and a Kurdistan regional government cloud environment were compromised, and the activity is linked to APT34 with medium confidence.

bfc6c5ff9e5af03c.title: Florida Student Financial Aid Website Breach Exposes Data of About 4.9 Million People
summary: The Florida Department of Education (FLDOE) said unauthorized access to a student financial aid website may have exposed personal data of about 4.9 million people, according to SecurityWeek, or about 5 million per The Record.
The intrusion was discovered on October 19, and the attack method and the attackers have not been disclosed. The intrusion has since been blocked.
Exposed data may include names, Social Security numbers, dates of birth, addresses, phone numbers, and email addresses. Existing financial aid applicants may be affected.
The website has been taken offline. The department said scholarship and student loan disbursements were not affected, and it advised residents to monitor their credit reports and financial accounts.

773f9c1ac2ea5abd.title: Apple warns users in 99 countries of mercenary spyware
summary: Apple has sent new threat notifications to victims of suspected mercenary spyware attacks in nearly 100 countries.
Alerts went to targeted users in 99 countries, including a Turkey-based reporter and a Lebanese documentary filmmaker.
Apple has not attributed the attacks to any actor or region, and some recipients have publicly shared their notices. Apple did not comment.

0e7b1374b05d8d1b.title: Russian and Ukrainian hackers hijack emergency apps to spread fake nuclear attack warnings
summary: Ukraine's Air Alert emergency app was hijacked, sending Kyiv residents fake warnings of radiation and chemical threats.
The hacking group Hitcore Corp claimed the breach, and its messages included a Telegram channel link. The developers disabled push notifications and temporarily suspended the service.

A group calling itself DC8044 reportedly hacked Russia's EMERCOM mobile app through its API to send false nuclear launch warnings. Both governments said their official warning systems were unaffected.

beda1fedd9cca992.title: Microsoft fixes Smart App Control broken by October Windows update
summary: Microsoft fixed an issue that stopped some Windows 11 devices from turning on Smart App Control after installing the October 2026 security update KB5127648.
On affected devices the option was grayed out, while devices that already had the feature enabled were not impacted.
The fix shipped in the November preview update KB5127936, and admins waiting for it can use a registry edit or Group Policy workaround.

51ae4446acb76b50.title: Critical GitLab Remote Code Execution Flaw CVE-2026-97229 Exploited in Attacks
summary: A critical GitLab remote code execution flaw, CVE-2026-97229, is being exploited in real attacks after its patch was released, and the US CISA has added it to its KEV catalog.

Attackers can inject a crafted regular expression into CI/CD configuration, triggering an integer overflow in the Onigmo regex engine used by Ruby and running arbitrary code on the server without authentication.
Alpine Linux detected exploitation attempts from October 20 to 21 and rebuilt its GitLab server. Because logs were insufficient to rule out compromise, it reset passwords for all accounts.
According to Shadowserver, about 2,800 GitLab instances are exposed, while other reports say more than 1,000 servers are under attack.
Administrators should update immediately to fixed versions 19.4.2, 19.3.5, or 19.2.8 or later.

a3e3f363bf223183.title: Critical Langflow Flaws Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Run Code on Servers
summary: IBM disclosed four critical Langflow flaws in its AI agent builder that let a remote attacker with no account bypass authentication or run arbitrary code.
The authentication bypass (CVE-2026-93680) and code generation flaw (CVE-2026-110186) are both rated CVSS 9.8, and a public Metasploit module uses the bypass to list tools on an MCP endpoint.
All versions from 1.0.0 through 1.12.8 are affected and the only fix is 1.13.0. Users should upgrade and turn off automatic login, as the flaws are not yet in CISA's KEV catalog.

8d2bf204059a4f53.title: Supply Chain Attack Plants SSH Backdoor via Tampered Claude Code Extension on Cursor Marketplace
summary: Tampered versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 of the Claude Code extension were published on the Cursor marketplace for about 11 hours on October 29, 2026.
The injected JavaScript loader ran when the extension loaded, adding an attacker SSH key and attempting to set up a reverse SSH tunnel and re-execution persistence.
According to BleepingComputer, a bug in the SSH configuration code likely caused remote access to fail on most Windows and macOS systems.
SecurityWeek estimated that about 5,000 developer systems may have installed the extension, while Microsoft confirmed the official Visual Studio Marketplace and npm packages were not affected.
Cursor removed the malicious versions, released 2.1.314, suspended the marketplace, and blocked the attack server. Users are advised to remove the unauthorized SSH keys and rotate credentials.

6526ce57719f92ce.title: Attackers Impersonate IT Helpdesk on Microsoft Teams and Abuse AD CS Misconfigurations to Steal Corporate Data
summary: Attackers impersonated IT support staff on Microsoft Teams and convinced employees to open Quick Assist remote sessions, then executed malicious scripts.
Attackers abused misconfigured AD CS (Active Directory Certificate Services) certificate templates to obtain certificates for privileged accounts, including domain controllers.

According to Microsoft Threat Intelligence, one case used an ESC1-vulnerable template to obtain a certificate for DCSync, while another obtained a domain controller certificate via PetitPotam and an ESC8 relay.
In one case, a privileged account excluded from automatic containment was abused, and corporate data was exfiltrated to an external server.
Microsoft did not link the activity to a specific threat group and said the root cause was AD CS misconfiguration rather than a software vulnerability.

86c046e5d514797d.title: GMO Trust Login Misconfiguration Exposes Data of 45,030 Users from 2,492 Companies
summary: GMO GlobalSign disclosed a data breach affecting its GMO Trust Login identity management and single sign-on service, based on an external investigation.
A misconfiguration left files generated by batch processing and contract information files exposed in an external public storage area originally intended for distributing logos and other images.
Names and email addresses of 45,030 users at 2,492 companies may have been accessible for download from external sources between November 2017 and September 2026.

The issue was discovered through a vulnerability report from an external security researcher, and external access was blocked on September 15. Passwords and payment information were not included, and recurrence prevention measures are being implemented.

f72c3521cccd0fa3.title: CL-UNK-1211 Espionage Campaign Uses Suspected AI-Generated Scripts to Target Government Linux Servers
summary: Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 disclosed CL-UNK-1211, a cyber espionage campaign that targeted Linux servers of government agencies and state-linked organizations from October 2025 to April 2026.

Attackers planted web shells and custom backdoors on Linux servers, modified .bashrc to capture sudo passwords, and used the SysGoRAT remote access trojan to steal credentials and harvest government email.
Comments in the scripts suggest the malware may have been generated by AI or run automatically by an AI agent.
The attackers disabled security tools and cleared system logs to conceal their activity.
The number of victims has not been disclosed, and researchers warned that AI-assisted attacks are becoming faster.

86ca4a19e2c25110.title: Ivanti Connect Secure Zero-Day Chain Attack Enables Unauthenticated Root Access, Additional Patches Released
summary: Ivanti released patches for two zero-day flaws (CVE-2026-111357, CVE-2026-118527) used alongside an authentication bypass flaw (CVE-2026-104935) in Connect Secure.
Attackers chained the three vulnerabilities to gain unauthenticated root-level code execution, even on fully patched appliances, with the aim of credential theft and data exfiltration.
Volexity attributes the campaign to the unknown threat group UTA0576, which reportedly re-exploited devices with each command without malware and manipulated logs.
One report says more than 5,000 exposed devices exist without confirming how many are protected, while another tracks about 5,600 ICS hosts.
CISA added two flaws to its KEV catalog, fixed versions 25.1.1.3 and 22.8R2.6 are available, and federal agencies must apply them in November.

521d1cfccaf59b6f.title: CyberStrikeAI in the wild: the use of AI in real-world attacks on organizations
summary: Kaspersky confirmed a campaign targeting education organizations in Africa and Latin America that used C2 agents controlled by a large language model.

The open-source CyberStrikeAI framework let an LLM orchestrator on the C2 server plan and generate commands, which an implant ran on compromised hosts, progressing from reconnaissance to full domain compromise.
The report also describes artifacts such as self-signed certificates and implant headers that can help link samples to specific campaigns and attackers.

6a1962b7d624c382.title: PHP2Shell RCE Flaws Exploited in Attacks on Palo Alto Networks Firewalls
summary: Attackers linked to China exploited the PHP2Shell RCE flaws, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, together with the Linux kernel privilege escalation flaw Fragnesia (CVE-2026-46300).
The attackers targeted Palo Alto Networks management interfaces exposed to the internet, planted web shells and gained root privileges.
Dream Security reported at least 25 servers were compromised, including 3 linked to the US government, while The Record reported 24 firewalls were affected, so the full scope remains unconfirmed.
CISA added Fragnesia to its KEV catalog and required federal agencies to patch by October 31, and Palo Alto Networks has released a fix.
Vendor analysis indicates most public PoC code only crashes processes, making generic exploitation difficult, but Elastic says shell execution or file writes by web server processes can be detected.

a1fadc19d6d9a166.title: Multiple Vulnerabilities Found in pgAdmin 4 Database Management Tool - Two Rated Critical
summary: Multiple vulnerabilities were found in pgAdmin 4, a database management tool for PostgreSQL, and the developers released security update pgAdmin 4 9.19 on October 29, 2026 local time.

An OS command injection flaw in the data import and export feature stems from input validation issues and differences in how psql parses syntax, and CVE-2026-116241 is an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-17566.

The update fixes 15 CVE-listed vulnerabilities, two of which are rated Critical. Exploitation requires pgAdmin authentication and export privileges, and users are advised to update to the latest version.

8ae4c01d0949354c.title: Rakuten Securities: Up to 362 Customer Records May Have Leaked After Unauthorized Access at NTT Data Subcontractor
summary: Rakuten Securities said up to 362 customer records of buyers of its digital-benefit bonds may have been leaked.
The breach hit a bond-benefit system called STdirectServices, run by a subcontractor of NTT Data, after unauthorized access by a third party on October 30.

The affected data items were not disclosed, but Rakuten Securities said login credentials and trading information were not included. NTT Data suspended the service while its subcontractor investigates the intrusion route.

82dee5d1550f8760.title: WordPress 7.1.4 Fixes Remote Code Execution During Updates and Multiple XSS Flaws
summary: The WordPress development team released security update 7.1.4 on October 28, 2026 and urged users to update immediately.
The upgrade process contained a flaw that could allow remote code execution during updates, and several stored cross-site scripting (XSS) flaws were also found.
The XSS flaws can reportedly be exploited through crafted block markup or specially formed privacy data erasure requests. No CVE numbers were disclosed.

f0d554a4da9c7986.title: Digital Arts Cloud Operating Environment Breached Using Stolen Credentials
summary: Digital Arts disclosed on October 21 unauthorized access to its cloud service operating environment and internal network.
Attackers stole authentication credentials used for cloud operations and used them to infiltrate the operating environment.
The company discovered the intrusion during an October 9 inspection, and traces date back to July 2025, according to Security NEXT.
Customer information for six cloud services, including i-FILTER@Cloud, may have been viewed by unauthorized parties.
ScanNetSecurity reported no confirmed external leakage or secondary damage, and the company has asked all customers to change their passwords.

e7cadffb15b1f86d.title: WordPress Plugin Vulnerability Exploited to Breach TSS Link Website; No Product Security Issues Found
summary: TSS Link disclosed on October 21 unauthorized access to its website, which was operated by an external contractor.
Attackers exploited a vulnerability in a WordPress plugin used to manage the site between June 12 and October 13.

About 160 inquiry and trial application form entries and about 250 product support site credentials may have been leaked. The company reported no website defacement and no security issues in its products.

c23d4f8adebf6d4b.title: Employee Used Other Staff IDs and Passwords to Repeatedly Access Internal Shared Folders, Also Forged Supervisors' Seal Impressions
summary: A male clerk aged 26 in Yamamoto Town, Miyagi Prefecture, used other employees' IDs and passwords to repeatedly access internal shared folders after hours from June to July 2026, viewing and deleting data.

He also entered the office illegally at night and on holidays, used the town mayor's official seal without authorization to issue contracts to two contractors, and forged supervisors' seal impressions.
The town dismissed the employee on October 16 and issued reprimands to related staff for management supervision responsibility.

fe5eff34c22787fa.title: Unauthorized Access to Rakuten Travel Booking Sites Exposes Customer Data
summary: Rakuten Group said unauthorized access by a third party hit parts of the overseas hotel booking pages and the multilingual booking site of Rakuten Travel.
Suspicious activity was detected on September 10, but the attack path and methods were not specified in the reports.
Up to about 40,000 booking customers may be affected, with about 36,000 records including card last four digits, names, and expiry dates.
Up to about 2.6 million logged-in users had contact details such as names and email addresses exposed.
The multilingual site exposed account data for about 860,000 customers and 40,000 accommodation staff.

ca9ce0e61e10afeb.title: Unauthorized Access at Contractor Handling Fujicco Campaign Entry Forms
summary: Fujicco Co. announced on October 22, 2026 that unauthorized access to a server of a contractor handling its campaign entry reception may have leaked personal information from entry forms.
The possibly exposed data covers about 15,500 entries from non-member forms, including names, ages, phone numbers, and addresses.
The company is treating the data as taken by a third party, has suspended the relevant entry reception, and plans to notify affected customers and strengthen monitoring and security.

0ea3fdbada7239c1.title: Unauthorized Access to Swym Wishlist Plus App Used by SHIPS CYCLE MARKET Redirects Customers to Fake Site
summary: Free Standard said on October 22, 2026 that Swym Corporation, the developer of the external app Swym Wishlist Plus used for the favorites feature on its SHIPS CYCLE MARKET store, suffered unauthorized third-party access.

Attackers injected a malicious program into the developer's system, redirecting customers at some shops to a fake site that imitated the legitimate checkout page when they clicked the purchase button.

Customers who checked out during the window may have entered card numbers on the fake site, so they are urged to review their card statements, while the developer has suspended the app's features at all shops as a precaution.

a1d718ff259107be.title: Shinryo Corporation Hit by Cyberattack, Some Services Affected by System Failure
summary: Shinryo Corporation announced on October 21 that a system failure was caused by a cyberattack from a third party.
The failure also affected some of the company's services, and the attack method has not been disclosed.
No leak of personal or customer data has been confirmed so far, and the company is working with external specialists on recovery and impact assessment.

02834ae51c005cf9.title: Sally Reports Two Unauthorized Access Incidents Possibly Exposing Inquiry Data
summary: Sally reported on October 21 that inquiry data may have been exposed through two unauthorized access incidents.
The first incident occurred on October 14, 2026, when a third party misused an employee email account to log in to the inquiry management system, potentially exposing data of 544 people.

The second involved unauthorized access to the cloud environment of Studio, a service formerly used for website production, which may have exposed names, emails, and inquiry content of 404 people. The company is notifying affected individuals and securing accounts and systems.

04fcf0b691041b6e.title: PingCAP Breached via Stolen Credentials, Up to About 50,000 Personal Records Leaked in Japan
summary: PingCAP Inc. disclosed in October that a third party used stolen account credentials to access its internal systems from September 9 to October 7, 2026, and copied data.
The attacker used valid credentials to enter internal systems, and the company recognized the incident on October 7 and began revoking affected credentials.

Up to about 50,000 personal records were leaked in Japan, including TiDB Cloud account information, customer contact details, contract data, and the public key portion of API keys. The investigation with an external firm is ongoing.

058a5122866c4959.title: Unauthorized Access to Work-at-Home Job Site Mama Works; Data Believed to Be Member List Reported by Police
summary: Idoma Holdings said unauthorized third parties accessed its work-at-home job site Mama Works through a system configuration vulnerability, possibly leaking some member personal data.
After police reported that a file believed to be a member list was posted online, an external forensic firm confirmed unauthorized access caused by the configuration flaw.

Exposed data may include names, birth dates, genders, phone numbers, addresses, email addresses, work history, and password hashes. The vulnerability has been fixed, and the company is strengthening security and monitoring.

bf56c0be4ad10dcf.title: Cross-Border E-Commerce Service WorldShopping Hit by Unauthorized Access, Personal Data of 301 Overseas Customers Leaked
summary: Zigzag, operator of the cross-border e-commerce service WorldShopping, disclosed that a third party gained unauthorized access and leaked overseas customers' personal data.
The intrusion occurred from October 15 to 16 and was identified after suspicious external access was detected and investigated. The specific attack method has not been disclosed.

Names, email addresses, addresses, phone numbers and order information of 301 customers in Taiwan, Hong Kong, the United States, South Korea and China were exposed. The company blocked the access path, revoked and reissued the credentials, and is notifying affected customers.

408148f10c2dcd3b.title: National Cyber Office Launches Cyber Response Special Website With Consultation Desks and Agency Information and Social Media Accounts
summary: The National Cyber Office (NCO) launched a Cyber Response Special Website on October 30 that brings together consultation desks, announcements, and alerts from related agencies.
No attack methods or vulnerability details were reported, and the article only describes the structure of the site.
No damage or incidents were reported; the main point is a single hub for public and business users to find agency contacts and guidance.

7ca946e945adb293.title: OneNote File Extraction, (Sun, Nov 1st)
summary: Analysts often need to extract files embedded in many OneNote (.one) documents at once.
