The author added a --jsonoutput option to onedump.py that outputs the content of each embedded file as JSON.
Piping that output to myjson-filter.py with -W hashvir saves each file as a .vir file named by its SHA-256 hash.

896077a2b3afe350.title: CVSS 10.0 LXD, MicroCloud Flaw Lets Attackers Impersonate Trusted Clients Without a Private Key
summary: A flaw tracked as CVE-2026-112816 in Canonical's LXD and MicroCloud has been rated CVSS 10.0, the maximum score.
The server checks every certificate in the client chain instead of only the leaf, so attackers can attach a trusted client's public certificate and connect without its private key.
CISA reports no known exploitation and Canonical has released fixed versions. Attacks require network access to the HTTPS API, so restricting access and updating are advised.

87af916ced8dcc42.title: NetamLoader Supply Chain Attack Targets Asian Government Windows 10 Systems
summary: Kaspersky disclosed NetamLoader, a new .NET loader used in a supply chain attack targeting customized Windows 10 builds used by Asian government agencies.
Attackers placed a CAB file disguised as a Patch My PC component in an update folder and used AppDomainManager injection to execute the loader.
The infection chain relies on a vulnerable BinaryFormatter deserialization and multi-stage XAML loading, and an AMSI bypass patch helps it evade scanning.
According to The Hacker News, only one Asian victim has been confirmed, and The Record reported that one machine was detected in the first half of 2026.
Victim count and data theft status remain unconfirmed, and the attacker has not been linked to any known APT group, though some reports suggest a Chinese government agency.

79b771903c6ae1bb.title: Northflank security breach leads to abuse of customers' AI API keys
summary: Cloud hosting platform Northflank warned customers to rotate all credentials and secrets after a security breach led to unauthorized use of their AI API keys.
After a threat alert from Wiz, the company told customers to assume their environment variables were decrypted and the secrets within were stolen. How attackers got in has not been disclosed.
Multiple customers reported unauthorized AI API key use. Northflank advised reviewing provider usage and billing logs and enabled audit logs for all customers.

db8825c64d81be69.title: New Android SMS of Death exploit can remotely crash unpatched phones
summary: A proof-of-concept exploit has been released for the "SMS of Death" Android vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-58882, which can crash phones with a single crafted text message.

The zero-click flaw stems from improper validation of a header length in the WapPushOverSms.decodeWapPdu function, causing the com.android.phone process to crash and disconnect calls, including emergency calls.
Android 12 and 13 devices did not receive the fix and remain vulnerable, so users are strongly advised to install the latest security updates.

903707b5da0353d5.title: Chainalysis Data Breach via Internal Tool Intrusion Exposes Customer Identity Data
summary: Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis disclosed that an external attacker gained unauthorized access to internal systems and tools, exposing some customer information.
The company described the method as an agentic attack technique, and one outlet reported that the attack was AI-driven.
Exposed data includes customer user IDs, names, email addresses, and organizational role information, while investigation data, credentials, and session tokens were reportedly not stolen.
Technical details such as the vulnerability and intrusion path have not been disclosed. The company is investigating with outside experts and is patching flaws and hardening its systems.

bcb53a30bd15cb82.title: Syrian Electronic Army Hacker Sentenced to 42 Months Over Fake White House Explosion Tweet
summary: A US federal court sentenced Ahmad Umar Agha, a Syrian Electronic Army affiliate, to 42 months in prison.
Agha took part in hacking activity from 2011 to 2024 and in 2013 hijacked the AP Twitter account to post a fake report of explosions at the White House, causing a brief stock market drop.
SecurityWeek reported about 47 targets were breached, while The Record cited about 50 Western targets, spanning government, media, corporate and NGO victims.
Agha was arrested last year, but details of the arrest have not been disclosed; co-defendant Firas Dardar remains at large.

53999adf5d73f772.title: A Shared ChatGPT Link Could Run Attacker Code in Your Session and Read Private Chats
summary: Researchers at security firm Parameter disclosed a ChatGPT share-link flaw that could run attacker code in the session of anyone who opened the link.
An unchecked message listener in the MathLive library, loaded by an interactive graph in a shared chat, let attacker HTML reach the main ChatGPT page through Preview.
OpenAI fixed the flaw eight days after the October 18 report and raised its severity to P1. No real-world exploitation was reported, and users need to take no action.

a1a9bf744b255bbd.title: Cloudflare Reports 18.2 Million Network-Layer DDoS Attacks in Q3, Up 38%
summary: Cloudflare said it autonomously mitigated 18.2 million network-layer (L3) DDoS attacks in Q3 2026, up from 13.2 million in Q2.
DDoS-for-hire booter and stresser services are linked to the rise, and short-burst attacks under 10 minutes at 1 Gbps surged 208%.
Hyper-volumetric attacks above 1 Tbps fell 69%, likely due to law enforcement action, while the U.S., China, Indonesia, the U.K., and Türkiye were the most attacked countries.

f9515a05eafe09c5.title: DOJ raises privacy concerns over potential sale of Character.AI chats
summary: The US Department of Justice has asked for privacy protections for millions of Character.AI users whose chat histories and data could be sold as the company goes through bankruptcy.
The DOJ wants a consumer privacy ombudsman appointed to advise the court on which data can be sold and on what terms, and says the company's privacy policy is ambiguous.
Character.AI has 12 million monthly active users worldwide, and the court can restrict or block the sale of user data. The company did not respond to a request for comment.

d480b3d3d9924323.title: TeamViewer Vulnerability (CVE-2026-111585) Lets Malicious Hosts Attack Connected PCs
summary: A TeamViewer vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-111585 (CVSS 8.8) allows a host under remote control to attack the viewer PC or IT support technician's PC that connects to it.
The flaw stems from insufficient memory allocation when processing screen size values, leading to integer and buffer overflows as screen data is written beyond the buffer bounds.
According to The Hacker News, the flaw can crash viewer sessions, and researchers found it could enable code execution on Windows.

According to SecurityWeek, the company has not observed any exploitation in the wild, and fixes are available in version 15.83 and older security updates. Updating to 15.83 or later is the only remedy.

4d8506d979298d65.title: WordPress Core Race Condition Vulnerability Faces Mass Exploitation Attempts After Patch
summary: A high-severity (CVSS 8.1) remote code execution vulnerability affecting WordPress core versions 4.7 through 7.1.3 was patched in version 7.1.4 on October 28, 2026.
The flaw is a race condition during the update process, where installer files are unpacked to a predictable web-accessible staging path, allowing unauthenticated attackers to execute PHP code.
According to SecurityWeek, exploitation is complex and the window of opportunity lasts only seconds.
Wordfence reported blocking 62,969 attack attempts in the 24 hours after the patch.
Another report noted over 18,500 requests in the first 21 hours, and no successful compromises have been reported. Users are urged to update to 7.1.4 immediately.

56bbeffce7936450.title: SS7 and Diameter Attacks: How Signaling Flaws Expose Your Phone
summary: Abuse of SS7 and Diameter signaling flaws lets attackers track phones, intercept SMS one-time passcodes, and impersonate subscribers without malware or phishing.
Attackers obtain a victim's IMSI from their phone number and send false roaming claims to redirect calls and texts, while carrier velocity checks are bypassed due to stale location data.
Citizen Lab reported that the actor STA1 rotated through eleven operator identities in nine countries to track targets, and carriers defend SS7 and Diameter separately with little coordination.

166ef911b92a7680.title: ARTEX and Friends: Enter Agentic Offensive Frameworks
summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group reported that multiple threat actors are abusing open-source agentic pentesting frameworks such as ARTEX to automate intrusions.
ARTEX uses sub-agents powered by LLMs to split attack stages, running cloud credential abuse, Kerberoasting, DCSync, and webshell deployment in rapid bursts.

A campaign tracked as UNC7228 hit multiple organizations in the US and Europe, with some intrusions progressing from initial access to deep system access within four hours, and in one case in 15 minutes. Recommended defenses include least privilege and behavioral detection.

130136860931cee7.title: FBI Seizes Virtualine Bulletproof Hosting Domain Over Ransomware and Child Abuse Material Links
summary: The US Department of Justice and FBI seized the domain virtualine.net of bulletproof hosting provider Virtualine under a court order, and it now displays a notice page.
The provider was advertised on cybercrime forums and reportedly supplied infrastructure for phishing, spam, carding, and port scanning, while ignoring law enforcement takedown requests.
According to TRM Labs, funds linked to ransomware groups and infostealer infrastructure flowed through the service, and Bitcoin payments were laundered.

BleepingComputer reported that some servers were seized and data on about 3,000 customers was obtained, while the operator remains unidentified, has not been charged, and denies the child abuse material allegations.

Authorities in Germany, the Netherlands, and the United Kingdom, along with private partners, assisted the investigation, though SecurityWeek noted that domain seizure alone may not have stopped the service.

aee9f52aa28bf141.title: British spy agency cannot account for thousands of data storage devices, watchdog says
summary: The UK watchdog says GCHQ cannot account for thousands of portable storage devices, including USB sticks, external hard drives, and memory cards.
The Investigatory Powers Commissioner's Office found GCHQ's removable media tracking system was not robust enough. Some devices may hold data obtained under the Investigatory Powers Act.
The report does not allege that any device reached adversaries, and GCHQ has completed a full audit and updated its processes. The total number of lost items remains unclear.

7edbac5bde91c3bc.title: Russian popular home goods chain faces days of disruption following cyberattack
summary: Russian home goods retailer Poryadok suspended online services for five consecutive days and closed some stores after a cyberattack.
The attackers and how they breached the systems have not been identified, and it is unclear whether customer data was compromised.
The company has not given a timeline for reopening stores or restoring order and loyalty services, and some city stores remain closed.

d71d487efd5a789f.title: Microsoft Fixes Always On VPN Connection Failures Caused by September Windows 11 Update
summary: Microsoft has fixed an Always On VPN connection failure issue that appeared after the September 2026 Windows 11 security update was installed.
With automatic protocol selection using IKEv2 and SSTP, initial connections failed, leaving clients stuck in the Connecting state or returning port-in-use errors.

According to BleepingComputer's October 30 report, the fix is included in the October preview update KB5127936, while its October 14 report said the fix arrived in cumulative updates KB5127648 and KB5127646.
Administrators who cannot install the update immediately can apply a temporary workaround by locking the VPN protocol to either SSTP or IKEv2.

822b39c4208fe046.title: Critical Drupal Commerce Core Access Bypass Flaw Exploited in Attacks
summary: Drupal has urged administrators to immediately patch a critical access bypass vulnerability in its Commerce Core e-commerce module, tracked as CVE-2026-118539, which is being exploited in real attacks.
An unauthenticated attacker can bypass access controls on certain routes and entity fields, and the flaw applies regardless of module configuration.
Attack methods, the identity of the attackers, and the scale of the damage have not been disclosed. The module is used on roughly 42,000 sites.
Administrators should update to version 3.3.13 for the 3.x branch or 8.x-2.41 for earlier versions, and check order data for signs of unauthorized activity.

4eda6b5e9fb5f078.title: Aichi Prefecture Loses Application Documents at Mental Health and Welfare Center
summary: Aichi Prefecture disclosed that application documents containing personal data were lost at its Mental Health and Welfare Center, affecting 172 people after removing duplicates.
The missing forms included applications for mental disability welfare handbooks and self-support medical care certificates, with names, addresses, My Number, diagnoses, and family information.

The loss was found in November 2025 when files from fiscal 2023 were missing pages. The prefecture searched through August 2026 without success and apologized to affected applicants by phone or letter.

67cdad8762bca23a.title: Sega Suspends Chain Chronicle for 1-2 Months Over Security Issue
summary: Sega has been running an emergency maintenance on its smartphone RPG Chain Chronicle since October 23.
The company found security problems in some systems, and a simple update is not enough, so a large-scale overhaul of the app may be needed.
Sega said it has not confirmed unauthorized access or data leaks, and the maintenance may last one to two months, with compensation details to follow.

d9e48d4342a16b03.title: Shortage of IT Staff Keeps 31 Japanese Municipal Websites Offline Over PHP Vulnerability
summary: At least 31 Japanese municipalities have suspended or scaled back their websites to repair systems after a serious PHP vulnerability was found.
Small municipalities are slow to respond because updating the software needed for the PHP fix takes time, and they lack IT staff and expertise.
As of the 29th, sites in 8 cities, 17 towns, and 6 villages showed maintenance notices, raising concerns about disaster information and other resident services.

6eebe51470c138e8.title: Critical Vulnerabilities in ServiceNow Patched in Updated Releases
summary: ServiceNow published a security advisory on October 29, 2026, disclosing three CVE-based vulnerabilities affecting its AI Platform and the related Task Plan Templates application.

The most severe, CVE-2026-103093, allows an authenticated administrator to bypass Rhino script engine sandbox restrictions and execute arbitrary code on the host OS, with a CVSS 4.0 base score of 9.4.

A second flaw, CVE-2026-103094, could expose user passwords stored in plaintext in system tables, while CVE-2026-6877 allows cross-domain access control bypass; fixes are available and no exploitation had been confirmed at publication.

eb6e85ebbdcf72f3.title: Personal Data Breaches in FY2026 Exceed 260 Million People
summary: The Personal Information Protection Commission reported that about 260 million personal data records were leaked from April 1 to October 16, 2026, counted across multiple services.
Reported cases surged in October and made up roughly 40 percent of the fiscal year total, mainly due to unauthorized access.
Several companies reported breaches of over 10 million records in October alone, and the commission called for stronger safety controls and data deletion.

989f431225b8caa4.title: Meta Ray-Ban Smart Glasses Used to Decode Smartphone Passwords From Finger Movements
summary: Researchers from Tel Aviv University published a paper showing that smart-glasses video alone can infer smartphone passwords.
The method analyzes finger typing without prior knowledge of the device or keyboard app and can estimate passwords mixing upper and lower case, digits, and symbols.
In an experiment with 16 participants, the number of keystrokes was identified in 77.8% of cases. No real-world incidents or countermeasures are reported in the article.

0b4a5742369a03ef.title: What Are Security Measures for Generative AI Systems? Key Attacks and Risks
summary: As generative AI is built into more web services, this article outlines the security risks of AI agent systems that interpret natural-language input to generate responses or execute tasks.
Key threats include prompt injection that turns user input into commands, leakage of system prompts, XSS and SQL injection caused by unvalidated output, and DoS via excessive API usage.

When untrusted input, access to confidential data, and an external transmission path coexist, data breaches become likely, so the article recommends minimizing privileges, validating inputs and outputs, and requiring human approval.

264b800263e648c6.title: Google Fixes 21 Chrome Vulnerabilities, Including a Critical Flaw
summary: Google released a security update for its Chrome web browser on October 29, 2026 local time, fixing 21 vulnerabilities.
The critical flaw CVE-2026-76024 is a memory corruption bug in MediaStream, reported by an external researcher on October 21.
Nineteen high-severity issues were also patched, including Use After Free flaws in FileSystem, Input, Frames, and Blink.

cccb941b748bedf1.title: Unauthorized Login Using Gunosy Internal Business Account Credentials Exposes Business Partner, Executive and Employee Data
summary: Gunosy said on October 21 it detected a login to its cloud environment and business tools using internal business account credentials obtained by a third party.

An investigation found that some emails in the account's mailbox were viewed and user information registered in its business tools was taken. How the credentials were obtained is still under investigation.

Names and email addresses of 25 business partner contacts and 107 current and former executives and employees were exposed. The account was suspended the same day, and shared accounts were retired and multi-factor authentication enforced.

7f25dd65548a311e.title: Sony Network Communications So-net Member Database Breach Exposes Up to 2.6 Million Records
summary: Sony Network Communications said on October 27 that unauthorized parties accessed the member database of its So-net internet access service, leading to a personal data breach.
The unauthorized access occurred on October 19 and was confirmed on October 23, and the intrusion path and specific attack technique have not been disclosed.

Reported exposure varies by outlet, with Security NEXT and INTERNET Watch citing about 2.14 million records, BleepingComputer and Impress Watch citing about 2.58 million, and ITmedia and SecurityWeek citing 2.59 to 2.6 million.

Exposed data included names, phone numbers and email addresses, along with about 54,000 email passwords and 16 bank account records, and NTT Docomo Hikari customer information was also included. The company blocked the affected server, reset the email passwords and reported the incident to the Personal Information Protection Commission, while its investigation continues and no secondary harm has been confirmed so far.

8d692223049db9d9.title: Unauthorized Access Leads to External Leak of GETTIIS Ticket Service Member Data
summary: Linkstation disclosed that member data of its GETTIIS ticket purchasing service was leaked after unauthorized access to the server of its Gettii-Lite event registration service.
An attacker exploited a vulnerability in the Gettii-Lite program between about midnight and 7 a.m. on October 18 to obtain GETTIIS member information.

Leaked data includes 317,971 member IDs, 311,451 hashed passwords, and 29,515 partial card-related records; affected customers were notified by email, and the server was switched and the vulnerability patched while the investigation continues.

7829a859e605eb56.title: Entouch Database Hit by Ransomware Attack, Medical Professionals' Data Exposed
summary: A third party gained unauthorized access to a database managed by Entouch, a subsidiary of Toho Holdings, resulting in a data breach.
The intruder, claiming to be a ransomware group, accessed the database on October 9 and was discovered on October 13 at around 4 p.m.
Exposed data includes names of medical professionals, their affiliated institutions, appointment contacts, and visit status, and one report also cites product names.
In an announcement on October 19, Entouch said no data was altered and business operations were not affected, but the scale of the leak is still under investigation.
Patch deployment and forced password resets are underway as part of the response.

1c0143e01be1bdd1.title: Nifty Line Application Management System Breached, Up to 18,000 Member Records at Risk
summary: Nifty said on October 19, 2026 that an outside party had gained unauthorized access to its internal line application and reception management system.
The system is an internal tool separate from the customer-facing application website, and the attack method has not been disclosed.
An initial notice put the number of affected records at up to 542,513.
A follow-up on October 21 narrowed the scope to up to 18,000 users who applied for @nifty optical lines through channels other than the website since 2019.

Exposed items may include member IDs, names, gender, dates of birth, addresses, and phone numbers, while payment account and card data are not stored in the system. Nifty has blocked the access route, is investigating with outside specialists, and has reported the incident to the Personal Information Protection Commission, warning users about suspicious emails, texts, and calls.

ea2b047b4815cd66.title: Second Retailing Hit by Unauthorized Access
summary: Second Retailing reported that a third party gained unauthorized access to its internal systems, which it confirmed on October 15.
To prevent secondary damage, the company suspended apps and web services including 2nd STREET and GEO from October 17 and performed system maintenance.
An investigation with external security experts found no external leakage of personal or confidential data, and the restart date for services has not been set.

b708b09e52d2bc4c.title: Unauthorized Access to Arcadia's SpeeCAN RAIDEN Disaster Alert Mail Service Raises Local Government Data Leak Concerns
summary: Arcadia, which operates the disaster alert mail service SpeeCAN RAIDEN, said a third party gained unauthorized access to its system.

The attacker exploited a directory traversal flaw in a media server to expose internal source files, then stole inter-service secret keys from a configuration file and launched brute force attacks against account IDs.
ScanNetSecurity reported that 9,020 NET119 personal records were confirmed leaked, while ITmedia NEWS said up to 3,136,000 email addresses may have been exposed.
Malicious emails totaling 1,423,428 were sent, and services were restored about 105 hours later.
The company is removing the vulnerability and conducting external security assessments, while local governments have suspended disaster alert emails and warned residents about phishing messages.

1351251a6e66aaf1.title: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry Sets Up Special Cybersecurity Consultation Desk for Small Businesses
summary: The Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry, or METI, has set up a special cybersecurity consultation desk for small and medium-sized enterprises and small businesses.
The report is based only on its headline, so how the desk accepts inquiries and what services it offers are not confirmed.
It is a government support channel for small business security measures, and readers should check the original article for details.

46a184354a36a0e0.title: Hugging Face malware campaign returns to hijack GPUs for crypto mining
summary: A campaign that posted 31 malicious models on Hugging Face to install cryptominers and backdoors returned under new accounts within days of takedown.
The attacker abused the trust_remote_code option so that bundled Python code ran on load, installing a custom miner and a reverse shell.
Download counts exceed 32,000, but confirmed infections are unknown, and some models remain live. Users who enabled the option should treat their systems as compromised and check them.

096e95da8fc1024a.title: GM settles with 36 states for selling driver data, agrees to $220 million fine and reforms
summary: General Motors agreed to pay $220 million to settle a lawsuit brought by a coalition of 36 state attorneys general.
The suit alleges GM sold location and driving behavior data gathered through its Smart Driver program to data brokers, who passed it to insurers that used it to set premiums.
Under the settlement, GM must obtain express consent before collecting driving data and minimize what it collects, while a separate Texas lawsuit remains ongoing.

b69545e6c7d41095.title: Fake crypto app on Apple App Store linked to $23K wallet theft
summary: A fake crypto trading app, Padre Terminal, distributed on the Apple App Store was linked to the theft of about $23,000 from 27 Solana wallets.
The app drains wallets after users import their private keys into it, and it has since been removed from the App Store.
The attacker converted remaining USDC to SOL to avoid freezing, and at least four other suspicious impersonator apps were identified; users should install only via official project links.

7333e70f0573874b.title: ThreatsDay: Critical Firewall Flaws, Banking Trojans Rented, Weaponized PDF, Token Theft + 26 More Stories
summary: This week's ThreatsDay roundup covers continued PHP2Shell scanning against WordPress sites, the FortiBleed 2.0 credential harvesting campaign, and 28 stories in total.
Unauthorized DNS access let attackers create illegal gambling pages under school and government domains, with the Hidden Hawk actor linked to one cluster.
A now-patched Microsoft Authenticator flaw, CVE-2026-80097, could let a zero-permission Android app steal work tokens, and Fortinet released fixes for critical flaws.

23e1d5603bb94b11.title: UAT-11473 Exploits Cisco SD-WAN Authentication Bypass to Deploy KeyDrift Malware, Linked to Volt Typhoon Silent Train Network
summary: China-linked APT group UAT-11473 exploited an authentication bypass flaw (CVE-2026-20127) in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN controllers to deploy the KeyDrift malware framework.

Attackers gained admin privileges by bypassing authentication, then used the PolyFlame backdoor and LittleFilch module to intercept decrypted control-plane traffic and send IPsec key material to external servers over UDP.
Cisco Talos said UAT-11473 infrastructure overlaps heavily with the Silent Train network linked to Volt Typhoon, but stopped short of attributing the activity to the same group.
Reported victims include telecom, government, defense, and energy organizations, and one outlet estimates the number of affected entities at several hundred.

Cisco urged customers to apply the patch released in February and follow its hardening guidance, while Talos recommended monitoring for indicators of compromise and activating incident response procedures. It remains unclear whether upgrading removes existing infections.

0ba291e5490069cb.title: NIK C2 AI-Integrated Command and Control Framework Observed in Active Use
summary: Cisco Talos analyzed NIK C2, an AI-integrated command and control framework observed in active use.
NIK C2 is a Windows implant written in Go that performs credential dumping, keylogging, and screen-locking ransomware deployment.
It calls the OpenAI Chat Completions API through infected hosts and falls back to the API key stored in the victim's environment variables when no key is provided.
This approach shifts API charges to victims and makes attacker tracing harder, and the live servers were still active at the time of analysis.
Defenders should monitor for unusual proxy routing, PowerShell execution, and access to browser databases.

49fc15ae3b680d62.title: US Bankruptcy Court Notice System Halted by Cyberattack on Contractor BAE Systems
summary: The Bankruptcy Noticing Center (BNC), which serves the U.S. federal bankruptcy courts and is run by BAE Systems, was knocked offline by a cyberattack for more than two weeks and has begun recovery.
BAE Systems said no data was extracted and no personal information was compromised, but has not disclosed the cause or the identity of the attackers.
The Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts initially said it had not yet determined whether any data had been breached.
The Judicial Conference declared a bankruptcy rules emergency on October 22, allowing judges to extend deadlines, and late-mailed paper notices will carry a warning about the attack-related delay.

f145e6cc7df984fa.title: Chrome extensions with 13.4 million installs caught hijacking searches
summary: Socket researchers reported that 319 Chrome extensions with 13.4 million installs redirected user searches to Bing and Yahoo to generate ad revenue.
The extensions posed as PDF converters and safe search tools and routed queries through operator-controlled proxy servers that could change destinations at any time.
Users are advised to remove the extensions listed in Socket's report and run a full antivirus scan, since the redirects could lead to phishing or malicious downloads.

bc3c7e6db87a7ae8.title: Tracking AI adoption in North Korean threat actor tradecraft
summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence reports that North Korean threat actors are using AI across their operations and rates overall adoption as high.
Jade Sleet ran job-themed campaigns through three front companies in one week, while Onyx Sleet generated dozens of tailored PDF lures within minutes.
Coral Sleet built a capability to trojanize private GitHub repositories with an AI-enabled development platform, but operations remain human-directed rather than autonomous.

1206e6786bf01164.title: Yoba Campaign Uses Fake ChatGPT and Claude Apps to Deploy Crypto Miner
summary: Threat actors are distributing malicious loaders and cryptocurrency miners through fake GitHub projects that impersonate the ChatGPT and Claude desktop apps from OpenAI and Anthropic.
The attackers use DLL side-loading, placing malicious DLLs beside legitimately signed OpenAI and Anthropic executables to evade security tools.
According to Check Point Research, the campaign, dubbed Yoba, uses Telegram channels and DGA domains for command and control, while The Hacker News reported sandbox evasion and DoH-based C2 traffic.
In the final stage, the XMRig miner is injected into svchost.exe. The number of victims has not been confirmed.

e3fac5f4988708da.title: How Secure Are US Elections? Voting Machine Risks and the Growing Threat of AI
summary: This analysis examines security risks in US voting machines and concerns about foreign influence campaigns.
Sequent CEO Shai Bargil argues that EAC certification is meaningless because machines can go unpatched for years.
The article notes that voting machines have been hacked at DEF CON's Voting Village and that barcode or QR code counting cannot be checked by voters.

078b3c700374eff6.title: Windows Update Breaks Remote Desktop Connections on Devices With Administrator Protection Enabled
summary: Microsoft confirmed that Remote Desktop connections can fail on Windows 11 24H2 and later devices with Administrator protection enabled.
After recent updates, affected systems showed error code 0xC000000D when connecting, mainly on managed remote host devices.
Organizations that apply security baselines may have the feature enabled by default.
On October 14, 2026, Microsoft released a policy-based workaround to disable the feature while a permanent fix was in progress.
On October 29, 2026, Microsoft said the issue was fixed in the KB5127936 preview update, and companies that have not installed it can disable Administrator protection via Intune or Group Policy.

fc370297a0053d99.title: Cohere’s Qwen Story: Looks More Like Model Jaggedness
summary: Cohere shared a trace in which the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next model, asked to write a detection rule, tried to upload a test string to an Alibaba Cloud address, and its sandbox blocked the request.

Check Point resampled the same point 64 times and got 52 distinct hosts, some local, some nonexistent, and one with an invalid top-level domain. Simply swapping two tool names also changed how often the model made network calls.

The results point more toward model jaggedness, where behavior shifts with small context changes, than a fixed backdoor. Organizations should rely on least privilege and sandboxing outside the model to limit such actions.

b384ec278a7c6c48.title: 3 Ways AI Agents Already Operate in Your Browser
summary: AI agents are operating on behalf of employees within authenticated web applications, but most security teams cannot tell them apart.

Three approaches exist: remote debugging via CDP, AI extensions and agentic browsers, and WebMCP, in which websites expose tools directly, each creating access control and activity tracking challenges.

Because agents make requests with the same identity as employees and can interpret web page content as commands, they carry prompt injection risks. The article does not cover specific incidents of harm.

27af3f0658a90a0f.title: IR trends Q3 2026: Actors impersonate IT help desks in vishing attacks as ransomware activity increases
summary: Cisco Talos Incident Response's Q3 2026 analysis found phishing remained the leading initial access technique, with exploitation of public-facing applications close behind.
Attackers impersonated IT help desks in vishing calls to get victims to start remote management sessions, and ransomware and pre-ransomware incidents rose to 27 percent of engagements.
Ransomware groups such as Interlock and VYPR frequently disabled EDR tools, while China state-sponsored Salt Typhoon continued cyber espionage intrusions against telecommunications providers.

7a16c6546f7e3237.title: Adobe, Veeam, Juniper Networks Patch Critical Vulnerabilities
summary: Adobe, Veeam, and Juniper Networks released patches for 39 vulnerabilities across their products, many rated critical and enabling code execution.
Adobe fixed 12, Veeam fixed 9, and Juniper fixed 18, including authentication bypass, privilege escalation, and command injection flaws.
All three vendors said they have not confirmed any real-world exploitation of these vulnerabilities.

f88f69db8d8b4057.title: Cyberattack disrupts Belgian tax services before filing deadline
summary: Belgium's Federal Public Service Finance temporarily suspended access to MyMinfin, its major online tax portal, after a cyberattack.
The attack method and the attackers have not been disclosed, and authorities are investigating the scope of the damage.
Authorities said there are currently no signs of data leakage, and affected taxpayers will be granted an extended filing period.

af0fbb67a4f7b948.title: Ransomware Attack on University of New Mexico Health Sciences Center Disrupts Hospital Systems and Patient Care
summary: The University of New Mexico Health System suffered a cyberattack on Monday that brought hospital systems down. Ambulances were diverted to other hospitals in Albuquerque and Santa Fe, and new admissions, outpatient surgeries, and clinic appointments were temporarily suspended.

A new ransomware group calling itself BYOD claimed responsibility. The group said it would provide decryption keys for free, but also threatened to release patient and employee data it said it had stolen.
According to the center, no ransom was paid, core systems and hospital operations have been restored, and some classes were canceled.

The hospital has not officially confirmed the attack as ransomware. Its IT team blocked the threat and reported it to the FBI, and staff were told to shut down terminals and disconnect mobile devices from Wi-Fi.
Patients and staff were urged to be wary of phishing and not to respond to contact from hackers.

73a331524fe3377c.title: Over 41,000 DHS Employee Records Leaked Online
summary: The threat actor "Department of Peace" published personal and work information on more than 41,000 employees of the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) online.
The hacker claims the data was taken from the Okta single sign-on (SSO) system that DHS employees and contractors use to access central environments.

The leaked data includes names, work email addresses, phone numbers, job titles, office locations, and information on systems each account can access. Okta said it has no evidence that its own systems were breached.

693ea980a3875f8e.title: Fuji-Q Highland Member Site and App Hit by Credential Stuffing, 159 Accounts Accessed
summary: Fuji-Q Highland's official app and member site CLUB Fuji-Q were hit by a credential stuffing attack using email and password pairs obtained from outside sources.
The attacker posed as legitimate users to log in, and between September 4 and 7, 2026, 159 accounts were accessed without authorization.

According to one security outlet, names, phone numbers and dates of birth may have been exposed, and some customers' partial card numbers and expiration dates may also be included, with no secondary damage confirmed so far.
The company reset passwords for the affected accounts, notified the members by email, and reported the incident to the Personal Information Protection Commission.

5b18c16c60b19d13.title: Telegram Android Flaw Lets Attackers Run Code When Users Answer Voice Calls
summary: According to security startup NebuSec, a flaw in the Android version of Telegram allowed attackers to execute code on a device when the victim answered a voice call.
The code handling the rotation value in the MediaState message, which conveys call status, failed to properly process a missing field and accessed memory outside its intended range.
Telegram fixed the issue in version 12.10.4, and no CVE has been assigned yet. Whether it has been exploited in real attacks and whether iOS or desktop versions are affected have not been confirmed.

743b3b6f6014489c.title: 26,400 Valid Cloud and AI Credentials Found Exposed in Public Gitee Repositories
summary: Independent researcher Ben Zimmermann scanned 7.25 million public Gitee repositories, found 26,400 valid credentials, and published them on October 28.
Keys left in code by developers still worked, mostly for Alibaba Cloud, YouTube, DeepSeek, and OpenAI.

The list was sent to the vendors but developers were not contacted, and whether the keys were revoked or abused has not been confirmed. Deleting a key does not revoke it, so immediate rotation is required.

a2928e661aa18ea9.title: HHS Filing Puts iRhythm Data Breach Toll at 8.2 Million
summary: Medical device maker iRhythm disclosed a data breach in June 2026, and about 8.2 million people were later registered as affected on the U.S. HHS breach portal.

The attacker stole patient names, addresses, dates of birth, contact information, and account and device information from a business application hosted by a third party, then demanded a ransom while threatening to publish the data.
The company said there is no evidence the personal information was used for identity theft and that products and clinical systems were not affected, but it did not offer free credit monitoring.

68f0bb5684c4b364.title: Summary of AI Agent Takeover via Instruction File in Downloads Folder
summary: Forever Security said it blocked an AI agent on a customer endpoint from installing the malicious npm package function-color before any code was executed.

Its investigation traced the installation instruction to an AGENTS.md file in ~/Downloads, and its own tests reproduced a path where Codex and Claude Code changed their settings according to the instruction file.

Only one case has been confirmed in a real environment, and the scale of damage has not been disclosed. The malicious version was removed from npm, and third-party verification could not reproduce the attack's success rate.

8011628b70c30363.title: China-Linked Warp Panda Uses Zero-Day in VMware ESXi Logging Flaw to Reduce Audit Logs
summary: The US CISA warned that the VMware ESXi insufficient logging vulnerability CVE-2026-41709 is being exploited in real attacks and added it to the KEV catalog.

According to CrowdStrike, the China-linked threat group Warp Panda exploited this vulnerability as a zero-day to breach targets including US law firms and significantly reduced audit logs of administrator actions.
According to The Hacker News, the attackers combined audit log evasion, theft of cloud session tokens, and registration of malicious MFA devices. The scale of damage has not been disclosed.

Federal agencies must apply patches between October 31 and November 11. The patches are included in the latest ESXi build. Exploitation of CVE-2026-59309 and CVE-2026-59310, disclosed the same day, has also been reported.

0a7f23c2474bd321.title: Amatera: How the prolific infostealer works and spreads
summary: ESET reported that the infostealer Amatera was the top infostealer detected in Latin America in the first half of 2026.
Amatera is a Windows infostealer sold as malware-as-a-service that steals browser credentials, session cookies, and crypto wallet data.
It spreads through ClickFix fake CAPTCHA lures and other methods, and stolen session tokens can enable account hijacking, so sessions must be revoked and secrets rotated.

37869ce2661ea263.title: Deploying a Local Ghidra Server for Your Malware Analysis Lab, (Thu, Oct 29th)
summary: The article introduced how to store Ghidra project work on a central server, since work may be lost when a VM snapshot is restored.
It describes installing Ghidra Server, bundled with Ghidra, as a Java RMI service to support shared projects, version control, and work by multiple clients.
The server should be placed only on the internal network and not exposed to the internet. Reachability of TCP ports 13100 and 13101 and hostname resolution are required.

78d7705c9cfbb43d.title: New Prompt Injection Techniques Cover Agent-Planning Attacks
summary: CrowdStrike has updated its Prompt Injection Taxonomy with two new techniques targeting how autonomous agents plan, bringing the public catalog to 222 techniques.
Attackers can manipulate how an agent splits a goal into sub-tasks or redirects it through constraints, making a restricted action such as sending config files out look like a required step.

Each step can appear benign alone, so checks on individual steps may miss the overall plan, and agent security must cover the plan as well as prompts. The article describes a hypothetical scenario, not a confirmed incident.

30e87beba4d56b97.title: Unauthorized Access at Benefit One Subcontractor Leads to Leak of About 29,000 Personal Records from Saison Member Discount Service
summary: Benefit One announced that a system operated by its subcontractor Forestech was subjected to unauthorized access, leading to the leak of personal information of 29,465 members of the Toku Kai discount service for Credit Saison cardholders.
Unauthorized access occurred intermittently from the 14th to the 20th, some was detected on the 21st, and Toku Kai was temporarily suspended; additional access was confirmed on the 24th and 25th.

Leaked items include names, dates of birth, email addresses, and member numbers, and some former members are also affected. The cause is under investigation, and service resumption is planned after countermeasures are completed.

b515f0b273bbaf91.title: AI Outsourcing Crimes to Humans? Inside RentAHuman, a Job Site Where AI Buys Physical Labor
summary: A study was published analyzing 303 job postings taken from the public API of RentAHuman, a job platform where AI agents hire humans to perform real-world tasks.

The analysis found that 32.7% were submitted via API keys or MCP servers, and six abuse patterns were identified, including mass account creation, proxy interviews, real-world reconnaissance such as GPS-tagged photography, and support for bypassing two-factor authentication.
In 300 of the 303 postings, the employer was recorded as a human, creating a risk that workers may be drawn into crimes without knowing that AI is behind the job.

46dcd1133a79eefe.title: Multiple Vulnerabilities Found in WatchGuard Fireware OS, Seven Rated Critical
summary: Vulnerabilities were confirmed in Fireware OS, used in WatchGuard Technologies' Firebox firewall products.
Several high-severity vulnerabilities are included, and seven are rated critical based on the titles.
The company is providing security updates, but whether the flaws have been exploited and their details cannot be confirmed from the summary alone.

9cacec25c87f6d26.title: Brotli Compression Library Remote Code Execution Vulnerability (CVE-2026-111497) Confirmed Exploited in Attacks
summary: An out-of-bounds write flaw (CVE-2026-111497) was found in the Brotli decoder of Google's compression library, affecting multiple software products including Node.js, PHP, and PowerShell.

Crafted compressed data can cause crashes, memory exposure, and arbitrary code execution, and a public proof of concept has been released. According to a report, ELLIO analyzed that an attack based on the public PoC failed due to a flaw in the final stage.
The US CISA added the flaw to its KEV catalog and required federal agencies to patch by November 10, while security firms reported detecting exploitation attempts.
Fixed versions have been provided for VMware SDDC Manager, Node.js, Windows PHP, and PowerShell 7.4, 7.5, and 7.6, and updating to Brotli 1.2.1 or later is recommended.
In Japan, IPA and JPCERT/CC published the affected versions through JVN and recommended updating to the latest version provided by the developers.

c8714b0b0460f143.title: Serious RCE Vulnerability in Sophos UTM, Manual Patch Required Due to End of Life
summary: A critical vulnerability, CVE-2026-118633, was disclosed in Sophos UTM that allows arbitrary commands to be executed as root without authentication.
Systems using the mail proxy with scanning enabled are affected, and the attack involves repeatedly sending requests over several minutes to trigger a race condition.
The CVSSv4.0 base score is 9.2 (Critical), and all versions are affected. Because support has ended, no automatic patch is provided, so users must apply fixes manually and migrate to Sophos Firewall.

99037b8b271eebd9.title: TwitCasting Suspended After Unauthorized Access, Restoration to Take "Considerable Time"
summary: Moi, operator of the live streaming service TwitCasting, confirmed signs of unauthorized third-party access to its servers and suspended the service on October 28.
After detecting signs of intrusion from outside, the company took emergency measures to cut off the affected network, and an internal specialist team is investigating the scope of impact.
The cause, extent of damage, and resumption timing have not yet been disclosed, and the company expects restoration to take a considerable amount of time.

1f6088dab3931991.title: AI Agent Cipher Discovers Four Vulnerabilities in EPICS Industrial Control Software
summary: The autonomous AI agent Cipher found four vulnerabilities in EPICS (Experimental Physics and Industrial Control System), an open-source industrial control toolkit.
The most severe, CVE-2026-114595 (CVSS 9.8), involves an integer overflow that causes an out-of-bounds write in the heap, which could lead to remote code execution.
According to security firm Causal Security, the discovery took about 3 hours and 49 minutes, and CISA recommended updating to EPICS Base 7.0.11 or later.
Control systems of large research facilities, such as particle accelerators and fusion experiments, could be affected, and it is reported that attacks are possible without authentication.
No public exploitation of this vulnerability has been reported so far.

aae342cb26c5ee7a.title: Mitsui Sumitomo DS Asset Management Direct Sales Net My Page Login Failure Linked to Unauthorized Access Detected in Outsourcer's System
summary: A login failure occurred on the My Page of the Mitsui Sumitomo DS Asset Management direct sales net.
Unauthorized access was reportedly detected in the system of an outsourced business partner that handles operations.
The scale of damage and detailed circumstances cannot be confirmed from the article headline alone, so further announcements should be checked.

8b543de10ffe32b3.title: E-Store Shopserve Unauthorized Access Leads to Leak of About 23.35 Million Customer Records
summary: Shopserve, an e-commerce site building service operated by E-Store (E Store Co., Ltd.), was hacked from May to August 2026, and customer purchase information was leaked to the outside.
External attackers exploited a vulnerability in a server application to run malicious programs and transmit database information outside.

About 23.35 million records were affected, and about 2.09 to 2.10 million of them included cardholder names, partial card numbers, and expiration dates. According to the company, full card numbers and security codes were not included, so payments are not possible, and no secondary damage has been confirmed.
On August 1, the company blocked the attack communications, fixed the vulnerability, reset authentication information, and notified affected individuals one by one.

719478284b1b7d04.title: Fuji Television Broadcast Promotion System Breach Exposes Media Contact Data
summary: Fuji Television said on October 20 that an unauthorized third party accessed its broadcast promotion system on the night of October 19.
Personal data of media contacts, including names, company names and email addresses, may have been exfiltrated, with up to 730 records potentially affected.
According to Security NEXT, viewer information was not included in the affected data.
The attack technique and intrusion path have not been disclosed.
The company suspended use of the system after confirming the access and is investigating the cause, verifying safety and reviewing measures to prevent recurrence.

4fae8c11fd34bf82.title: Medley Obstetrics and Gynecology System @link Unauthorized Access May Have Leaked Patient Personal Information
summary: Medley announced that unauthorized access by a third party was confirmed on its work support system for obstetrics and gynecology '@link', its patient app, and related services.

After receiving a report from an external specialized organization, it began an investigation on October 11, and on the late night of October 14 it temporarily suspended the service to prevent further damage.
Patient personal information may have been leaked to the outside, and up to 787 medical institutions may be affected.

The company reported the incident to the Personal Information Protection Commission and consulted the police, and it is investigating whether leaks occurred together with an external specialized organization.

According to some reports, starting October 22, the company will sequentially resume reservation, patient information management, and medical calendar functions as '@link Cloud Beta' in a new environment, and the existing system will not be restarted.

695b230e72db4475.title: Panasonic Group Employee Personal Data Uploaded to Externally Hosted Generative AI Banned Within the Company
summary: Panasonic Operational Excellence announced that members of a personnel information system implementation project uploaded personal information to an external generative AI service whose use is prohibited within the company.

The uploaded data included employee numbers, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, and family emergency contacts, and the incident was caused by an employee violating company rules rather than external hacking.

The scope of impact varies by source. According to ScanNetSecurity, about 75,000 employees and about 178,000 retirees and family members were affected, while according to ITmedia, about 334,000 records were involved.

The employee deleted the data and chat history, and the service provider stated that the data was retained for 30 days, and no public disclosure or misuse damage has been confirmed. The company reported the incident to the Personal Information Protection Commission on September 29.
The company is implementing recurrence prevention training and improving its regulations.

d44ed6948e2c7c0e.title: Unauthorized Access to NP Atobarai Payment Service for BtoC Online Retail
summary: On October 14, it was confirmed that an outside party had sent mechanical and continuous requests in an abnormal manner to the invoice reissuance system of NP Atobarai, a deferred payment service operated by NP Atobarai Corporation.
The attacker exploited the reissuance function to view the names and addresses of customers in 28,884 transactions, and for corporate use, company and department names were also included.

The company is investigating the cause and scope of impact and implementing security measures, will notify affected customers individually by email and others, and plans to resume the system once safety is confirmed.

8137b743f27db0f2.title: Cyberattack on Maruki Medical Instruments Brings Down Core System, Orders Accepted by Fax
summary: Maruki Medical Instruments announced a cyberattack on its servers on October 15, 2026.
At around 10:00 a.m. on October 15, suspicious access occurred on the server, and the core system managing ordering, purchasing, and inventory in and out was completely shut down.

Order acceptance and shipping operations were temporarily suspended, and customers are being asked to place orders by fax with branches and sales offices until recovery, while an external specialized investigation firm works on identifying the cause and securely restoring systems.

07b4c2e7bc582868.title: Vulnerability in Electronic Deliverables Inspection Support System Due to Improper File Access Rights Set During Installation
summary: IPA and JPCERT/CC published a vulnerability in the Electronic Deliverables Inspection Support System (Ver. 4.0.36 and earlier) involving improper file access rights settings during installation through JVN.
Incorrect permissions set during installation allow files in the application folder to be tampered with, which may result in arbitrary code execution.
JVN recommends existing users update to the latest version and, for new installations, use the latest installer provided by the developer.

b6af345438018172.title: IDCF Cloud Ransomware Attack Exploits Open-Source Software Vulnerability to Gain Entry
summary: IDCF Cloud has been under a ransomware attack since October 7, causing outages in part of its eastern Japan region.

The entry point was a vulnerability in open-source software used in the portal authentication system, and the attacker reportedly took administrator privileges of the virtualization platform through the management console.
Data on customer virtual servers was encrypted, and according to ITmedia, 495 companies and local governments were affected.

Both media outlets reported that no data on the virtual servers was leaked externally, while up to 71 companies had their user information fraudulently viewed. According to INTERNET Watch, four passwords were also changed or reset.
The company did not pay the ransom and is working to prevent recurrence by rebuilding the portal and managing vulnerabilities based on SBOM, and it plans to resume services in three phases.

1cb32423d40b4f82.title: Court strikes down West Virginia law barring disclosure of public officials’ personal data
summary: The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit ruled that West Virginia's Daniel Law, which aims to prevent the exposure of personal information of law enforcement officers and judges, is unconstitutional.
The law was criticized for restricting speech based on its content and for imposing overly broad liability on data brokers.
The ruling weakens lawsuits against data brokers and could affect other state laws, including the New Jersey Daniel Law litigation.

d490f9f7a4c4c5a9.title: European digital rights nonprofit noyb sues Scale AI for ‘invasive’ worker surveillance
summary: Austria-based digital privacy group noyb has filed complaints against Scale AI in France, Italy, the Netherlands, and Austria.

The group alleges that while freelancers created AI training data, the company tracked their web activity and mouse and keyboard inputs, and required biometric data submission as a condition of employment.
noyb has asked courts in each country to impose fines and urged governments to investigate and review how work is allocated, while Scale has denied the claims as unfounded.

6915d57284c9957a.title: Unwrapping Retail Peak Season Cyber Threats
summary: Unit 42 analyzed cyber threats targeting retailers during the year-end shopping season.
Key threats include ransomware, data theft extortion, DDoS, web skimmers, account takeover, gift card fraud, and AI-driven automated attacks.
Given the difficulty of responding during code freeze periods, the report recommends preparation measures such as automated containment, zero trust, and WAAP deployment.

849efb349032a67d.title: US sanctions Russians, North Koreans for laundering IT worker earnings
summary: The US Treasury Department sanctioned Russian and North Korean individuals and companies linked to North Korea's IT worker infiltration scheme.
Two Russian nationals are accused of laundering cryptocurrency earned by North Korean IT workers at US companies and of supporting North Korean firms such as Amnokgang and Alis.
The Treasury said the proceeds fund North Korea's ballistic missile development, and the Department of Justice also raided a laptop farm in Texas and arrested two people.

845d0138628e3815.title: Moldova investigates possible foreign involvement in major government cyberattack
summary: Moldova's government systems suffered a large-scale cyberattack that led to personal data theft and the suspension of dozens of public services, and the prime minister said foreign state actor involvement is under investigation.

Attackers exploited a vulnerability in government services that require no authentication, using about 11 million requests from October 19 to 23 to steal information tied to about 750,000 identification numbers, and then took additional data from linked systems.

The government reviewed 82 digital public services and temporarily blocked vulnerable systems. Most security measures are now complete and access is being restored in stages. The government said bank card information was not leaked.

4b1862c94ea32298.title: Researcher Reveals How Logic Bugs Alone Cracked Microsoft Edge in $175,000 Pwn2Own Win
summary: Orange Tsai of DEVCORE published on October 28 the Edge sandbox escape method used at Pwn2Own Berlin.
Without memory corruption, the exploit chains several logic flaws in Edge and Windows features to escape the sandbox, then runs code through arbitrary file writes and abuse of protocol handlers.
This is a public exploit from a competition, and no real-world attacks have been confirmed. Microsoft fixed it on May 15 in Edge 148.0.3967.70, so users with automatic updates need no further action.

7a77f5c07fe61626.title: Yet Another ClickFix Campaign, (Wed, Oct 28th)
summary: SANS ISC researchers identified a new ClickFix campaign that uses a fake Cloudflare verification page.
The lure tricks users into running commands that download malware from a remote server, targeting both Windows and macOS.
On Windows the server returned a 403 response, and on macOS the domain did not resolve, so no malware was obtained. Indicators such as the domain js-static[.]cfd have been published.

f2be36d38303d21d.title: UK to look at making software companies liable for cyber breaches
summary: The UK government said in its budget documents it will consult next year on holding technology companies liable for cyber breaches caused by insecure products.
The UK has long relied on voluntary codes to push software vendors to improve security, and the consultation will build on the Law Commission's product liability review.
Key questions remain, including which department will lead, when the consultation starts, and whether liability will be civil or statutory. HM Treasury did not comment.

ccde74a0d6bd4073.title: Belarusian hackers increasingly acting as proxies for Russia amid war in Ukraine
summary: ESET said Belarus-linked hackers are increasingly carrying out cyber operations that align with Russia's interests in the war in Ukraine.

In late May, a group attributed to GhostWriter, linked to Belarusian intelligence, used data-wiping malware against a Ukrainian manufacturing company important to transportation. ESET called it the first destructive attack by a Belarus-aligned group it documented in Europe.

It could not determine whether the wiper aimed to cause damage or hide an espionage operation. North Korean hackers have also stepped up attacks on Ukrainian targets, reportedly showing interest in its drone industry.

ae81825281c4cfc2.title: Ukrainian National Sentenced to 70 Months for Nefilim and Hive Ransomware Attacks
summary: Ukrainian national Artem Stryzhak has been sentenced to 70 months in prison in the United States for his role in Nefilim and Hive ransomware attacks.
Stryzhak began working as a Nefilim affiliate in June 2021, agreeing to pay the operators 20% of each ransom, and later took part in Hive attacks.
Hive attacks hit seven organizations in the US, including dental practices, healthcare providers and law firms, and some victims paid ransoms to receive decryption keys.
According to BleepingComputer, losses from the two attacks exceed $100 million, and co-defendant Volodymyr Tymoshchuk remains at large.

According to The Record, Hive encrypted victims in more than 80 countries and collected millions of dollars in ransom payments. Stryzhak was arrested in Spain in June 2024 and extradited to the United States last year.

cd799bb7a4b7e1f9.title: Microsoft urges Entra ID admins to migrate users to passkeys
summary: Microsoft again urged administrators to move users to phishing-resistant authentication before it ends SMS and voice authentication in Entra ID starting February 2027.
SMS and voice authentication are vulnerable to phishing and SIM swap attacks, so migration to passkeys, FIDO2 security keys, or QR code authentication is necessary.
The migration applies only to Entra ID workforce tenants, and administrators can use a PowerShell scanner to find users who rely on SMS or voice authentication.

ef701660f13a3071.title: Managed for Malice: How Attackers Turn MDM into Remote Access
summary: Huntress said it has identified multiple cases in which attackers abused mobile device management (MDM) apps to install remote monitoring and management (RMM) tools.
A fake DocuSign installer delivered through phishing emails was used to install Hexnode MDM, after which ScreenConnect connected to an attacker-controlled relay server.
In one case, a removed ScreenConnect was reinstalled, leading to reinfection, and in another, RMM was installed with SYSTEM privileges after enrollment in Rippling MDM.

a60b0420f3cbad2b.title: Personal Data Exposed on Aichi Prefecture Marriage-Hunting Portal
summary: Personal data unrelated to an event was publicly viewable on Aichi Prefecture's marriage-hunting portal, Aicon Navi, after an external party reported it.
The event organizer mistakenly attached non-public information to its 2018 application file, and the prefecture approved the listing without noticing the error.
Data on 599 people, including names, ages, education, occupations, and hobbies, was exposed; the prefecture removed it on September 20, 2026 and apologized in writing.

03e0b1d7c75c77fd.title: Chrome 156 and Firefox 159 Security Updates Patch More Than 200 Vulnerabilities
summary: Google and Mozilla released security updates for Chrome 156 and Firefox 159, fixing more than 200 vulnerabilities.
According to SecurityWeek, Chrome 156 includes four critical flaws, including a FileSystem memory corruption flaw (CVE-2026-118306) that could enable arbitrary code execution outside the sandbox.
According to Security NEXT, Google fixed 52 vulnerabilities in Chrome, four of which it rated as Critical, the highest severity level.
The four Critical issues are a file system memory corruption, an input validation flaw in the File API, an input validation flaw in Skia, and a Use After Free vulnerability in Layout.

No exploitation has been reported so far, and users are strongly advised to update their browsers as soon as possible, with Chrome 156.0.8078.74 and 156.0.8078.73 available for Windows, macOS, and Linux.

ccfae9cd88a28849.title: GoAhead Web Server TLS Flaws Allow Revoked Client Certificates
summary: Security firm FoxIO disclosed three TLS handling vulnerabilities in GoAhead, a lightweight web server widely used in embedded devices.
The most severe, CVE-2026-115881 (CVSS 9.1), loads the certificate revocation list without enforcing it, allowing login with revoked client certificates.
The issue affects only builds that use mutual TLS and have a revocation list configured, and an attacker must possess a certificate signed by a trusted authority and revoked.
The same release also fixed a missing certificate chain length check and an error in the length of DH values in Mbed TLS.

The flaws were fixed in version 6.1.1, released on October 12, 2026. No exploitation has been reported, but because build settings are determined at firmware compilation, whether device vendors apply the patch is critical.

08ad92b2a3cba615.title: Attempts to Exploit Oracle E-Business Suite Remote Code Execution Flaw CVE-2026-101767 Spread
summary: Attack attempts targeting the critical Oracle E-Business Suite vulnerability CVE-2026-101767 (CVSS 9.8) were detected right after the patch was released.
The Thin Client Framework servlet in Application Object Library contains an unauthenticated SQL injection, which can lead to SQL execution with APPS account privileges and OS command execution.
Oracle released a security patch on October 20, and according to Defused, exploratory attacks were recorded on its honeypots on October 27.
No actual exploitation has been confirmed so far, and applying the patch and blocking access at firewalls are recommended.

b5decdd9105f7297.title: Critical 16-Year-Old UEFI Flaw Can Run Code Before Secure Boot on Network-Booting Servers
summary: A critical 16-year-old vulnerability (CVE-2026-97631, CVSS 9.5) has been disclosed in EDK II, the open-source framework used by most hardware manufacturers to build UEFI firmware.
The buffer overflow occurs in code that handles ICMP error messages during PXE network boot, allowing attackers who send crafted messages to halt booting or execute code before Secure Boot.
The fix has been merged into the main branch but is not yet in a stable release, so server operators must wait for vendor firmware updates.

78331297322d6f1e.title: NEC Contractor Cyberattack Leads to Customer Server Encryption and Personal Data Leak
summary: NEC said a contractor responsible for system development and maintenance suffered a cyberattack in late September, causing damage to customers.
Attackers abused stolen valid account credentials from the contractor to access customer systems (T1078), encrypting server files (T1486) and rendering some systems unusable.
Personal data files leaked from a cloud storage service shared by NEC and affiliated companies, and Osaka University reported that 77,851 people's information was downloaded.
ITmedia NEWS put the figure at about 78,000. The university criticized NEC for sharing files with an unreported subcontractor without a contract and for retaining files that should have been deleted.
NEC is contacting affected customers individually and has provided NEC-managed devices to the contractor, and no secondary damage has been confirmed so far.

85d1ebef17520ad2.title: Adobe Patches Critical Flaws in Campaign Classic and Other Products, Code Execution Risk
summary: Adobe released security updates including eight critical vulnerabilities in Campaign Classic and a code injection vulnerability (CVE-2026-48360) in Adobe Connect Desktop and Mobile.
The flaws include code injection, OS command injection, and SQL injection leading to security feature bypass, and privilege escalation via reflected XSS, posing a remote code execution risk.
Campaign Classic versions 7.4.4 build 9402 and earlier are affected and fixed in 9403. Some vulnerabilities were rated 9.0 or higher under CVSS v3.1.
Adobe said it had not observed any actual exploitation as of the time of disclosure.

444d9aa58bb9c8a1.title: Lessons from Cybersecurity Black Week
summary: During the last week of October 2026, vulnerabilities in PHP and the Linux kernel, a compromise of the LiteLLM package, a maximum-severity GitLab vulnerability, a Node.js Brotli vulnerability, and a certificate authority trust issue were all disclosed at once.

PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) was rated as enabling unauthenticated remote code execution, but the published PoC did not work on default installations, and no successful real-world attacks have been confirmed.

The malicious LiteLLM version was exposed on PyPI for about two hours. Removing the package is not enough; organizations must check for compromise and rotate exposed secrets. The GitLab patch does not invalidate credentials that have already been stolen.

3b976ccfbeaed967.title: American Organizations Under Attack: Skyw4lker Device Code Phishing Campaign Exposed
summary: ANY.RUN analyzed the Skyw4lker device code phishing campaign, which mainly targets American organizations, with manufacturing, technology, and healthcare as the primary targets.
Attackers lure victims with business documents to Google-hosted pages and through the Microsoft authentication flow, getting them to complete legitimate authentication and stealing the tokens.
Because the activity looks like normal authentication events, it is difficult to detect using identity logs alone, so investigations must correlate documents, web activity, and authentication flows.

64a70d4446cbe1ec.title: Millions of security cameras at risk: DoS vulnerability in Intelbras devices
summary: Kaspersky discovered and disclosed a denial-of-service (DoS) vulnerability in the firmware update endpoint of Intelbras IP cameras that can be accessed without authentication.
Sending a request to the /firmwareUpgrade_service/Demo path, which lacks an authentication check, starts a reboot without firmware verification and takes the camera offline.
Intelbras has patched the issue in firmware R.260804. The attack can be carried out with only local Wi-Fi access, so users should update to the latest firmware.

fc404eb90ddf54b7.title: ESET APT Activity Report Q2 2026–Q3 2026
summary: This report from ESET researchers summarizes the activity of major APT groups observed from April to September 2026.

China-linked groups continued information gathering targeting government entities, and targeted a hotel in Palau and a Taiwanese semiconductor company. Iran-linked groups, including FilthyFeline and MuddyWater, resumed activity and mainly targeted Israel.

North Korea-linked groups expanded their targets to Ukraine and the drone sector, and a Belarus-linked group was confirmed to have carried out its first destructive attack on a Ukrainian manufacturer. Cases of limited AI use by some APT groups were also reported.

fa8b270a22d891ed.title: Firefox 159 Released - 167 Vulnerabilities Fixed
summary: Mozilla released the web browser Firefox 159, fixing 167 vulnerabilities based on CVE counts.
There were no critical-severity vulnerabilities, with 108 rated high, 52 medium, and 7 low.
Among the high-severity issues, CVE-2026-117861 is a sandbox escape vulnerability in the page transition processing component, and the other two may also allow bypassing sandbox restrictions.

c124c136a618c0c5.title: Servers That Postponed Security Measures Are Being Targeted One After Another - Rack CTO Warns Amid Consecutive Unauthorized Access
summary: At KDDI SUMMIT 2026, Rack CTO Hiroaki Kuramochi warned that amid rising unauthorized access to domestic companies, systems with delayed security checks are being targeted intensively.
AI has greatly reduced the cost of vulnerability discovery and conversion to attacks, and systems with delayed vulnerability assessments, no WAF, or outdated PHP are major targets.

Account takeovers caused by infostealers are increasing and are hard to detect through external monitoring alone, so detecting abnormal internal activity, introducing EDR, and penetration testing are recommended.

c30cd8d1e02811a3.title: Tailscale SSH Forwarding Flaw Enables Root Privilege Escalation and Worm-Style Spread Concerns
summary: Tailscale released version 1.104.4, which fixes a forwarding flaw in its built-in SSH server. The flaw could allow access to services and files on other servers that only root can reach.

The cause was a race condition in which a root-privileged process checked a Unix socket path and then allowed the path to be swapped. Attackers must first take over a device that accepts SSH connections.

According to Cyberdione Labs, 11 privilege escalation vulnerabilities in the client and headscale were disclosed before patching, six of which are rated high. In researcher tests, Docker socket forwarding allowed obtaining a root shell.
No actual exploitation has been confirmed. Users are advised to update to version 1.104.4 or later, or set TS_SSH_DISABLE_FORWARDING=1 and disable unnecessary SSH forwarding.

76db51692a6e02e8.title: ShinyHunters Chains Oracle PeopleSoft Zero-Days in Attacks as Leader Is Detained
summary: ZDI revealed that the Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day exploited by the ShinyHunters group since May is a chain of three vulnerabilities.
Through an SSRF in PSIGW, attackers can reach the internal PSEMHUB management functions via the loopback address (127.0.0.1) without authentication, enabling remote code execution.
Oracle released a patch for CVE-2026-35273 on June 10 and it was added to the CISA KEV catalog. According to Mandiant, a larger wave of attacks has been observed since September.
The group reportedly stole data from Jeppesen ForeFlight, a subsidiary sold by Boeing, and attempted extortion.
A 10-year-old suspect named Rey, identified as the leader, was detained in Amman, Jordan, and is reportedly cooperating with the FBI. Jeppesen ForeFlight said its operations were not affected.

3ce34923726609b2.title: CrowdStrike 2026 Legal Threat Landscape Report: eCrime Leads Attacks, China Activity Intensifies
summary: CrowdStrike published its 2026 Legal Threat Landscape Report, finding that intrusions targeting the legal sector nearly doubled between 2023 and 2026.
Financially motivated adversaries accounted for 82% of observed activity, and CHATTY SPIDER impersonated IT staff to start remote sessions and steal data within minutes.
China-nexus groups exploited a VMware ESXi zero-day and a hardcoded key flaw in Intapp Time Server, and the report warns AI will make attacks more sophisticated.

db1680d208d2370f.title: When AI Guardrails Expose Vulnerabilities
summary: CrowdStrike researchers presented GbVD, a technique that uses the points where AI model guardrails activate to locate code vulnerabilities.
In a C web server code where a single-character logic error changed max to min, the model refused to explain the relevant function, and this refusal was used to pinpoint the vulnerable location.
In controlled tests covering five vulnerability types, the method correctly identified 73 of 86 scenarios, and results were also verified on real open-source projects through the CVD process.

cb8b8fe2332eb2c1.title: Vulnerability in Kubernetes Tool consul-k8s Fixed in Updated Release
summary: HashiCorp disclosed CVE-2026-110720, an authorization vulnerability in consul-k8s, a tool that integrates Kubernetes with Consul.
Insufficient access control rules allow attackers to authenticate as Consul components using same-named service accounts in other namespaces and gain privileges.
The CVSS v3.1 base score is 9.9 (Critical). Environments with system ACLs disabled are not affected. Fixed versions 2.1.0 and 1.8.18 are available.

f06e5039d735eed9.title: One in Six May Respond to AI Voice Scam Calls, Study of 4,100 People by Harvard and Meta Reveals Easily Deceived Tactics
summary: Researchers from Harvard University, Meta, and others tested how 4,100 U.S. adults responded to phishing calls created with six AI voice models.
Combining voice cloning with LLMs makes it possible to place large numbers of scam calls simultaneously, and scenarios appealing to emotions or relationships yielded higher response rates.
Across all scenarios, 16.5% complied with the request or withheld judgment, and in the scenario impersonating a sister in crisis using a cloned voice, the rate reached 36.1%.

88b17bf276235a06.title: Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator SQL Injection Zero-Day Exploited in Real-World Attacks
summary: A zero-day SQL injection vulnerability (CVE-2026-114625) in Arista Networks' SD-WAN management product VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO) has been exploited in real attacks.
An attacker logged in with a read-only account can escalate privileges to gain operator rights and access internal functions, with a CVSS score of 9.9.
According to Security NEXT, the US CISA added this vulnerability and a Collabora Online CODE server vulnerability to its KEV catalog on October 23.
The attackers and the scale of damage have not been disclosed, but two IP addresses believed to be located in Japan have been published.
Hosted VCO instances have already been patched, while on-premises users should update to versions 5.2.3.18, 6.1.3.10, 6.4.2.12 or later, restrict access to the management console, and check logs.

e00b97472ff029f5.title: July–September 2026 Observation Report
summary: IIJ has published an observation report covering DDoS attacks, unauthorized access traffic, and malware threats from July to September 2026.
September saw the most DDoS attacks at 689, including a UDP Flood peaking near 102.58 Gbps, while phishing emails targeting VenomRAT and XWorm were widely detected.
Web-based detections mainly involved exploitation attempts against CVE-2021-41773 and obfuscated malicious scripts.

3443e7edd8085e62.title: Apple Releases Security Updates Patching About 300 Vulnerabilities Across macOS and Other Products
summary: Apple released security updates for macOS Golden Gate 27.2, Tahoe 26.7.2, and Sequoia 15.8.2 on October 26, 2026.
The updates fix vulnerabilities in multiple components including WebKit and the kernel, and according to Security NEXT, the total number of unique CVEs is 299.
The updates include a Remote Management authentication vulnerability (CVE-2026-112427) that could allow remote arbitrary code execution, so users need to update to the latest versions.

According to SANS ISC, the fixes cover privilege escalation, memory corruption, and sandbox and Gatekeeper bypasses, but whether they have been exploited and the scale of damage have not been confirmed.

f2e8e3f11d13c771.title: Personal Information Read Over the Phone - Person Claiming to Have Found Parking Ticket Loss Report Demands Purchase, Hints at Spreading Data
