The original report does not specify the types of vulnerabilities, attack methods, or scope of impact.
The recommended remedy is to update the affected modules to fixed versions, and readers are directed to developer notices for details.

ea143c380da53c9a.title: Remote Desktop Connections Suspected as Intrusion Route to Be Blocked; Hachioji Gakuen Ransomware Attack, Second Report
summary: Hachioji Gakuen Hachioji Junior and Senior High School issued a second report on the ransomware attack it announced in July.

The attacker bypassed the firewall by illegitimate means on April 26 and entered the internal network via remote desktop access. In the early morning of July 10, the attacker took over a server and encrypted files with ransomware.

No external leak of files containing personal information has been confirmed, but some logs were deleted, so a leak cannot be fully ruled out. The school plans to block remote desktop connections and rebuild its network.

76bfe9e217a1b671.title: Job Site Baitoru Unauthorized Access Leaks Up to 3.88 Million Member Email Addresses
summary: Unauthorized access by a third party was confirmed on Baitoru and Baitoru NEXT, job services operated by Deep Co., Ltd.
On October 6, 2026, overseas access aimed at a specification gap in some system functions was confirmed, and members' email addresses were leaked to the outside.
The maximum number of leaked records is 3,885,771. The operator blocked overseas access and completed technical countermeasures by modifying the program.
According to Security NEXT, the operator reported the incident to the Personal Information Protection Commission and others, consulted the police, and individually notified affected members.

421af8662fff33ef.title: Dai-ichi Life Group and Dai-ichi Life Insurance Possible Leak of About 120,000 Employee Records via Unauthorized Access to HR System
summary: Dai-ichi Life Group and Dai-ichi Life Insurance announced on October 2 that they had detected unauthorized access to their employee HR system on September 24.
Personal information of employees and retirees stored in the system may have been viewed by a third party and leaked to the outside.

Possibly affected are about 120,000 current and former employees, with data including employee numbers, names, addresses, phone numbers, genders, departments, and job titles, and about 70,000 of them are retirees.
The intrusion route and cause have not yet been identified, and no customer information breach had been confirmed as of the announcement.

c6c068b061e40686.title: Toyobo Textile Subsidiary Email Account Hijacked, About 1,500 Phishing Emails with PDF Attachments Sent
summary: Unauthorized third-party access to an employee email account at Toyobo Textile, a subsidiary of the Toyobo Group, led to about 1,500 suspicious emails being sent to internal and external contacts.
The emails contained PDF attachments. Opening them redirected recipients to an external site that asked them to enter credentials such as email addresses, IDs, and passwords.

After discovering the incident, the company immediately took steps to prevent further damage, including password changes and expiring authentication sessions. No intrusion into core systems has been confirmed to date.
Separately, other reports say two employees at Toyobo MC also fell victim to phishing, but whether personal information was leaked is still under investigation.

e783c57643eb7599.title: Ryomo Systems Hit by Ransomware Attack
summary: Ryomo Systems confirmed unauthorized access to its internal systems on August 14, cut off its network, and conducted an investigation with an external specialist organization.
The investigation found that on August 12, an external attacker abused a VPN account to infiltrate the internal network, and the incident was confirmed to be a ransomware attack.

Traces of unauthorized access were found on some servers, and business and transaction information as well as personal information may have been leaked. The company plans to identify affected individuals and contact them individually.

fac679f4d7872a6e.title: Unauthorized Access to Online Booking Platform Used by LEGOLAND Japan Hotel
summary: LEGOLAND Japan GK announced unauthorized access to the online booking platform used by the hotel's official reservation website.
The platform operator, Amadeus IT Group, S.A., reported that names, email addresses, and phone numbers contained in booking information were accessed without authorization.
A total of 1,557 bookings may have been affected. The company warned customers to be wary of phishing contacts impersonating booking information.

a2ce5028a5e2beaf.title: Unauthorized Access to Finds Reservation System Affects 1,536,322 Booking Records
summary: Finds Co., Ltd. announced on September 25 that unauthorized access had occurred on its reservation system.
While investigating an anomaly in the reservation system on September 22, the company confirmed access by a third party. The method and cause have not been disclosed.

Personal data of 1,536,322 customers, including names, phone numbers, email addresses, and booking store, menu, and date and time, may have been affected. The company is blocking access and identifying the scope of impact.

cb02f5ec8578f654.title: King Printers Hit by Unauthorized Access; Attackers Aimed to Misuse Generative AI Service Using Credentials
summary: King Printers detected unauthorized access by a third party to its managed system infrastructure on September 10 and temporarily suspended its site and related functions.
The company's investigation found no signs of data transmitted externally, and it believes the purpose was unauthorized use of a generative AI service using credentials it held.
As of September 25, no leak of customer personal information or other data has been confirmed. A forensic investigation by an external specialist organization is scheduled for early October.

9ed4c7706a4a9fbe.title: Early Detection Using Decoys: US CISA Publishes Guide on Adopting Cyber Decoys
summary: On September 16, the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) published a guide to strengthening detection and response capabilities using cyber decoys.

Based on the premise that attackers will eventually gain a certain level of access, it recommends placing decoys such as honeypots within internal networks to detect attackers at the early stages of intrusion.
The guide recommends using decoys alongside a zero trust model and explains their benefits for collecting attack information and reducing mean time to detect (MTTD).

521e09b07fbb6d2f.title: North Macedonian police arrest alleged administrator behind OLVX cybercrime market
summary: North Macedonian and FBI investigators arrested a man alleged to be the administrator of OLVX, a cybercrime marketplace.
OLVX operated from 2023 to 2025 and reportedly sold stolen personal data and login credentials through more than 1,500 seller accounts.
The FBI said the market endangered thousands of American users, and police said the suspect also ran the ONEMILI Telegram group selling refund fraud tools.

8c18424aacef66d6.title: Brooklyn DA’s office disrupts crypto scam targeting Russian community
summary: New York law enforcement seized or blocked 241 web domains and 112 servers used by a cryptocurrency investment fraud group targeting Russian-speaking residents of Brooklyn.
The group recruited investors through Russian-language Facebook ads, then stole funds through fake investment platforms and demanded additional fees and taxes when victims tried to withdraw.
Losses are estimated at several million dollars, and about 300,000 dollars has been recovered. The group also carried out secondary fraud by offering victims recovery services as bait.

d3ce606db866e0bc.title: US Crackdown on North Korean IT Worker Laptop Farms Leads to Two Arrests
summary: The US Department of Justice and FBI cracked down on laptop farms used in a North Korean IT worker scheme, arresting two US nationals and indicting 14 people.
North Korean IT workers obtained remote jobs at US companies using stolen or fabricated identities, while American facilitators received company-issued laptops and relayed access.
In Texas, agents searched 40 residences and seized about 187 laptops, and according to an Ohio indictment, the scheme generated about $3 million from more than 70 companies.
Other reports say over 40 laptop farms were shut down, and authorities warned that the tactics will continue to evolve.

b7113d69e64d6493.title: Passkeys Raise the Bar. Here’s Where Attackers Can Still Get In.
summary: Huntress analyzed phishing campaigns that use passkeys as bait and cases of abuse of device code authentication.
Attackers do not break passkey cryptography. Instead, they target registration and recovery procedures, alternative authentication flows, and social engineering to obtain legitimate sessions.
The report recommends combining strong identity verification, EDR-based endpoint protection, security awareness training, and ITDR monitoring after login.

b385a988803690e4.title: Spyware manufacturer had access to data harvested by former Polish government, current PM says
summary: Polish prosecutors said the Central Anti-Corruption Bureau (CBA) did not have full control over the Pegasus spyware system run by NSO Group.
The server module stayed under the manufacturer's exclusive control, and the CBA lacked passwords for many administrative accounts. Collected data was sent abroad through foreign IP addresses.

Prime Minister Donald Tusk called the affair one of Poland's biggest scandals and a crime against the state. Investigators say NSO had technical access but cannot confirm it obtained specific case material.

b328223c0ebf0e45.title: AI Agents Navigate Unfamiliar OT Systems and Move Equipment in Minutes, Booz Allen Finds
summary: Booz Allen has published the results of testing agents built on recent AI models in its own isolated OT lab.

The agents linked asset discovery, device analysis, and attack planning without source code or engineering documents. In some tests, actions inside the industrial control network followed an external intrusion within 16 minutes.

Existing defenses blocked or delayed some actions, but no single control stopped every test. No actual damage has been reported. The report recommends blocking intrusion paths into OT environments, removing implicit trust, and detecting changes to industrial settings.

866bb97e33930127.title: Microsoft VSS: Still Essential, But Not the Whole Story
summary: Huntress has published a technical column outlining the role and limits of Microsoft VSS.
VSS creates application-consistent snapshots but does not support volumes larger than 64TB, and it has limitations such as write performance overhead and dependence on Windows.
Ransomware deletes local shadow copies, so VSS alone is not enough and must be used with immutable off-host backups.

628ad213369ac609.title: ICS Patch Tuesday: Siemens Issues 17 Advisories, Rockwell Fixes ArmorBlock Takeover Flaw
summary: Siemens, Schneider Electric, and Rockwell Automation published industrial control system (ICS) security advisories on this Patch Tuesday, and Siemens issued 17 new advisories.

The GNU/Linux subsystem of Siemens Simatic S7-1500 CPUs has more than 400 flaws, and Ruggedcom Crossbow SAC and other products have high-severity vulnerabilities. Some have patches, while others only have interim mitigations.

A critical-rated flaw in the Rockwell 1732E ArmorBlock allows an unauthenticated attacker to change web server passwords and take over administrator accounts. In ABB dynovaPRO, 26 password change events were seen across nine customers, raising the possibility of testing or reconnaissance.

e18f95eb154f8da2.title: U.K. Sanctions Cryptomus for RU Money Laundering
summary: The U.K. government imposed economic sanctions on the cryptocurrency platform Cryptomus, including Heleket, for processing payments that benefited the Russian government and financial institutions.

Analysis indicates that payments for ransomware, drugs, dark markets, and cybercrime services passed through the platform. Chainalysis and TRM Labs pointed to illicit fund flows and high transaction volumes.

Assets in the U.K. will be frozen and U.K. companies will be prohibited from transacting with it. Canada imposed a 176 million Canadian dollar penalty for money laundering violations, but it has not been enforced.

b57b6083b436664d.title: Shosen Mitsui Cruises Loses Storage Media Used for Data Migration, Investigating Contents
summary: Shosen Mitsui Cruises announced that it lost external storage media containing business information.
The loss was confirmed in July 2026 when some media could not be found during an inspection of storage locations aboard a ship. The media had been used for ship data migration work.

Because customer and crew personal information may be included, the company has reported the loss to the police and the Personal Information Protection Commission, and is investigating about 200,000 backup files.

0bb5531bb32ed156.title: Russian travel booking platform suspends reservations after cyberattack
summary: Russian online travel agency Anywayanyday suspended new bookings after a cyberattack on its IT infrastructure.
The attackers and the intrusion path have not been disclosed, and the company said it is strengthening security measures.
The company said it found no evidence of personal data leakage, and existing confirmed bookings remain valid. No timeline for restoring service has been announced.

e571036eeeb6274b.title: Congressional probe faults Match Group for failing to rein in dating app scams
summary: A congressional investigation found that Match Group's dating platforms, including Tinder and Hinge, matched users with about 1.5 million scammers and bad actors in the first nine months of 2025.
Investigators said Tinder's scam profiles were shown far more often, and that its AI detection models had not been updated for years, which the company disputes.
Match Group said it launched the Face Check video verification tool, but lawmakers say more progress is needed as AI makes fake profiles easier to create.

1e3c84569356c5d0.title: curl Patches HTTP/2 Upload Flaw After PoC Demonstrates Client-Side Code Execution
summary: A use-after-free flaw in curl's HTTP/2 upload handling (CVE-2026-92392) was fixed in curl 8.23.0.

A proof-of-concept was published showing that a malicious server can stop transmission mid-upload and reset the stream, causing the remaining data to be interpreted as a new request, which could enable code execution.
No real-world attacks have been reported, and curl rated the likelihood of success as low and classified the flaw as High. Users of versions 8.12.0 through 8.22.0 should upgrade or disable HTTP/2.

124f9acbc531ec11.title: Researchers Used a Public OpenAI Model to Build a $250,000 Chrome Full-Chain Exploit in Six Days
summary: The XBOW team chained three unknown Chrome vulnerabilities to create an attack chain that executes code on Windows just by having a user open a web page.
An AI agent using the GPT-5.6 Sol model handled source code exploration and PoC writing, while humans selected targets and verified results.
Google patched the three vulnerabilities and paid a $250,000 bounty, and XBOW said there was no exploitation of real users. Users should restart and update to Chrome 152.0.7977.82 or later.
